    .theme-toggle {

    /* Dark theme: screen only, printing always uses the light theme */

  <script>
    (function () {
      var KEY = 'notes-theme';
      var root = document.documentElement;
      var saved = null;
      try { saved = localStorage.getItem(KEY); } catch (e) {}
      var prefersDark = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
      root.setAttribute('data-theme', saved || (prefersDark ? 'dark' : 'light'));

      function label(btn) {
        btn.textContent = root.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark' ? '\u2600\uFE0F Light' : '\uD83C\uDF19 Dark';
      }

      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
        var btn = document.createElement('button');
        btn.type = 'button';
        btn.className = 'theme-toggle';
        btn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Toggle dark mode');
        label(btn);
        btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
          var next = root.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
          root.setAttribute('data-theme', next);
          try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, next); } catch (e) {}
          label(btn);
        });
        document.body.appendChild(btn);
      });
    })();
  </script>

<h1 id="ai-driven-mernmean-prep-plan-sanket-raut">AI-Driven MERN/MEAN
Prep Plan — Sanket Raut</h1>
<h2 id="overview">Overview</h2>
<p>In 4 weeks of 5 study days each (Mon–Fri, weekends off), at 4 hours a
day (80 hours), this plan takes you from a strong Node.js/React engineer
to an interview-ready, AI-driven Senior/Principal MERN/MEAN engineer who
can own system design, DB design and agentic AI features. Every hands-on
block is done with Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, so the AI workflow
becomes habit, not a separate topic.</p>
<p><strong>Target role:</strong> Senior / Lead / Principal Full-Stack
Engineer (Node.js + React/Angular) with GenAI and system design
ownership. At 8+ years, interviewers will spend less time on syntax and
more on design trade-offs, scaling, debugging stories and
leadership.</p>
<p><strong>Your starting point:</strong> deep in Node.js (8 yrs), solid
in React (4 yrs), new to Angular (6 months), Claude-certified. So the
plan goes deeper on Node internals and system design, refreshes React,
and builds real Angular depth.</p>

<h2 id="week-1-jsts-node.js-internals-api-design">Week 1 — JS/TS,
Node.js internals, API design</h2>
<p>Goal: you already know Node.js and JavaScript well, so this week is
revision for interviews, not learning from scratch. Each day pairs fast
concept revision with the questions interviewers actually ask and a
timed coding task. TypeScript and API design still get full depth.</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 20%" />
<col style="width: 20%" />
<col style="width: 20%" />
<col style="width: 20%" />
<col style="width: 20%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Day</th>
<th>Topic</th>
<th>Revise fast</th>
<th>Interview questions to nail</th>
<th>Coding / build</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1 (Mon)</td>
<td>JS core — interview revision</td>
<td>Closures, <code>this</code> binding rules, prototypes, event loop
(micro vs macro tasks), promise chaining, async error handling,
ES2023+</td>
<td>Output puzzles mixing <code>setTimeout</code>, promises and
<code>process.nextTick</code>; “explain closures with a real bug you
fixed”</td>
<td>Write polyfills from scratch: <code>Promise.all</code>,
<code>Promise.allSettled</code>, <code>debounce</code>,
<code>throttle</code>, <code>bind</code>, deep clone,
<code>curry</code>. Set up the capstone repo and
<code>CLAUDE.md</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2 (Tue)</td>
<td>TypeScript (full depth)</td>
<td>Generics, utility types, conditional and mapped types,
<code>infer</code>, discriminated unions, type guards,
<code>strict</code> mode, decorators</td>
<td>“type vs interface”, “unknown vs any vs never”, implement
<code>DeepPartial&lt;T&gt;</code></td>
<td>Shared <code>types</code> package for backend and both frontends;
typed <code>EventEmitter</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3 (Wed)</td>
<td>Node internals — interview revision</td>
<td>Event loop phases, <code>nextTick</code> vs
<code>setImmediate</code> vs <code>setTimeout(0)</code>, libuv thread
pool, streams and backpressure, <code>cluster</code> vs
<code>worker_threads</code> vs <code>child_process</code>, heap
snapshots</td>
<td>“Is Node single-threaded?”, “How does Node handle 10k concurrent
connections?”, “What blocks the event loop?”, “Find a memory leak in
production”</td>
<td>Stream a 2 GB file with backpressure; move CPU hashing to worker
threads; take and read a heap snapshot</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4 (Thu)</td>
<td>Node architecture, security + machine coding</td>
<td>Middleware order, central error handling, graceful shutdown, Express
vs NestJS vs Fastify, scaling (cluster, PM2, horizontal), JWT and
refresh tokens, OWASP API Top 10</td>
<td>“Design error handling for a large Express app”, “Scale a Node API
to 50k RPS”, “JWT vs sessions”, “Your API security checklist”</td>
<td>2 h: auth service with JWT refresh rotation, RBAC guard, rate
limiter. 2 h timed, no AI: LRU cache, token-bucket rate limiter, async
task queue with concurrency limit</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5 (Fri)</td>
<td>REST, GraphQL, Swagger + testing</td>
<td>Resource naming, versioning, cursor pagination, idempotency keys;
GraphQL N+1 and DataLoader; OpenAPI 3; Jest/Supertest, test pyramid; Git
rebase vs merge</td>
<td>“Design the API for an order system”, “REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC”,
“How do you solve N+1?”</td>
<td>REST with cursor pagination and idempotent POST; GraphQL with
DataLoader; Swagger docs; Claude Code writes tests, you review each;
lint/test CI</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>AI habit this week:</strong> use Claude Code for scaffolding
and tests, Copilot for inline completion, and review every diff as if a
junior wrote it. Note where the AI was wrong — those notes make great
interview stories.</p>

design, React, Angular</h2>
<p>Goal: design data models you can defend under questioning, and put
two production-grade frontends (React and Angular) on the same API.</p>

decisions</label></li>

custom Skill showing your AI workflow</label></li>

</ul>
<p>If time runs short, cut the Analytics service first and keep the AI

<h3 id="interview-question-bank-practise-out-loud">Interview question
bank (practise out loud)</h3>
<p><strong>Node.js (must-answer for 8+ years):</strong></p>
<ol type="1">
<li>Walk through the event loop phases and predict the order of
<code>nextTick</code>, promises, <code>setImmediate</code> and
<code>setTimeout</code>.</li>
<li>Is Node single-threaded? What runs in the libuv thread pool and how
do you size it?</li>
<li>How do streams and backpressure work? <code>pipe</code> vs
<code>pipeline</code>?</li>
<li><code>cluster</code> vs <code>worker_threads</code> vs
<code>child_process</code> — when to use each?</li>
<li>How do you find and fix a memory leak in production?</li>
<li>What blocks the event loop, and how do you measure event-loop
lag?</li>
<li>Error handling: operational vs programmer errors,
<code>unhandledRejection</code>, <code>uncaughtException</code>.</li>
<li>How do you shut down gracefully on SIGTERM in Kubernetes?</li>
<li>CommonJS vs ES modules; how does <code>require</code> caching
work?</li>
<li>How does Express middleware run, and how does <code>next(err)</code>
reach the error handler?</li>
<li>How do you scale a Node API horizontally, and what must be
stateless?</li>
<li>JWT vs sessions; refresh-token rotation; where should tokens be
stored?</li>
<li>Your checklist for securing a Node API.</li>
<li>How do you profile and speed up a slow endpoint?</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>React (must-answer):</strong></p>
<ol type="1">
<li>How do the virtual DOM and reconciliation work, and why do keys
matter?</li>
<li>What triggers a re-render? Render phase vs commit phase.</li>
<li>What is a stale closure in hooks and how do you fix it?</li>
<li>useEffect pitfalls: dependencies, cleanup, double run in
StrictMode.</li>
<li>When do useMemo, useCallback and React.memo hurt more than
help?</li>
<li>useEffect vs useLayoutEffect; uses of useRef beyond DOM access.</li>
<li>Controlled vs uncontrolled components.</li>
<li>How do you choose between local state, Context, Redux Toolkit,
Zustand and TanStack Query?</li>
<li>Concurrent rendering: useTransition, useDeferredValue,
Suspense.</li>
<li>Server Components vs client components; SSR vs SSG vs ISR.</li>
<li>What can error boundaries not catch?</li>
<li>How would you fix a slow page with a large list?</li>
<li>Which custom hooks have you written and why?</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Angular:</strong> How does OnPush change detection work, and
what do signals change? switchMap vs mergeMap vs concatMap vs
exhaustMap? How do you avoid RxJS subscription leaks?</p>
<p><strong>Databases:</strong> Embed or reference for orders and line
items? Explain isolation levels with an anomaly for each. How do you
pick a shard key? How do you migrate a 500 GB table with zero
downtime?</p>
<p><strong>Microservices &amp; messaging:</strong> How do you keep data
consistent across services? Saga vs 2PC? How do you handle a poison
message? How do you guarantee ordering in Kafka?</p>
<p><strong>DevOps:</strong> Readiness vs liveness probes? How do you
roll back a bad deploy? Blue-green vs canary?</p>
<p><strong>GenAI &amp; agents:</strong> RAG vs fine-tuning? How do you
evaluate an LLM feature? How do you defend against prompt injection? How
do you control cost and latency of LLM calls? When should a workflow be
an agent vs a fixed pipeline?</p>
<p><strong>Behavioral:</strong> Tell me about a design decision you’d
reverse. A time you disagreed with your manager. How you mentor juniors.
How you used AI to deliver faster — and where it failed you.</p>

resource team — a visible AI-focused capstone often speeds up project
allocation.</p>

<h1 id="capstone-project-plan-ecommerce-ai">Capstone Project Plan —
ecommerce-ai</h1>
<p>A build plan for the capstone that runs alongside the 20-day study
plan: what to build each day, how you’ll know it’s done, and what to cut
if time runs short. Each day’s build work fits the “Build” block of your
daily routine (about 1½–2 hours).</p>
<h2 id="overview-and-scope">Overview and scope</h2>
<p><strong>ecommerce-ai</strong> is an online store with a React
storefront, an Angular admin portal, Node.js services that communicate
through events, and two AI features: a product Q&amp;A assistant (RAG)
and an order-support agent that can take actions safely. It exists to
prove, in one repo you can demo, every skill you’ll claim in
interviews.</p>
<p><strong>User journeys the finished system supports:</strong></p>
<ol type="1">
<li>A customer signs up, browses and searches products, reads reviews,
adds to cart and checks out.</li>
<li>Payment succeeds: stock is reserved, the order is confirmed, a
confirmation email is sent, analytics update.</li>
<li>Payment fails: stock is released and the order is cancelled
automatically (saga compensation).</li>
<li>The customer asks the assistant product questions and gets answers
with citations.</li>
<li>The customer asks the support agent to cancel an order; the agent
checks eligibility and the customer confirms in the UI.</li>
<li>An admin manages products and orders in the Angular portal and sees
sales metrics.</li>
</ol>

<p>Every event uses the envelope from Day 12 (eventId, type, version,
occurredAt, traceparent, data) and a Zod schema in
<code>packages/types</code>.</p>
<h3 id="checkout-saga-orchestrated-by-order-service">Checkout saga
(orchestrated by order-service)</h3>
<p><code>PENDING</code> → reserve stock (gRPC) →
<code>STOCK_RESERVED</code> → charge payment (event) → <code>PAID</code>
→ <code>CONFIRMED</code>. On <code>stock.rejected</code>:
<code>CANCELLED</code>. On <code>payment.failed</code>: release stock →
<code>CANCELLED</code>. Timeout after 10 minutes in any intermediate
state: compensate and cancel. Every step idempotent; every message
through the outbox.</p>
<h2 id="repo-structure-conventions-local-setup">Repo structure,
conventions, local setup</h2>
<pre class="text"><code>ecommerce-ai/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ storefront/            # React + Vite + TanStack Query
│  └─ admin/                 # Angular (zoneless, signals, SignalStore)
├─ services/
│  ├─ api-gateway/
│  ├─ auth-service/
│  ├─ product-service/
│  ├─ order-service/
│  ├─ payment-service/
│  ├─ inventory-service/
│  ├─ notification-service/
│  ├─ analytics-service/     # Could
│  ├─ ai-assistant/
│  └─ orders-mcp-server/
├─ packages/
│  ├─ types/                 # Zod schemas, DTOs, event envelopes (shared)
│  ├─ utils/                 # polyfills, retry, limiter, LRU (Day 1, Day 4)
│  ├─ service-kit/           # logger, request context, error middleware, health, metrics, tracing
│  ├─ api-client/            # generated from OpenAPI (Day 5)
│  ├─ prompts/               # versioned prompt templates (Day 17)
│  └─ proto/                 # gRPC definitions (Day 11)
├─ deploy/
│  ├─ compose.yaml           # local stack (Day 13)
│  ├─ charts/node-service/   # shared Helm chart (Day 14)
│  └─ env/                   # values per environment
├─ docs/
│  ├─ adr/                   # architecture decision records
│  └─ architecture.md        # diagrams, event catalogue
├─ evals/                    # RAG and agent eval sets + runner
├─ .github/workflows/
├─ CLAUDE.md
├─ turbo.json
└─ pnpm-workspace.yaml</code></pre>
<h3 id="conventions">Conventions</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>TypeScript strict</strong> everywhere with the extra flags
from Day 2; shared base <code>tsconfig</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Every service uses
<code>packages/service-kit</code></strong>: same logging, error format,
health endpoints, metrics, tracing, graceful shutdown. Build it once on
Day 4 and reuse.</li>
<li><strong>Feature-module layout</strong> inside services (Day 4):
controller → service → repository.</li>
<li><strong>Validation at every boundary</strong> with Zod schemas from
<code>packages/types</code> (HTTP bodies, events, env vars, LLM
outputs).</li>
<li><strong>Conventional commits</strong>, small PRs to
<code>main</code>, CI must be green.</li>
<li><strong>One ADR per significant decision</strong> in
<code>docs/adr</code> (aim for 5–6 by the end).</li>
<li><strong>AI workflow:</strong> <code>CLAUDE.md</code> at the root,
custom commands for repeated tasks (new service, new endpoint, write
tests), review every diff.</li>
</ul>

and Swagger, all tested in CI.</p>

<h3 id="day-11-mon-checkout-saga">Day 11 (Mon) — Checkout saga</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" /><code>payment-service</code> with a
fake gateway (configurable success rate and latency) and its own
Postgres schema</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Outbox table + relay
(<code>FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED</code> inside a transaction) in
order-service and payment-service</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Orchestrated saga in order-service:
<code>PENDING → STOCK_RESERVED → PAID → CONFIRMED</code>, compensations,
10-minute timeout job</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />gRPC between order-service and
inventory-service with deadlines</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Idempotent consumers with
<code>processed_events</code>; circuit breaker (opossum) around the
payment call</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation
in every service via service-kit</label></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Done when:</strong> in Jaeger, one checkout trace spans
gateway → order → inventory → payment → order, and a forced payment
failure ends with stock released and the order cancelled.</p>

</ul>
<p><strong>Done when:</strong> publishing a malformed event lands it in

<h2 id="definition-of-done-testing-demo-time-savers">Definition of done,
testing, demo, time savers</h2>
<h3 id="definition-of-done-per-feature">Definition of done (per
feature)</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Acceptance criteria met and checked
by hand once</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Input validated with shared Zod
schemas; errors return the standard error format</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Unit tests for business rules;
integration test for the endpoint or consumer
(Testcontainers)</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Logs with request/trace IDs; metrics
where useful</label></li>

main as a small PR</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Docs or ADR updated if a decision
was made</label></li>
</ul>

<h3 id="time-savers">Time savers</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Use Claude Code for scaffolding, tests, Dockerfiles, Helm
values and boilerplate;</strong> write the specs, review plans, and own
the saga, agent safety and auth logic yourself. Keep a running list of
corrections for your interview story.</li>
<li><strong>Generate, don’t hand-write:</strong> API clients from
OpenAPI, types from Zod, seed data with a script.</li>
<li><strong>One service template:</strong> build
<code>service-kit</code> and the Dockerfile/Helm chart once (Days 3, 13,
14), then every service is mostly business logic.</li>
<li><strong>Cut early, not late:</strong> if a day overruns by more than
an hour, move its “Could” items to the backlog immediately.</li>
<li><strong>Fake what isn’t the point:</strong> payments, email, and
cloud resources can be faked or local; the interesting engineering is in
the flows between them.</li>
<li><strong>Commit daily</strong> with a short note in the README
changelog; it doubles as evidence of steady progress.</li>
</ul>

<h1 id="week-1-study-notes-jsts-node.js-internals-api-design">Week 1
Study Notes — JS/TS, Node.js internals, API design</h1>
<p>For each concept: what it is, how it behaves in a real Node or React
codebase, where it breaks in production, my rule of thumb, and how I’d
answer it in the room.</p>
<h1 id="day-1-mon-javascript-core-interview-revision">Day 1 (Mon) —
JavaScript core, interview revision</h1>
<h2 id="hour-1-scope-hoisting-closures">Hour 1 — Scope, hoisting,
closures</h2>
<p>At 8 years nobody expects you to define a closure from a textbook.
They want to hear that you understand the runtime well enough to debug
it: why a variable is <code>undefined</code>, why memory keeps growing,
why a React handler reads old state. Keep that lens while revising.</p>
<h3 id="execution-context">1.1 Execution context</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> every time JS runs code it builds an
execution context: the variables in reach, the scope chain, and
<code>this</code>. The global script gets one; every function call
pushes a new one onto the call stack and pops it on return.</p>
<p><strong>How it works:</strong> each context is set up in two
passes.</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><strong>Creation:</strong> memory is reserved. <code>var</code> gets
<code>undefined</code>, function declarations are stored whole,
<code>let</code>/<code>const</code>/<code>class</code> are registered
but not initialised.</li>
<li><strong>Execution:</strong> code runs top to bottom and assigns
values.</li>
</ol>
<p>Once you see the two passes, hoisting stops being magic. It is just
the creation pass.</p>
<p><strong>In production:</strong> the call stack is what you read in
every error trace. “Maximum call stack size exceeded” is almost always
unbounded recursion, often a recursive tree walk on unexpected data or
two modules calling each other.</p>
<h3 id="scope-and-the-scope-chain">1.2 Scope and the scope chain</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> scope decides where a name is visible.
JS uses lexical scope: visibility is fixed by where the code is written,
not by who calls it.</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Scope</th>
<th>Created by</th>
<th>Holds</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Global</td>
<td>The script</td>
<td>Top-level declarations (avoid in Node; use modules)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Module</td>
<td>Each ES module / CommonJS file</td>
<td>Top-level declarations, private unless exported</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Function</td>
<td>Every function</td>
<td><code>var</code>, <code>let</code>, <code>const</code>, inner
functions</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Block</td>
<td><code>{}</code> in if / for / try</td>
<td><code>let</code>, <code>const</code>, <code>class</code> only, never
<code>var</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Lookup walks outward: current scope, parent, up to global. Not found
means <code>ReferenceError</code>.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb4"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb4-1"><a href="#cb4-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> service <span class="op">=</span> <span class="st">&#39;orders&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-2"><a href="#cb4-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">handler</span>() {</span>
<span id="cb4-3"><a href="#cb4-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> requestId <span class="op">=</span> <span class="st">&#39;r-42&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-4"><a href="#cb4-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">log</span>(msg) {</span>
<span id="cb4-5"><a href="#cb4-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(service<span class="op">,</span> requestId<span class="op">,</span> msg)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// both resolved through the scope chain</span></span>
<span id="cb4-6"><a href="#cb4-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb4-7"><a href="#cb4-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;start&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb4-8"><a href="#cb4-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>My rule:</strong> keep scopes small. A variable that lives at
module level in a Node server is shared by every request. A classic
production bug is user data leaking between requests because someone
cached <code>currentUser</code> in a module-level variable.
Request-scoped data belongs in the request (or
<code>AsyncLocalStorage</code>), never in module scope.</p>
<h3 id="hoisting-and-the-tdz">1.3 Hoisting and the TDZ</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> declarations are processed in the
creation pass, so they exist before the line that declares them
runs.</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Declaration</th>
<th>Before its line runs</th>
<th>Re-declare</th>
<th>Re-assign</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>var</code></td>
<td><code>undefined</code></td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Yes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>let</code></td>
<td>Throws (TDZ)</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Yes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>const</code></td>
<td>Throws (TDZ)</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>No</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>function declaration</td>
<td>Fully usable</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Yes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>const fn = () =&gt; {}</code></td>
<td>Throws (TDZ)</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>No</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>class</code></td>
<td>Throws (TDZ)</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>No</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Temporal Dead Zone:</strong> the window between entering a
scope and the <code>let</code>/<code>const</code>/<code>class</code>
line. Touching the name there throws instead of silently giving
<code>undefined</code>.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb5"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb5-1"><a href="#cb5-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(a)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// undefined</span></span>
<span id="cb5-2"><a href="#cb5-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">var</span> a <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-3"><a href="#cb5-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-4"><a href="#cb5-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(b)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// ReferenceError: Cannot access &#39;b&#39; before initialization</span></span>
<span id="cb5-5"><a href="#cb5-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">let</span> b <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb5-6"><a href="#cb5-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-7"><a href="#cb5-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">start</span>()<span class="op">;</span>        <span class="co">// works: function declarations are fully hoisted</span></span>
<span id="cb5-8"><a href="#cb5-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">start</span>() {}</span>
<span id="cb5-9"><a href="#cb5-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb5-10"><a href="#cb5-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">boot</span>()<span class="op">;</span>         <span class="co">// TypeError: boot is not a function</span></span>
<span id="cb5-11"><a href="#cb5-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">var</span> boot <span class="op">=</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {}<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>My rule:</strong> <code>const</code> by default,
<code>let</code> only when the value really changes, <code>var</code>
never. The TDZ is a feature: it turns a silent <code>undefined</code>
into a loud error at the exact line. Remember that <code>const</code>
blocks re-assignment, not mutation; <code>const config = {}</code> can
still be changed, so use <code>Object.freeze</code> for config objects
you share.</p>
<p><strong>In production:</strong> the TDZ shows up in circular imports.
Module A imports B, B imports A and reads a <code>const</code> from A
before A has finished initialising. The fix is to break the cycle (move
the shared piece to a third module), not to switch to
<code>var</code>.</p>
<h3 id="closures">1.4 Closures</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a function keeps a live reference to the
variables of the scope it was created in, and can use them after that
scope has returned. It holds references, not copies, so it always sees
the current value.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb6"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb6-1"><a href="#cb6-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">createRateCounter</span>() {</span>
<span id="cb6-2"><a href="#cb6-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">let</span> hits <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span>                        <span class="co">// private, only reachable through the closure</span></span>
<span id="cb6-3"><a href="#cb6-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> {</span>
<span id="cb6-4"><a href="#cb6-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="dt">hit</span><span class="op">:</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="op">++</span>hits<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb6-5"><a href="#cb6-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="dt">count</span><span class="op">:</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> hits<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb6-6"><a href="#cb6-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb6-7"><a href="#cb6-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Where you already use closures daily:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Express middleware factories:
<code>const requireRole = (role) =&gt; (req, res, next) =&gt; {...}</code></li>
<li>Debounce and throttle (the timer lives in a closure)</li>
<li>Memoisation caches and lazy singletons (<code>getDbClient()</code>
that creates once)</li>
<li>Every React hook callback, which closes over that render’s
state</li>
<li>Module pattern: private state without classes</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>The interview classic:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb7"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb7-1"><a href="#cb7-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> (<span class="kw">var</span> i <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span> i <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="dv">3</span><span class="op">;</span> i<span class="op">++</span>) <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(i))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb7-2"><a href="#cb7-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// 3 3 3: one function-scoped i, read after the loop finished</span></span>
<span id="cb7-3"><a href="#cb7-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb7-4"><a href="#cb7-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> (<span class="kw">let</span> i <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span> i <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="dv">3</span><span class="op">;</span> i<span class="op">++</span>) <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(i))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb7-5"><a href="#cb7-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// 0 1 2: let gives each iteration its own binding</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Stale closure in React (the version seniors get
asked):</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb8"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb8-1"><a href="#cb8-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">Timer</span>() {</span>
<span id="cb8-2"><a href="#cb8-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> [count<span class="op">,</span> setCount] <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">useState</span>(<span class="dv">0</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb8-3"><a href="#cb8-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">useEffect</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb8-4"><a href="#cb8-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> id <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">setInterval</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="fu">setCount</span>(count <span class="op">+</span> <span class="dv">1</span>)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">1000</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// count is always 0 here</span></span>
<span id="cb8-5"><a href="#cb8-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">return</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="pp">clearInterval</span>(id)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb8-6"><a href="#cb8-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">,</span> [])<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb8-7"><a href="#cb8-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="co">// fix: setCount(c =&gt; c + 1), or add count to the dependency array</span></span>
<span id="cb8-8"><a href="#cb8-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Where closures hurt in production:</strong> anything a
closure references stays in memory as long as the closure is reachable.
Long-lived closures (a global cache, an event listener never removed, a
<code>setInterval</code> never cleared) quietly pin large objects.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb9"><pre class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb9-1"><a href="#cb9-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> handlers <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Map</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb9-2"><a href="#cb9-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">onRequest</span>(req) {</span>
<span id="cb9-3"><a href="#cb9-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> payload <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Buffer</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">alloc</span>(<span class="dv">5</span> <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">1024</span> <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">1024</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb9-4"><a href="#cb9-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  handlers<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="op">,</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> payload<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">length</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// 5 MB pinned per request, never released</span></span>
<span id="cb9-5"><a href="#cb9-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>How I’d find it: heap grows steadily under constant load. Take two
heap snapshots a few minutes apart with <code>node --inspect</code>,
compare them, sort by retained size, and follow the retainer path to the
Map. Fix by bounding the cache (LRU or TTL), keeping only what you need,
and removing listeners and timers on cleanup.</p>
<p><strong>Trade-offs:</strong> closures give real privacy and very
small, composable code. The cost is hidden lifetime: it is not obvious
from the code how long captured data lives, which is exactly why leaks
are hard to spot in review.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-1">How I’d answer — Hour 1</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. What is a closure? Give a real use.</strong> “A function
plus a live reference to the variables where it was defined, so it can
use them after that scope has returned. I use them all the time:
middleware factories like <code>requireRole('admin')</code>, debounced
handlers, lazy DB client singletons. The one I watch for is the memory
side: a closure stored in a long-lived structure keeps everything it
captured alive.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. Are <code>let</code> and <code>const</code>
hoisted?</strong> “Yes. Everything is registered in the creation pass.
The difference is initialisation: <code>var</code> starts as
<code>undefined</code>, while <code>let</code>, <code>const</code> and
<code>class</code> stay uninitialised in the temporal dead zone, so
touching them early throws. I prefer that, because it fails at the exact
line.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. Output?</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb10"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb10-1"><a href="#cb10-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">var</span> x <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb10-2"><a href="#cb10-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">f</span>() { <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(x)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">var</span> x <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb10-3"><a href="#cb10-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">f</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>“<code>undefined</code>. The inner <code>var x</code> is hoisted to
the top of <code>f</code> and shadows the outer one before it’s
assigned.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. How would you find a memory leak caused by closures in a
Node service?</strong> “First confirm it: heap and RSS rising under
steady traffic, GC not bringing it back down. Then two or three heap
snapshots under load, diff them, look at what’s growing and walk the
retainer chain. It’s usually a Map used as a cache with no eviction,
listeners added per request, or intervals never cleared. Fix the
lifetime, then add a heap metric to the dashboard so it can’t come back
silently.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. Why does this React interval always show 1?</strong> “The
interval callback closed over <code>count</code> from the first render,
which is 0, and the effect never re-runs because the dependency array is
empty. Use the functional updater <code>setCount(c =&gt; c + 1)</code>
or include <code>count</code> in the deps.”</p>
<h3 id="practice">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write <code>once(fn)</code> and
<code>memoize(fn)</code> from memory</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Reproduce the closure memory leak
above, find it with heap snapshots, then fix it</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Reproduce the stale-closure Timer
bug in a small React app and fix it both ways</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-2-this-prototypes-classes-modern-js">Hour 2 —
<code>this</code>, prototypes, classes, modern JS</h2>
<p>These come up less as trivia and more as “why did this break”: a
controller method that lost its <code>this</code>, an inheritance tree
nobody can change, a utility library pulled in for something the
language now does. Revise with those failures in mind.</p>
<h3 id="how-this-is-decided">2.1 How <code>this</code> is decided</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> <code>this</code> is bound when a
function is <strong>called</strong>, based on how it is called. Arrow
functions are the exception: they have no <code>this</code> of their own
and use the one from the surrounding code.</p>
<p>Check the call site against these rules, top rule wins:</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Rule</th>
<th>Call looks like</th>
<th><code>this</code> is</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>new</code></td>
<td><code>new Order()</code></td>
<td>The new object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Explicit</td>
<td><code>fn.call(obj)</code>, <code>fn.apply(obj)</code>,
<code>fn.bind(obj)</code></td>
<td><code>obj</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Implicit</td>
<td><code>obj.fn()</code></td>
<td>Whatever is left of the dot</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Default</td>
<td><code>fn()</code></td>
<td><code>undefined</code> in strict mode and ES modules (global object
in sloppy scripts)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb11"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb11-1"><a href="#cb11-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> svc <span class="op">=</span> {</span>
<span id="cb11-2"><a href="#cb11-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">name</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;orders&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb11-3"><a href="#cb11-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">regular</span>() { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">name</span><span class="op">;</span> }<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb11-4"><a href="#cb11-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">arrow</span><span class="op">:</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">?.</span><span class="at">name</span><span class="op">,</span>              <span class="co">// module scope, so undefined</span></span>
<span id="cb11-5"><a href="#cb11-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">later</span>() { <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">name</span>))<span class="op">;</span> }<span class="op">,</span> <span class="co">// arrow inherits from later()</span></span>
<span id="cb11-6"><a href="#cb11-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb11-7"><a href="#cb11-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>svc<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">regular</span>()<span class="op">;</span>          <span class="co">// &#39;orders&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb11-8"><a href="#cb11-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> detached <span class="op">=</span> svc<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">regular</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb11-9"><a href="#cb11-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">detached</span>()<span class="op">;</span>             <span class="co">// TypeError in strict mode: this is undefined</span></span>
<span id="cb11-10"><a href="#cb11-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>svc<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">later</span>()<span class="op">;</span>            <span class="co">// &#39;orders&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>In production:</strong> the bug is almost always a method
passed as a callback, which detaches it from its object.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb12"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb12-1"><a href="#cb12-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">class</span> OrderController {</span>
<span id="cb12-2"><a href="#cb12-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">constructor</span>(service) { <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">service</span> <span class="op">=</span> service<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb12-3"><a href="#cb12-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">async</span> <span class="fu">list</span>(req<span class="op">,</span> res) { res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">json</span>(<span class="cf">await</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">service</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">findAll</span>())<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb12-4"><a href="#cb12-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb12-5"><a href="#cb12-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> ctrl <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">OrderController</span>(orderService)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb12-6"><a href="#cb12-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>router<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/orders&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> ctrl<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">list</span>)<span class="op">;</span>              <span class="co">// crashes: this is undefined inside list</span></span>
<span id="cb12-7"><a href="#cb12-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>router<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/orders&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> (req<span class="op">,</span> res) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> ctrl<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">list</span>(req<span class="op">,</span> res))<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// fine</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Three fixes, in the order I’d pick them: wrap in an arrow at the call
site; define the method as a class field arrow
(<code>list = async (req, res) =&gt; {...}</code>); or
<code>this.list = this.list.bind(this)</code> in the constructor.
Frameworks like NestJS avoid the whole problem because the framework
calls methods on the instance.</p>
<p><strong>Arrow vs regular function — my rule:</strong> arrows for
callbacks and anything inside a method that needs the outer
<code>this</code>. Regular methods on classes and objects. Never arrows
as object methods that need the object, as constructors, or where you
need <code>arguments</code>.</p>
<h3 id="call-apply-bind">2.2 call, apply, bind</h3>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>Runs now?</th>
<th>Args</th>
<th>Returns</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>call(ctx, a, b)</code></td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>One by one</td>
<td>The result</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>apply(ctx, [a, b])</code></td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>As an array</td>
<td>The result</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>bind(ctx, a)</code></td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Can pre-fill some</td>
<td>A new function</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb13"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb13-1"><a href="#cb13-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">format</span>(prefix<span class="op">,</span> suffix) { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>prefix<span class="sc">}${</span><span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="sc">}${</span>suffix<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb13-2"><a href="#cb13-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> order <span class="op">=</span> { <span class="dt">id</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;ORD-9&#39;</span> }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb13-3"><a href="#cb13-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>format<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">call</span>(order<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;#&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;!&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span>     <span class="co">// &#39;#ORD-9!&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb13-4"><a href="#cb13-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>format<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">apply</span>(order<span class="op">,</span> [<span class="st">&#39;#&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;.&#39;</span>])<span class="op">;</span>  <span class="co">// &#39;#ORD-9.&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb13-5"><a href="#cb13-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> tag <span class="op">=</span> format<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">bind</span>(order<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;#&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb13-6"><a href="#cb13-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">tag</span>(<span class="st">&#39;?&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span>                         <span class="co">// &#39;#ORD-9?&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>A bound function cannot be re-bound; only <code>new</code> overrides
it. In modern code I rarely write <code>apply</code> (spread does the
same job), and <code>bind</code> mostly appears in older class
components and event wiring.</p>
<h3 id="prototypes">2.3 Prototypes</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> every object has an internal link to
another object, its prototype. When a property isn’t on the object, the
engine follows that link, and the next, until it hits <code>null</code>.
That chain is how JS inheritance works, and classes are built on it.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Fn.prototype</code> is the object that instances created with
<code>new Fn()</code> link to.</li>
<li><code>Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)</code> (old form
<code>obj.__proto__</code>) is the link on the instance itself.</li>
<li>An array’s chain: <code>arr</code> → <code>Array.prototype</code> →
<code>Object.prototype</code> → <code>null</code>.</li>
</ul>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb14"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb14-1"><a href="#cb14-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">Animal</span>(name) { <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">name</span> <span class="op">=</span> name<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb14-2"><a href="#cb14-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>Animal<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">prototype</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">speak</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">function</span> () { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">name</span><span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> makes a sound`</span><span class="op">;</span> }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb14-3"><a href="#cb14-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb14-4"><a href="#cb14-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">Dog</span>(name) { Animal<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">call</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">,</span> name)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb14-5"><a href="#cb14-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>Dog<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">prototype</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Object</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">create</span>(Animal<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">prototype</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb14-6"><a href="#cb14-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>Dog<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">prototype</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">constructor</span> <span class="op">=</span> Dog<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb14-7"><a href="#cb14-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>Dog<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">prototype</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">speak</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">function</span> () { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">name</span><span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> barks`</span><span class="op">;</span> }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb14-8"><a href="#cb14-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb14-9"><a href="#cb14-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">Dog</span>(<span class="st">&#39;Rex&#39;</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">speak</span>()<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// &#39;Rex barks&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>What <code>new</code> actually does:</strong> create an empty
object, link it to <code>Fn.prototype</code>, run <code>Fn</code> with
<code>this</code> set to it, and return it (unless <code>Fn</code>
returns its own object).</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb15"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb15-1"><a href="#cb15-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">myNew</span>(Fn<span class="op">,</span> <span class="op">...</span>args) {</span>
<span id="cb15-2"><a href="#cb15-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> obj <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Object</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">create</span>(Fn<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">prototype</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb15-3"><a href="#cb15-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> result <span class="op">=</span> Fn<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">apply</span>(obj<span class="op">,</span> args)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb15-4"><a href="#cb15-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> result <span class="op">!==</span> <span class="kw">null</span> <span class="op">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="kw">typeof</span> result <span class="op">===</span> <span class="st">&#39;object&#39;</span> <span class="op">?</span> result <span class="op">:</span> obj<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb15-5"><a href="#cb15-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Trade-offs:</strong> sharing methods through the prototype
means one copy in memory for a million instances, which is why it
scales. The downsides are deep chains that are hard to follow and the
temptation to patch built-ins. Never modify <code>Array.prototype</code>
or <code>Object.prototype</code> in an application; it breaks libraries
in ways that take days to trace. <strong>Prototype pollution</strong> is
also a real security issue: merging untrusted JSON with a
<code>__proto__</code> key into an object can inject properties into
every object in the process. Validate input and use
<code>Object.create(null)</code> or <code>Map</code> for dictionaries
built from user data.</p>
<h3 id="classes">2.4 Classes</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> syntax over prototypes. Methods still
live on <code>Class.prototype</code>. What classes add: strict mode by
default, mandatory <code>new</code>, <code>super</code>, true private
fields, and static members.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb16"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb16-1"><a href="#cb16-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">class</span> Repository {</span>
<span id="cb16-2"><a href="#cb16-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  #items <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Map</span>()<span class="op">;</span>              <span class="co">// private: not reachable from outside, not even via bracket access</span></span>
<span id="cb16-3"><a href="#cb16-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">static</span> instances <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb16-4"><a href="#cb16-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">constructor</span>(name) { <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">name</span> <span class="op">=</span> name<span class="op">;</span> Repository<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">instances</span><span class="op">++;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb16-5"><a href="#cb16-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">save</span>(item) { <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span>#<span class="at">items</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(item<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="op">,</span> item)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="cf">return</span> item<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb16-6"><a href="#cb16-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">get</span> <span class="fu">size</span>() { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span>#<span class="at">items</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">size</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb16-7"><a href="#cb16-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb16-8"><a href="#cb16-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb16-9"><a href="#cb16-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">class</span> UserRepository <span class="kw">extends</span> Repository {</span>
<span id="cb16-10"><a href="#cb16-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">constructor</span>() { <span class="kw">super</span>(<span class="st">&#39;users&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> }   <span class="co">// must run before using this</span></span>
<span id="cb16-11"><a href="#cb16-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">save</span>(user) {</span>
<span id="cb16-12"><a href="#cb16-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span>user<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">email</span>) <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Error</span>(<span class="st">&#39;email required&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb16-13"><a href="#cb16-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">super</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">save</span>(user)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb16-14"><a href="#cb16-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb16-15"><a href="#cb16-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>My rule: composition over inheritance.</strong> One level of
<code>extends</code> for a genuine “is-a” (a
<code>NotFoundError extends AppError</code>) is fine. Beyond that,
inject collaborators instead. A <code>UserService</code> that receives a
<code>UserRepository</code> and a <code>Mailer</code> is easier to test,
mock and change than a
<code>UserService extends BaseService extends Auditable</code>. This is
exactly how NestJS and Angular DI are designed, and saying so links your
JS knowledge to architecture.</p>
<h3 id="modern-js-worth-using">2.5 Modern JS worth using</h3>
<p>Know what each one replaces; interviewers like hearing that you
dropped a dependency because the language caught up.</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Feature</th>
<th>Example</th>
<th>What it replaces</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Optional chaining</td>
<td><code>order?.customer?.address?.city</code></td>
<td><code>a &amp;&amp; a.b &amp;&amp; a.b.c</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Nullish coalescing</td>
<td><code>limit ?? 20</code></td>
<td><code>limit \|\| 20</code>, which wrongly overrides
<code>0</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Promise.allSettled</code> / <code>Promise.any</code></td>
<td>Bulk sends, fastest replica</td>
<td>Custom wrappers</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Top-level <code>await</code> (ESM)</td>
<td><code>const cfg = await loadConfig()</code></td>
<td>Async IIFE at startup</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>Reverse then find</td>

</tr>

<td><code>hasOwnProperty.call</code></td>
</tr>

<td><code>#items</code></td>
<td><code>_items</code> naming convention</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Check your Node version before relying on the newest ones
(<code>Object.groupBy</code> needs Node 21+); Node 24 LTS has all of the
above (as of Nov 2026, Node 26 is the Active LTS line and Node 22
reaches end of life in April 2027).</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-2">How I’d answer — Hour 2</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. How is <code>this</code> determined?</strong> “By how the
function is called. <code>new</code> first, then explicit
<code>call</code>/<code>apply</code>/<code>bind</code>, then the object
before the dot, otherwise undefined in strict mode. Arrow functions
don’t have their own <code>this</code>; they use the enclosing one. In
practice the bug I look for is a method passed as a callback, like an
Express route handler, which loses its object.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. call vs apply vs bind?</strong> “<code>call</code> and
<code>apply</code> invoke immediately with a chosen <code>this</code>;
<code>call</code> takes arguments individually, <code>apply</code> as an
array. <code>bind</code> returns a new function with <code>this</code>
fixed, for later. Spread syntax has mostly replaced
<code>apply</code>.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. Explain prototypal inheritance and how classes
relate.</strong> “Objects link to other objects; lookups walk that
chain. Classes are syntax over it: methods sit on the prototype,
<code>extends</code> wires the chain, <code>super</code> calls up.
Classes add strict mode and real private fields. Architecturally I keep
inheritance shallow and prefer composition through DI.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. What is prototype pollution?</strong> “Merging untrusted
input that contains <code>__proto__</code> or
<code>constructor.prototype</code> into an object, which adds properties
to <code>Object.prototype</code> and therefore to every object. It has
caused real CVEs in merge utilities. Defences: validate request bodies
with a schema, avoid recursive merges of user input, use
<code>Map</code> or <code>Object.create(null)</code> for user-keyed
dictionaries, keep dependencies patched.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. Output?</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb17"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb17-1"><a href="#cb17-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> counter <span class="op">=</span> {</span>
<span id="cb17-2"><a href="#cb17-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">count</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">10</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb17-3"><a href="#cb17-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">inc</span>() { <span class="cf">return</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="op">++</span><span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">count</span><span class="op">;</span> }<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb17-4"><a href="#cb17-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb17-5"><a href="#cb17-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> f <span class="op">=</span> counter<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">inc</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb17-6"><a href="#cb17-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="fu">f</span>()<span class="op">,</span> <span class="fu">f</span>())<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>“<code>11 12</code>. The arrow captured <code>this</code> from
<code>inc</code>, which was called on <code>counter</code>.”</p>

<h2 id="hour-3-event-loop-promises-asyncawait">Hour 3 — Event loop,
promises, async/await</h2>
<p>For a Node engineer this hour matters more than any other in Week 1.
The event loop is where slow endpoints, timeouts under load and “the
server stopped responding” incidents come from. Interviewers will push
past the diagram into those consequences, so revise both.</p>
<h3 id="the-event-loop">3.1 The event loop</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> JS runs your code on one thread with one
call stack. Slow work (network, disk, timers, DNS) is handed off to the
OS or libuv. When it finishes, its callback waits in a queue. The event
loop’s job: when the stack is empty, pick the next callback and run
it.</p>
<p>The queues, in the order they get drained:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>process.nextTick</code> queue</strong> (Node only):
runs right after the current operation, before anything else.</li>
<li><strong>Microtask queue:</strong> promise callbacks
(<code>.then</code>, <code>.catch</code>, <code>.finally</code>, the
code after <code>await</code>) and <code>queueMicrotask</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Macrotask queues:</strong> timers, I/O callbacks,
<code>setImmediate</code>, close events.</li>
</ul>
<p>The rule that answers most puzzles: after each macrotask, Node drains
the whole nextTick queue, then the whole microtask queue, then moves to
the next macrotask. Since Node 11 this happens after every single
callback, matching browsers.</p>
<h3 id="nodes-phases-libuv">3.2 Node’s phases (libuv)</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Phase</th>
<th>Runs</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Timers</td>
<td>Expired <code>setTimeout</code> / <code>setInterval</code>
callbacks</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Pending callbacks</td>
<td>Some deferred system errors (e.g. TCP)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Poll</td>
<td>New I/O events and their callbacks; the loop waits here when
idle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Check</td>
<td><code>setImmediate</code> callbacks</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Close</td>
<td><code>'close'</code> handlers, e.g. sockets</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong><code>setTimeout(fn, 0)</code> vs
<code>setImmediate(fn)</code>:</strong> from the main module the order
is not guaranteed; it depends on loop start-up timing. Inside an I/O
callback <code>setImmediate</code> always wins, because check comes
straight after poll.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb18"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb18-1"><a href="#cb18-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;fs&#39;</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">readFile</span>(<span class="bu">__filename</span><span class="op">,</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb18-2"><a href="#cb18-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;timeout&#39;</span>)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb18-3"><a href="#cb18-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">setImmediate</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;immediate&#39;</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb18-4"><a href="#cb18-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// immediate, then timeout — every time</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong><code>process.nextTick</code>:</strong> the name is
misleading; it runs before the next phase, not on the next tick.
Recursive <code>nextTick</code> starves I/O completely. Legitimate use
is narrow (letting a caller attach listeners before you emit). Default
to <code>setImmediate</code> or <code>queueMicrotask</code>.</p>
<p><strong>What actually blocks the loop in real services:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>CPU work on the main thread: large
<code>JSON.parse</code>/<code>stringify</code> on multi-MB payloads,
crypto with sync APIs (<code>pbkdf2Sync</code>, <code>bcrypt</code>
sync), image or PDF processing, big sorts</li>
<li>Sync file APIs (<code>readFileSync</code>) inside request
handlers</li>
<li>Catastrophic regex backtracking on user input (ReDoS)</li>
<li>Huge loops over in-memory arrays for reporting</li>
</ul>
<p>While any of these runs, every other request waits, health checks
time out and Kubernetes may restart the pod. Detect with event-loop lag
metrics (<code>perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay</code>, or your APM),
find with <code>--cpu-prof</code> or clinic.js flame graphs, fix by
streaming, chunking work with <code>setImmediate</code>, moving CPU work
to <code>worker_threads</code>, or offloading to a queue.</p>
<h3 id="promises">3.3 Promises</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> an object for a value that will exist
later. Three states (pending, fulfilled, rejected); once settled it
never changes. <code>.then</code> handlers always run as microtasks,
even on an already-resolved promise, and every <code>.then</code>
returns a new promise, which is what makes chaining work.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb19"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb19-1"><a href="#cb19-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span>((resolve) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb19-2"><a href="#cb19-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="co">// the executor runs synchronously, right now</span></span>
<span id="cb19-3"><a href="#cb19-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="fu">resolve</span>(<span class="dv">42</span>)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">100</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb19-4"><a href="#cb19-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})</span>
<span id="cb19-5"><a href="#cb19-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>((v) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> v <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">2</span>)</span>
<span id="cb19-6"><a href="#cb19-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> { <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Error</span>(<span class="st">&#39;boom&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> })</span>
<span id="cb19-7"><a href="#cb19-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">catch</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="st">&#39;recovered&#39;</span>)     <span class="co">// returns a fulfilled promise</span></span>
<span id="cb19-8"><a href="#cb19-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">finally</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;cleanup&#39;</span>)) <span class="co">// sees no value, passes it through</span></span>
<span id="cb19-9"><a href="#cb19-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(<span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>)<span class="op">;</span>           <span class="co">// &#39;recovered&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Combinators and when I reach for each:</strong></p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Method</th>
<th>Settles when</th>
<th>I use it for</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Promise.all</code></td>
<td>All fulfil, or the first rejects</td>
<td>A page that needs user + orders + cart, all required</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Promise.allSettled</code></td>
<td>Everything settles, never rejects</td>
<td>Bulk emails or webhooks where partial failure is expected and
reported</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Promise.race</code></td>
<td>First to settle either way</td>
<td>Timeouts around calls that don’t support
<code>AbortSignal</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>Promise.any</code></td>
<td>First to fulfil; rejects only if all fail</td>
<td>Fastest of several mirrors or regions</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>One thing to mention unprompted: <code>Promise.all</code> fails fast
but does <strong>not</strong> cancel the others; they keep running and
consuming resources. For real cancellation pass an
<code>AbortController</code> signal to <code>fetch</code> and to drivers
that support it.</p>
<h3 id="asyncawait">3.4 async/await</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> syntax over promises. An
<code>async</code> function always returns a promise. <code>await</code>
suspends that one function; the rest of it resumes as a microtask. The
thread is free the whole time.</p>
<p><strong>The performance bug I look for in code review:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb20"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb20-1"><a href="#cb20-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// ~300 ms: three independent calls made one after another</span></span>
<span id="cb20-2"><a href="#cb20-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> user <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> userRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">find</span>(id)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb20-3"><a href="#cb20-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> orders <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> orderRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">byUser</span>(id)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb20-4"><a href="#cb20-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> wallet <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> walletRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">byUser</span>(id)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb20-5"><a href="#cb20-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb20-6"><a href="#cb20-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// ~100 ms: same calls in parallel</span></span>
<span id="cb20-7"><a href="#cb20-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> [u<span class="op">,</span> o<span class="op">,</span> w] <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">all</span>([</span>
<span id="cb20-8"><a href="#cb20-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  userRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">find</span>(id)<span class="op">,</span> orderRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">byUser</span>(id)<span class="op">,</span> walletRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">byUser</span>(id)<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb20-9"><a href="#cb20-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>])<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>The opposite mistake is just as bad: <code>Promise.all</code> over
10,000 items opens 10,000 DB queries at once and exhausts the connection
pool. For large lists, batch or cap concurrency (<code>p-limit</code>,
or chunks of 50).</p>
<p><strong>Error handling:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb21"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb21-1"><a href="#cb21-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>router<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/orders/:id&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">async</span> (req<span class="op">,</span> res<span class="op">,</span> next) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb21-2"><a href="#cb21-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">try</span> {</span>
<span id="cb21-3"><a href="#cb21-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">json</span>(<span class="cf">await</span> orderService<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">params</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb21-4"><a href="#cb21-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  } <span class="cf">catch</span> (err) {</span>
<span id="cb21-5"><a href="#cb21-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="fu">next</span>(err)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// Express 4 won&#39;t catch async errors for you; Express 5 does</span></span>
<span id="cb21-6"><a href="#cb21-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb21-7"><a href="#cb21-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Since Node 15 an unhandled rejection crashes the process. Treat that
as correct behaviour: log it, let the process exit, and let the
orchestrator restart it. Don’t register a handler that swallows it and
keeps running in an unknown state.</p>
<p><strong>Loops:</strong> <code>for...of</code> with <code>await</code>
is sequential, which is right when order matters or to protect a
downstream system. <code>array.forEach(async ...)</code> doesn’t wait
for anything; the function returns before the work is done and errors
become unhandled rejections.</p>
<p><strong>Callbacks vs promises vs async/await:</strong> callbacks
still live in core APIs (streams, events) and cost nothing, but nest
badly and repeat error handling. Promises give one <code>.catch</code>
and combinators. async/await reads like sync code and gives better stack
traces; its risk is accidental sequential code and forgotten
<code>await</code>s. Turn on the
<code>@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises</code> lint rule to catch
those.</p>
<h3 id="output-puzzles">3.5 Output puzzles</h3>
<p>Work each on paper first, then run it.</p>
<p><strong>Puzzle 1 (CommonJS file):</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb22"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb22-1"><a href="#cb22-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;1&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb22-2"><a href="#cb22-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;2&#39;</span>)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb22-3"><a href="#cb22-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resolve</span>()<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;3&#39;</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb22-4"><a href="#cb22-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">process</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">nextTick</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;4&#39;</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb22-5"><a href="#cb22-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;5&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><code>1 5 4 3 2</code>. Sync code, then nextTick, then the promise
microtask, then the timer. Worth adding: in an <code>.mjs</code> file
the output is <code>1 5 3 4 2</code>, because ES module code itself runs
inside a promise job, so promise callbacks drain before the nextTick
queue.</p>
<p><strong>Puzzle 2:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb23"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb23-1"><a href="#cb23-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">async</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">a</span>() { <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;a1&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="fu">b</span>()<span class="op">;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;a2&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb23-2"><a href="#cb23-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">async</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">b</span>() { <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;b&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb23-3"><a href="#cb23-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;start&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="fu">a</span>()<span class="op">;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;end&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><code>start a1 b end a2</code>. Everything before the first
<code>await</code> runs synchronously, including the body of
<code>b</code>. <code>a2</code> is a microtask.</p>
<p><strong>Puzzle 3:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb24"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb24-1"><a href="#cb24-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;t1&#39;</span>)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
