<span id="cb24-4"><a href="#cb24-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;t2&#39;</span>)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb24-5"><a href="#cb24-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb24-6"><a href="#cb24-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resolve</span>()<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;p2&#39;</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb24-7"><a href="#cb24-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb24-8"><a href="#cb24-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;t3&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb24-9"><a href="#cb24-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resolve</span>()<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;p3&#39;</span>))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb24-10"><a href="#cb24-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><code>p1 p2 t1 t3 p3 t2</code>. Microtasks first; timers in the order
they were created; <code>p3</code> runs immediately after
<code>t3</code> because microtasks drain after each macrotask;
<code>t2</code> was queued last.</p>
<p><strong>Puzzle 4:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb25"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb25-1"><a href="#cb25-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> p <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span>((resolve) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> { <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;A&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="fu">resolve</span>(<span class="st">&#39;B&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;C&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb25-2"><a href="#cb25-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>p<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(<span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb25-3"><a href="#cb25-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="st">&#39;D&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><code>A C D B</code>. The executor is synchronous and
<code>resolve</code> doesn’t stop it.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-3">How I’d answer — Hour 3</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Explain the event loop.</strong> “One thread runs JS. I/O
is delegated to the OS or the libuv thread pool, and completed work
queues a callback. Whenever the stack is empty, Node drains nextTick,
then promise microtasks, then runs the next macrotask, moving through
phases: timers, poll, check, close. The practical consequence is that
any synchronous CPU work stalls every request on that process, so I keep
handlers I/O-bound and push CPU work to worker threads or a queue.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. How does Node handle 10,000 concurrent requests on one
thread?</strong> “Most of a request’s life is waiting on the network or
a database. Sockets are non-blocking, so Node registers interest and the
OS tells libuv when data arrives. The thread only spends microseconds
per request on actual JS. It breaks down when requests need CPU, so you
scale with multiple processes (cluster or more pods) and worker threads
for heavy computation.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. A service’s p99 latency jumps to seconds but CPU sits at
100% on one core. What do you check?</strong> “Event-loop blocking. I’d
check the event-loop delay metric, then take a CPU profile under load to
find the hot function. Common culprits: a big JSON serialisation, a sync
crypto call, a regex on user input. Fix by streaming or chunking, moving
it to a worker thread, or caching the result.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. <code>Promise.all</code> vs
<code>allSettled</code>?</strong> “<code>all</code> when every result is
required: it fails fast on the first rejection, but the others keep
running. <code>allSettled</code> when tasks are independent and I want a
per-item report, like sending notifications. For large lists I cap
concurrency either way so I don’t flood the database.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. What’s wrong with
<code>items.forEach(async (i) =&gt; await save(i))</code>?</strong>
“<code>forEach</code> ignores the returned promises. The caller
continues before anything is saved and any failure becomes an unhandled
rejection, which crashes modern Node. Use <code>for...of</code> with
<code>await</code> for sequential, or <code>Promise.all</code> with a
concurrency limit for parallel.”</p>

<h2 id="hour-4-polyfills-round-capstone-setup">Hour 4 — Polyfills round
+ capstone setup</h2>
<p>Machine-coding rounds for senior Node roles often open with one of
these. They are not testing whether you have memorised the code; they
watch how you handle edge cases, name things and talk through
trade-offs. Do 40 minutes of polyfills with no AI and no autocomplete,
timing each one. Then 20 minutes setting up the capstone with Claude
Code.</p>
<p>For each one: write it, list the edge cases out loud, then compare
with the reference below.</p>
<h3 id="promise.all">4.1 <code>Promise.all</code></h3>
<p>Edge cases to call out before coding: empty input resolves to
<code>[]</code>; plain values are allowed; results keep input order, not
completion order; first rejection wins.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb26"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb26-1"><a href="#cb26-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">promiseAll</span>(iterable) {</span>
<span id="cb26-2"><a href="#cb26-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span>((resolve<span class="op">,</span> reject) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb26-3"><a href="#cb26-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> items <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Array</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">from</span>(iterable)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-4"><a href="#cb26-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> results <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Array</span>(items<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">length</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-5"><a href="#cb26-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">let</span> remaining <span class="op">=</span> items<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">length</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-6"><a href="#cb26-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (remaining <span class="op">===</span> <span class="dv">0</span>) <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="fu">resolve</span>([])<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-7"><a href="#cb26-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    items<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">forEach</span>((item<span class="op">,</span> i) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb26-8"><a href="#cb26-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resolve</span>(item)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>((value) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb26-9"><a href="#cb26-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        results[i] <span class="op">=</span> value<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-10"><a href="#cb26-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">--</span>remaining <span class="op">===</span> <span class="dv">0</span>) <span class="fu">resolve</span>(results)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-11"><a href="#cb26-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      }<span class="op">,</span> reject)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// later rejections are ignored: a promise settles once</span></span>
<span id="cb26-12"><a href="#cb26-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-13"><a href="#cb26-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb26-14"><a href="#cb26-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Likely follow-ups: why <code>Promise.resolve(item)</code> (it accepts
plain values and thenables), and why a counter instead of
<code>results.length</code> (assigning index 5 first makes
<code>length</code> 6 immediately).</p>
<h3 id="promise.allsettled">4.2 <code>Promise.allSettled</code></h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb27"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb27-1"><a href="#cb27-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> promiseAllSettled <span class="op">=</span> (iterable) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span></span>
<span id="cb27-2"><a href="#cb27-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">promiseAll</span>(<span class="bu">Array</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">from</span>(iterable<span class="op">,</span> (item) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span></span>
<span id="cb27-3"><a href="#cb27-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resolve</span>(item)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(</span>
<span id="cb27-4"><a href="#cb27-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      (value) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> ({ <span class="dt">status</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;fulfilled&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> value })<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb27-5"><a href="#cb27-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      (reason) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> ({ <span class="dt">status</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;rejected&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> reason })<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb27-6"><a href="#cb27-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    )<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb27-7"><a href="#cb27-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  ))<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>The point to make: map every outcome to a fulfilled result object,
then reuse <code>all</code>. Reusing your own building block is what
they want to see.</p>
<h3 id="debounce">4.3 Debounce</h3>
<p>Runs the function only after calls have stopped for <code>wait</code>
ms; every new call restarts the timer.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb28"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb28-1"><a href="#cb28-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">debounce</span>(fn<span class="op">,</span> wait <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">300</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb28-2"><a href="#cb28-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">let</span> timer<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb28-3"><a href="#cb28-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">debounced</span>(<span class="op">...</span>args) {</span>
<span id="cb28-4"><a href="#cb28-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="pp">clearTimeout</span>(timer)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb28-5"><a href="#cb28-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    timer <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> fn<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">apply</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">,</span> args)<span class="op">,</span> wait)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// latest this and args</span></span>
<span id="cb28-6"><a href="#cb28-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb28-7"><a href="#cb28-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  debounced<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">cancel</span> <span class="op">=</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="pp">clearTimeout</span>(timer)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb28-8"><a href="#cb28-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> debounced<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb28-9"><a href="#cb28-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Mention <code>cancel</code> yourself: in React you call it in the
effect cleanup, otherwise the debounced call fires after the component
unmounts.</p>
<h3 id="throttle">4.4 Throttle</h3>
<p>Runs at most once per <code>interval</code>, with a trailing call so
the last event isn’t lost.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb29"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb29-1"><a href="#cb29-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">throttle</span>(fn<span class="op">,</span> interval <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">200</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb29-2"><a href="#cb29-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">let</span> last <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-3"><a href="#cb29-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">let</span> trailing<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-4"><a href="#cb29-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">throttled</span>(<span class="op">...</span>args) {</span>
<span id="cb29-5"><a href="#cb29-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> remaining <span class="op">=</span> interval <span class="op">-</span> (<span class="bu">Date</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">now</span>() <span class="op">-</span> last)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-6"><a href="#cb29-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="pp">clearTimeout</span>(trailing)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-7"><a href="#cb29-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (remaining <span class="op">&lt;=</span> <span class="dv">0</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb29-8"><a href="#cb29-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      last <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Date</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">now</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-9"><a href="#cb29-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      fn<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">apply</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">,</span> args)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-10"><a href="#cb29-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    } <span class="cf">else</span> {</span>
<span id="cb29-11"><a href="#cb29-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      trailing <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb29-12"><a href="#cb29-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        last <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Date</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">now</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-13"><a href="#cb29-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        fn<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">apply</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">,</span> args)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-14"><a href="#cb29-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      }<span class="op">,</span> remaining)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-15"><a href="#cb29-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    }</span>
<span id="cb29-16"><a href="#cb29-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb29-17"><a href="#cb29-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>Debounce</th>
<th>Throttle</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Fires</td>
<td>Once, after things go quiet</td>
<td>Steadily, at a capped rate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Use for</td>
<td>Search-as-you-type, autosave, resize end</td>
<td>Scroll, mousemove, infinite-scroll checks, progress events</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Watch out</td>
<td>Never fires if events never stop</td>
<td>Drops intermediate events</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>On the backend the same idea appears as rate limiting (throttle) and
coalescing bursts of change events before reindexing (debounce).</p>
<h3 id="function.prototype.bind">4.5
<code>Function.prototype.bind</code></h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb30"><pre

<h3 id="deep-clone">4.6 Deep clone</h3>
<p>Handle primitives, arrays, plain objects, <code>Date</code>,
<code>Map</code>, <code>Set</code>, and circular references.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb31"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb31-1"><a href="#cb31-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">deepClone</span>(value<span class="op">,</span> seen <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">WeakMap</span>()) {</span>
<span id="cb31-2"><a href="#cb31-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (value <span class="op">===</span> <span class="kw">null</span> <span class="op">||</span> <span class="kw">typeof</span> value <span class="op">!==</span> <span class="st">&#39;object&#39;</span>) <span class="cf">return</span> value<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-3"><a href="#cb31-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (seen<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">has</span>(value)) <span class="cf">return</span> seen<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(value)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-4"><a href="#cb31-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (value <span class="kw">instanceof</span> <span class="bu">Date</span>) <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Date</span>(value)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-5"><a href="#cb31-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (value <span class="kw">instanceof</span> <span class="bu">Map</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb31-6"><a href="#cb31-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> copy <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Map</span>()<span class="op">;</span> seen<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(value<span class="op">,</span> copy)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-7"><a href="#cb31-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    value<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">forEach</span>((v<span class="op">,</span> k) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> copy<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(<span class="fu">deepClone</span>(k<span class="op">,</span> seen)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="fu">deepClone</span>(v<span class="op">,</span> seen)))<span class="op">;</span></span>

<span id="cb31-11"><a href="#cb31-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> copy <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Set</span>()<span class="op">;</span> seen<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(value<span class="op">,</span> copy)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-12"><a href="#cb31-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    value<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">forEach</span>((v) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> copy<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">add</span>(<span class="fu">deepClone</span>(v<span class="op">,</span> seen)))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-13"><a href="#cb31-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">return</span> copy<span class="op">;</span></span>

<span id="cb31-15"><a href="#cb31-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> copy <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Array</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">isArray</span>(value) <span class="op">?</span> [] <span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Object</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">create</span>(<span class="bu">Object</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">getPrototypeOf</span>(value))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-16"><a href="#cb31-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  seen<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(value<span class="op">,</span> copy)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb31-17"><a href="#cb31-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">for</span> (<span class="kw">const</span> key <span class="kw">of</span> <span class="bu">Reflect</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">ownKeys</span>(value)) copy[key] <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">deepClone</span>(value[key]<span class="op">,</span> seen)<span class="op">;</span></span>

<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />

<tr>
<th>Approach</th>
<th>Deep</th>
<th>Good</th>
<th>Bad</th>
</tr>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Spread / <code>Object.assign</code></td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Fast, enough for flat objects</td>
<td>Nested objects stay shared</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>Yes</td>
<td>Short</td>

</tr>
<tr>

<td>Yes</td>

</tr>

<p>In real code I use spread for flat state,
<code>structuredClone</code> for data, and question why I need a deep
copy at all before writing a custom one.</p>

<span id="cb32-3"><a href="#cb32-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (args<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">length</span> <span class="op">&gt;=</span> fn<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">length</span>) <span class="cf">return</span> fn<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">apply</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">,</span> args)<span class="op">;</span></span>

<p>Starter <code>CLAUDE.md</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb35"><pre

<p>Review every generated file as you would a PR from a new team member.
Keep a short list of what you changed and why; those notes become
concrete answers when an interviewer asks how you use AI tools.</p>
<p><strong>Monorepo trade-offs:</strong> shared types and tooling,
atomic frontend-plus-backend changes, one CI; against that, CI gets slow
without build caching, and access control is coarser than separate
repos.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-4">How I’d answer — Hour 4</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Debounce vs throttle, with a real example of
each.</strong> “Debounce the product search box so we call the API once
the user pauses for 300 ms. Throttle the scroll listener that checks
whether to load the next page, so it runs at most every 200 ms. On the
server, the same ideas are rate limiting and coalescing bursts of
events.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. Why not <code>JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())</code> for
cloning?</strong> “It silently corrupts data: dates become strings,
<code>undefined</code> and functions vanish, Maps and Sets become empty
objects, and cycles throw. <code>structuredClone</code> covers most
cases natively. Often the better question is whether a deep copy is
needed at all.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How does your <code>Promise.all</code> keep
order?</strong> “Each result goes into the index of its input, and a
counter tells me when everything is done, so completion order doesn’t
matter.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. How do you use AI coding tools without lowering
quality?</strong> “I give them constraints up front in a project rules
file, ask for a plan before code, and review the output like a PR. Tests
and lint run before anything is called done. AI speeds up scaffolding
and tests a lot; for core design decisions I still write the approach
myself and use the tool to challenge it.”</p>

<h1 id="day-2-tue-typescript-full-depth">Day 2 (Tue) — TypeScript, full
depth</h1>
<h2 id="hour-1-the-type-system">Hour 1 — The type system</h2>
<p>Most people with your experience write TypeScript every day but have
never had to explain how it reasons. Interviews for lead roles probe
exactly that: why two unrelated types are assignable, when
<code>unknown</code> beats <code>any</code>, how you model state so
impossible states can’t compile. That last one is the real senior
signal.</p>
<h3 id="what-typescript-actually-is">1.1 What TypeScript actually
is</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a static type checker and compiler on
top of JavaScript. Types exist only at compile time and are erased; the
emitted JS has no idea they existed.</p>
<p><strong>Why that matters in production:</strong> TypeScript cannot
protect you from data you didn’t create. A request body, a Kafka
message, a third-party API response or a row from MongoDB is
<code>unknown</code> at runtime no matter what interface you cast it to.
Every trust boundary needs runtime validation (Zod, class-validator,
JSON Schema). Saying this early in an interview tells them you’ve been
bitten by it.</p>
<h3 id="structural-typing">1.2 Structural typing</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> compatibility is decided by shape, not
by name. If an object has at least the required properties with
compatible types, it fits, whatever it was called.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb36"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb36-1"><a href="#cb36-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">interface</span> <span class="bu">Point</span> { x<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">;</span> y<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span> }</span>
<span id="cb36-2"><a href="#cb36-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">class</span> Pixel { <span class="kw">constructor</span>(<span class="kw">public</span> x<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">public</span> y<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">public</span> color<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>) {} }</span>
<span id="cb36-3"><a href="#cb36-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb36-4"><a href="#cb36-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> p<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Point</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">Pixel</span>(<span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;red&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// OK: Pixel has x and y</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Excess property checks</strong> are the one exception: object
literals assigned directly are checked for extra keys, because that is
usually a typo.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb37"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb37-1"><a href="#cb37-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> a<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Point</span> <span class="op">=</span> { x<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">,</span> y<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">,</span> z<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">3</span> }<span class="op">;</span>   <span class="co">// error: &#39;z&#39; does not exist</span></span>
<span id="cb37-2"><a href="#cb37-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> raw <span class="op">=</span> { x<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">,</span> y<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">,</span> z<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">3</span> }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb37-3"><a href="#cb37-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> b<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Point</span> <span class="op">=</span> raw<span class="op">;</span>                     <span class="co">// OK: not a fresh literal</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Where it bites:</strong> two IDs that are both
<code>string</code> are interchangeable, so
<code>getOrder(userId)</code> compiles. Branded types (Hour 3) fix this
when it matters.</p>
<h3 id="type-vs-interface">1.3 <code>type</code> vs
<code>interface</code></h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th><code>interface</code></th>
<th><code>type</code></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Object shapes</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Yes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Unions, tuples, primitives, mapped/conditional types</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Yes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>extends</code> / intersection</td>
<td><code>extends</code> (clear errors on conflict)</td>
<td><code>&amp;</code> (conflicts silently become
<code>never</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Declaration merging</td>
<td>Yes, same name merges</td>
<td>No, duplicate is an error</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Implemented by classes</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Yes, if it’s an object type</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>My rule:</strong> <code>interface</code> for public object
contracts (DTOs, service interfaces, anything a consumer might extend);
<code>type</code> for unions, function types, and anything computed. The
real reason to pick <code>interface</code> for library contracts is
declaration merging, which is how you extend Express’s
<code>Request</code>:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb38"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb38-1"><a href="#cb38-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// types/express.d.ts</span></span>
<span id="cb38-2"><a href="#cb38-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">declare</span> <span class="bu">global</span> {</span>
<span id="cb38-3"><a href="#cb38-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="im">namespace</span> <span class="dt">Express</span> {</span>
<span id="cb38-4"><a href="#cb38-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">interface</span> Request { user<span class="op">?:</span> { id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> roles<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>[] } }</span>
<span id="cb38-5"><a href="#cb38-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb38-6"><a href="#cb38-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb38-7"><a href="#cb38-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> {}<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>One team convention, applied consistently, matters more than which
you choose.</p>
<h3 id="any-unknown-never">1.4 <code>any</code>, <code>unknown</code>,
<code>never</code></h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
<th>Assign anything to it?</th>
<th>Use it as anything?</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>any</code></td>
<td>Turn type checking off</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Yes (that’s the danger)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>unknown</code></td>
<td>Some value, not yet checked</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>No, must narrow first</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>never</code></td>
<td>No value can exist</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Yes (it’s the empty set)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb39"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb39-1"><a href="#cb39-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">parse</span>(json<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">unknown</span> {</span>
<span id="cb39-2"><a href="#cb39-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="bu">JSON</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">parse</span>(json)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb39-3"><a href="#cb39-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb39-4"><a href="#cb39-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> data <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">parse</span>(body)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb39-5"><a href="#cb39-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>data<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="op">;</span>                               <span class="co">// error: data is unknown</span></span>
<span id="cb39-6"><a href="#cb39-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="kw">typeof</span> data <span class="op">===</span> <span class="st">&#39;object&#39;</span> <span class="op">&amp;&amp;</span> data <span class="op">!==</span> <span class="kw">null</span> <span class="op">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="st">&#39;id&#39;</span> <span class="kw">in</span> data) {</span>
<span id="cb39-7"><a href="#cb39-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  data<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="op">;</span>                             <span class="co">// OK after narrowing</span></span>
<span id="cb39-8"><a href="#cb39-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>My rule:</strong> <code>any</code> is banned by lint
(<code>@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any</code>) except in a few typed
adapters at the edges, each with a comment. <code>unknown</code> is the
honest type for anything from outside. <code>any</code> is contagious:
one <code>any</code> flows into everything it touches and switches off
checking far from where it was written.</p>
<p><code>never</code> shows up as the return type of functions that
always throw or loop forever, as the result of impossible intersections,
and most usefully in exhaustiveness checks (1.6).</p>
<h3 id="narrowing-and-type-guards">1.5 Narrowing and type guards</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> TypeScript follows control flow and
refines a union type inside each branch.</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Guard</th>
<th>Example</th>
<th>Narrows</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>typeof</code></td>
<td><code>typeof x === 'string'</code></td>
<td>Primitives</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>instanceof</code></td>
<td><code>err instanceof HttpError</code></td>
<td>Classes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>in</code></td>
<td><code>'email' in user</code></td>
<td>Object shapes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Equality / truthiness</td>
<td><code>if (x != null)</code></td>
<td>Removes null/undefined</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Discriminant</td>
<td><code>event.type === 'paid'</code></td>
<td>Tagged unions</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Custom predicate</td>
<td><code>function isUser(x): x is User</code></td>
<td>Anything you can check</td>
</tr>

<td>Assertion function</td>
<td><code>function assertUser(x): asserts x is User</code></td>
<td>Throws if not, narrows after</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb40"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb40-1"><a href="#cb40-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">isApiError</span>(e<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">unknown</span>)<span class="op">:</span> e <span class="kw">is</span> { status<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">;</span> message<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span> } {</span>
<span id="cb40-2"><a href="#cb40-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">typeof</span> e <span class="op">===</span> <span class="st">&#39;object&#39;</span> <span class="op">&amp;&amp;</span> e <span class="op">!==</span> <span class="kw">null</span> <span class="op">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="st">&#39;status&#39;</span> <span class="kw">in</span> e <span class="op">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="st">&#39;message&#39;</span> <span class="kw">in</span> e<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb40-3"><a href="#cb40-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb40-4"><a href="#cb40-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb40-5"><a href="#cb40-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">try</span> { <span class="cf">await</span> client<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">call</span>()<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb40-6"><a href="#cb40-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">catch</span> (e) {                <span class="co">// e is unknown under useUnknownInCatchVariables (part of strict)</span></span>
<span id="cb40-7"><a href="#cb40-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="fu">isApiError</span>(e) <span class="op">&amp;&amp;</span> e<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">status</span> <span class="op">===</span> <span class="dv">404</span>) <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">null</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb40-8"><a href="#cb40-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">throw</span> e<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb40-9"><a href="#cb40-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>A type predicate is a promise you make to the compiler; if the check
is wrong, TypeScript believes you anyway. Keep predicates small and
tested, or derive them from a Zod schema.</p>
<h3 id="discriminated-unions-making-invalid-states-impossible">1.6
Discriminated unions: making invalid states impossible</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a union of object types that share a
literal “tag” field. Checking the tag narrows to exactly one member.</p>
<p>The weak model most codebases start with:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb41"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb41-1"><a href="#cb41-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">interface</span> PaymentState {</span>
<span id="cb41-2"><a href="#cb41-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  status<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;idle&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;loading&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;success&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;error&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb41-3"><a href="#cb41-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  data<span class="op">?:</span> Receipt<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb41-4"><a href="#cb41-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  error<span class="op">?:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb41-5"><a href="#cb41-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb41-6"><a href="#cb41-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Nothing stops { status: &#39;success&#39;, error: &#39;x&#39; } or &#39;loading&#39; with stale data</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>The model a senior should propose:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb42"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb42-1"><a href="#cb42-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> PaymentState <span class="op">=</span></span>
<span id="cb42-2"><a href="#cb42-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">|</span> { status<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;idle&#39;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb42-3"><a href="#cb42-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">|</span> { status<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;loading&#39;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb42-4"><a href="#cb42-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">|</span> { status<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;success&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span> receipt<span class="op">:</span> Receipt }</span>
<span id="cb42-5"><a href="#cb42-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">|</span> { status<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;error&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span> error<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> retryable<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">boolean</span> }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb42-6"><a href="#cb42-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb42-7"><a href="#cb42-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">render</span>(s<span class="op">:</span> PaymentState) {</span>
<span id="cb42-8"><a href="#cb42-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">switch</span> (s<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">status</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb42-9"><a href="#cb42-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&#39;idle&#39;</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="st">&#39;Pay now&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb42-10"><a href="#cb42-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&#39;loading&#39;</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="st">&#39;Processing…&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb42-11"><a href="#cb42-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&#39;success&#39;</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="vs">`Paid: </span><span class="sc">${</span>s<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">receipt</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span><span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// receipt guaranteed here</span></span>
<span id="cb42-12"><a href="#cb42-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">case</span> <span class="st">&#39;error&#39;</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="cf">return</span> s<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">retryable</span> <span class="op">?</span> <span class="st">&#39;Retry&#39;</span> <span class="op">:</span> s<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">error</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb42-13"><a href="#cb42-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">default</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="fu">assertNever</span>(s)<span class="op">;</span>                 <span class="co">// compile error if a status is added and not handled</span></span>
<span id="cb42-14"><a href="#cb42-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb42-15"><a href="#cb42-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb42-16"><a href="#cb42-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb42-17"><a href="#cb42-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">assertNever</span>(x<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">never</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">never</span> {</span>
<span id="cb42-18"><a href="#cb42-18" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Error</span>(<span class="vs">`Unhandled case: </span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="bu">JSON</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">stringify</span>(x)<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb42-19"><a href="#cb42-19" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Same pattern on the backend for domain events
(<code>OrderCreated | OrderPaid | OrderCancelled</code>), reducer
actions, and job results. When someone adds a new event type, every
switch that forgot it fails the build instead of failing in
production.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-1-1">How I’d answer — Hour 1</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. <code>type</code> or <code>interface</code>?</strong>
“They overlap for object shapes. I use <code>interface</code> for public
contracts because they can be extended and merged, which is how we add
<code>user</code> to Express’s <code>Request</code>. I use
<code>type</code> for unions, function signatures and computed types,
which interfaces can’t express. More than the choice itself, I care that
the team picks one convention and lints for it.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. <code>any</code> vs <code>unknown</code>?</strong>
“<code>any</code> turns checking off and spreads to everything it
touches. <code>unknown</code> says ‘I have a value but haven’t proven
what it is’, so you must narrow before using it. Anything crossing a
boundary, like <code>JSON.parse</code>, request bodies or catch
variables, should be <code>unknown</code> and then validated.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. If we use TypeScript, why do we still need request
validation?</strong> “Types are erased at compile time. At runtime a
request body is whatever the client sent. I validate at every boundary
with a schema library like Zod and infer the TypeScript type from the
schema, so validation and types can’t drift apart.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. How do you model a value that can be loading, loaded or
failed?</strong> “As a discriminated union with a <code>status</code>
tag, where each variant carries only the fields that make sense for it.
Then a switch narrows correctly and an <code>assertNever</code> default
turns a forgotten case into a compile error. It removes a whole class of
‘data is undefined’ bugs.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. What is structural typing and when has it surprised
you?</strong> “Types are compatible if their shapes match, regardless of
name. The classic surprise is that every ID is just a
<code>string</code>, so passing a <code>userId</code> where an
<code>orderId</code> is expected compiles. For identifiers where a
mix-up would be expensive, like money or tenant IDs, I use branded
types.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-3">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Model <code>OrderEvent</code> as a
discriminated union of 4 events and write an exhaustive
<code>handle(event)</code> with <code>assertNever</code></label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write <code>isApiError</code> and an
<code>assertIsDefined&lt;T&gt;(x): asserts x is T</code>
helper</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Augment Express <code>Request</code>
with a typed <code>user</code> and use it in a middleware</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-2-generics-and-utility-types">Hour 2 — Generics and utility
types</h2>
<p>Generics are where TypeScript code either stays flexible and safe or
collapses into <code>any</code>. In interviews expect to write a small
generic function on the spot, and to explain why a constraint is needed.
In real codebases they show up in repositories, API clients, React hooks
and event buses.</p>
<h3 id="generics">2.1 Generics</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a type parameter, a placeholder filled
in at the call site, so one function or class works with many types
while keeping the link between input and output.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb43"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb43-1"><a href="#cb43-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Without generics: the caller loses the type</span></span>
<span id="cb43-2"><a href="#cb43-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">firstAny</span>(arr<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">any</span>[])<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">any</span> { <span class="cf">return</span> arr[<span class="dv">0</span>]<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb43-3"><a href="#cb43-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb43-4"><a href="#cb43-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// With generics: input type flows to output</span></span>
<span id="cb43-5"><a href="#cb43-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">first</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>(arr<span class="op">:</span> T[])<span class="op">:</span> T <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">undefined</span> { <span class="cf">return</span> arr[<span class="dv">0</span>]<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb43-6"><a href="#cb43-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> n <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">first</span>([<span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">2</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">3</span>])<span class="op">;</span>     <span class="co">// number | undefined, inferred</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Constraints</strong> (<code>extends</code>) say what the type
must at least have:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb44"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb44-1"><a href="#cb44-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">byId</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T <span class="kw">extends</span> { id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span> }<span class="op">&gt;</span>(items<span class="op">:</span> T[]<span class="op">,</span> id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>)<span class="op">:</span> T <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">undefined</span> {</span>
<span id="cb44-2"><a href="#cb44-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> items<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">find</span>((i) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> i<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span> <span class="op">===</span> id)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// allowed: T is guaranteed to have id</span></span>
<span id="cb44-3"><a href="#cb44-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Defaults</strong> cover the common case:
<code>interface ApiResponse&lt;T = unknown&gt; { data: T; meta?: PageMeta }</code>.</p>
<p><strong>A generic repository</strong> (the pattern behind TypeORM,
Prisma wrappers and most service layers):</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb45"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb45-1"><a href="#cb45-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">interface</span> Entity { id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span> }</span>
<span id="cb45-2"><a href="#cb45-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>

<span id="cb45-4"><a href="#cb45-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">findById</span>(id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">null</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb45-5"><a href="#cb45-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">findMany</span>(filter<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Partial</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T[]<span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb45-6"><a href="#cb45-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">create</span>(data<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Omit</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;id&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb45-7"><a href="#cb45-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">update</span>(id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> patch<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Partial</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="bu">Omit</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;id&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;&gt;</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb45-8"><a href="#cb45-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb45-9"><a href="#cb45-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb45-10"><a href="#cb45-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">class</span> MongoRepository<span class="op">&lt;</span>T <span class="kw">extends</span> Entity<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="kw">implements</span> Repository<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb45-11"><a href="#cb45-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">constructor</span>(<span class="kw">private</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> collection<span class="op">:</span> Collection<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>) {}</span>
<span id="cb45-12"><a href="#cb45-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="co">// ...</span></span>
<span id="cb45-13"><a href="#cb45-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>A generic typed fetch helper:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb46"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb46-1"><a href="#cb46-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">async</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">http</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>(url<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> init<span class="op">?:</span> RequestInit)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb46-2"><a href="#cb46-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> res <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="fu">fetch</span>(url<span class="op">,</span> init)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb46-3"><a href="#cb46-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span>res<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">ok</span>) <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">HttpError</span>(res<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">status</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="cf">await</span> res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">text</span>())<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb46-4"><a href="#cb46-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">json</span>() <span class="im">as</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;;</span> <span class="co">// a cast: the server is trusted, not verified</span></span>
<span id="cb46-5"><a href="#cb46-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb46-6"><a href="#cb46-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> user <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="fu">http</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>User<span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/api/users/1&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Call out the cast yourself. <code>http&lt;User&gt;</code> is a
promise you make, not a check; for external APIs, pass a Zod schema
instead and return <code>schema.parse(json)</code>.</p>
<p><strong>My rules for generics:</strong> name them meaningfully when
there’s more than one (<code>TInput</code>, <code>TOutput</code>); add a
constraint whenever you touch a property; if a type parameter appears
only once in the signature, you probably don’t need it.</p>
<h3 id="keyof-typeof-indexed-access">2.2 <code>keyof</code>,
<code>typeof</code>, indexed access</h3>
<p>The building blocks for deriving types instead of repeating them.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb47"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb47-1"><a href="#cb47-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">interface</span> User { id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> email<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> age<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span> }</span>
<span id="cb47-2"><a href="#cb47-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb47-3"><a href="#cb47-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> UserKey <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> User<span class="op">;</span>                <span class="co">// &#39;id&#39; | &#39;email&#39; | &#39;age&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb47-4"><a href="#cb47-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Email <span class="op">=</span> User[<span class="st">&#39;email&#39;</span>]<span class="op">;</span>               <span class="co">// string (indexed access)</span></span>
<span id="cb47-5"><a href="#cb47-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb47-6"><a href="#cb47-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">get</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">,</span> K <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T<span class="op">&gt;</span>(obj<span class="op">:</span> T<span class="op">,</span> key<span class="op">:</span> K)<span class="op">:</span> T[K] {</span>
<span id="cb47-7"><a href="#cb47-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> obj[key]<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb47-8"><a href="#cb47-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb47-9"><a href="#cb47-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">get</span>(user<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;age&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span>   <span class="co">// number</span></span>
<span id="cb47-10"><a href="#cb47-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">get</span>(user<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;name&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span>  <span class="co">// error: not a key of User</span></span>
<span id="cb47-11"><a href="#cb47-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb47-12"><a href="#cb47-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> config <span class="op">=</span> { port<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">3000</span><span class="op">,</span> env<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;prod&#39;</span> <span class="im">as</span> <span class="kw">const</span> }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb47-13"><a href="#cb47-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Config <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">typeof</span> config<span class="op">;</span>              <span class="co">// derive a type from a value</span></span>
<span id="cb47-14"><a href="#cb47-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb47-15"><a href="#cb47-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> ROLES <span class="op">=</span> [<span class="st">&#39;admin&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;editor&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;viewer&#39;</span>] <span class="im">as</span> <span class="kw">const</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb47-16"><a href="#cb47-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Role <span class="op">=</span> (<span class="kw">typeof</span> ROLES)[<span class="dt">number</span>]<span class="op">;</span>       <span class="co">// &#39;admin&#39; | &#39;editor&#39; | &#39;viewer&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>That last pattern is worth remembering: one array is the source of
truth for both runtime validation and the type.</p>

class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb48-1"><a href="#cb48-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">interface</span> UserEntity { id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> email<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> passwordHash<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> createdAt<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Date</span> }</span>
