<span id="cb48-4"><a href="#cb48-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> UpdateUserDto <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Partial</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="bu">Pick</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>UserEntity<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;email&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb48-5"><a href="#cb48-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> PublicUser <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Omit</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>UserEntity<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;passwordHash&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb48-6"><a href="#cb48-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb48-7"><a href="#cb48-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> permissions<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Record</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>Role<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dt">string</span>[]<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> {</span>
<span id="cb48-8"><a href="#cb48-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  admin<span class="op">:</span> [<span class="st">&#39;*&#39;</span>]<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb48-9"><a href="#cb48-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  editor<span class="op">:</span> [<span class="st">&#39;read&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;write&#39;</span>]<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb48-10"><a href="#cb48-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  viewer<span class="op">:</span> [<span class="st">&#39;read&#39;</span>]<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb48-11"><a href="#cb48-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// adding a new Role without updating this map is a compile error</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Trade-off:</strong> deriving DTOs from the entity keeps them
in sync, but couples your API contract to your database model. On larger
systems I keep API DTOs as their own types (often inferred from Zod
schemas) and map explicitly, so a column rename doesn’t silently change
a public API.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-2-1">How I’d answer — Hour 2</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Why use generics instead of <code>any</code>?</strong>
“Generics keep the relationship between input and output types.
<code>first&lt;T&gt;(arr: T[]): T</code> tells the caller they get back
what they put in; <code>any</code> throws that away and switches off
checking downstream.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. Write a typed <code>pluck</code> that returns one
property from each item.</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb49"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb49-1"><a href="#cb49-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">pluck</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">,</span> K <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T<span class="op">&gt;</span>(items<span class="op">:</span> T[]<span class="op">,</span> key<span class="op">:</span> K)<span class="op">:</span> T[K][] {</span>
<span id="cb49-2"><a href="#cb49-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> items<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">map</span>((i) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> i[key])<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb49-3"><a href="#cb49-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb49-4"><a href="#cb49-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">pluck</span>(users<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;email&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// string[]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>“<code>K extends keyof T</code> restricts the key to real properties,
and <code>T[K]</code> gives the exact property type back.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. <code>Omit</code> vs <code>Pick</code>, and how do you
type a PATCH endpoint?</strong> “<code>Pick</code> keeps listed keys,
<code>Omit</code> removes them. For PATCH I’d use
<code>Partial&lt;Pick&lt;Entity, 'allowed' | 'fields'&gt;&gt;</code>, so
clients can send any subset of an explicit allow-list and nothing else,
like <code>id</code> or <code>role</code>.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. How do you avoid duplicating a list of roles between
runtime code and types?</strong> “Define it once as a <code>const</code>
array with <code>as const</code> and derive the union with
<code>(typeof ROLES)[number]</code>. Validation uses the array, the type
uses the union, and they can’t drift.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-4">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Implement a generic
<code>Repository&lt;T&gt;</code> interface and an in-memory version for
tests</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write
<code>groupBy&lt;T, K extends PropertyKey&gt;(items: T[], fn: (t: T) =&gt; K): Record&lt;K, T[]&gt;</code></label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Define Create, Update and Public
DTOs for a <code>Product</code> entity using utility types</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-3-advanced-types">Hour 3 — Advanced types</h2>
<p>You won’t write conditional types every day, and you shouldn’t. But a
senior needs to read library types (Prisma, tRPC, React Hook Form are
full of them), write the occasional helper like
<code>DeepPartial</code>, and know when type cleverness is costing the
team more than it saves. Interviewers often ask for one of these helpers
on a whiteboard.</p>
<h3 id="mapped-types">3.1 Mapped types</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> build a new object type by looping over
the keys of another one. This is how <code>Partial</code>,
<code>Readonly</code> and <code>Record</code> are implemented.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb50"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb50-1"><a href="#cb50-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> MyPartial<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> { [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T]<span class="op">?:</span> T[K] }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb50-2"><a href="#cb50-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> MyReadonly<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> { <span class="kw">readonly</span> [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T]<span class="op">:</span> T[K] }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb50-3"><a href="#cb50-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Mutable<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> { <span class="op">-</span><span class="kw">readonly</span> [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T]<span class="op">:</span> T[K] }<span class="op">;</span>   <span class="co">// &#39;-&#39; removes a modifier</span></span>
<span id="cb50-4"><a href="#cb50-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Concrete<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> { [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T]<span class="op">-?:</span> T[K] }<span class="op">;</span>          <span class="co">// removes optional</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Key remapping with <code>as</code></strong> (TS 4.1+) renames
or filters keys:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb51"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb51-1"><a href="#cb51-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Getters<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> {</span>
<span id="cb51-2"><a href="#cb51-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T <span class="im">as</span> <span class="vs">`get</span><span class="sc">${</span>Capitalize<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">string</span> <span class="op">&amp;</span> K<span class="op">&gt;</span><span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span>]<span class="op">:</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> T[K]<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb51-3"><a href="#cb51-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb51-4"><a href="#cb51-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> UserGetters <span class="op">=</span> Getters<span class="op">&lt;</span>{ name<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> age<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span> }<span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb51-5"><a href="#cb51-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// { getName: () =&gt; string; getAge: () =&gt; number }</span></span>
<span id="cb51-6"><a href="#cb51-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb51-7"><a href="#cb51-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> OnlyStrings<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> { [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T <span class="im">as</span> T[K] <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">string</span> <span class="op">?</span> K <span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">never</span>]<span class="op">:</span> T[K] }<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="conditional-types-and-infer">3.2 Conditional types and
<code>infer</code></h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a type-level if/else:
<code>T extends U ? X : Y</code>.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb52"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb52-1"><a href="#cb52-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> IsString<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">string</span> <span class="op">?</span> true <span class="op">:</span> <span class="kw">false</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb52-2"><a href="#cb52-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb52-3"><a href="#cb52-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> ElementType<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> (<span class="kw">infer</span> <span class="cn">E</span>)[] <span class="op">?</span> E <span class="op">:</span> T<span class="op">;</span>   <span class="co">// infer captures part of a type</span></span>
<span id="cb52-4"><a href="#cb52-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> A <span class="op">=</span> ElementType<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">number</span>[]<span class="op">&gt;;</span>                        <span class="co">// number</span></span>
<span id="cb52-5"><a href="#cb52-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb52-6"><a href="#cb52-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> UnwrapPromise<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="kw">infer</span> V<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">?</span> UnwrapPromise<span class="op">&lt;</span>V<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">:</span> T<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb52-7"><a href="#cb52-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> B <span class="op">=</span> UnwrapPromise<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>User<span class="op">&gt;&gt;&gt;;</span>        <span class="co">// User (built-in: Awaited)</span></span>
<span id="cb52-8"><a href="#cb52-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb52-9"><a href="#cb52-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> FirstArg<span class="op">&lt;</span>F<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> F <span class="kw">extends</span> (first<span class="op">:</span> <span class="kw">infer</span> A<span class="op">,</span> <span class="op">...</span>rest<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">any</span>[]) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="dt">any</span> <span class="op">?</span> A <span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">never</span><span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Distribution gotcha (a favourite follow-up):</strong> a
conditional on a bare type parameter distributes over unions.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb53"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb53-1"><a href="#cb53-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> ToArray<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">any</span> <span class="op">?</span> T[] <span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">never</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb53-2"><a href="#cb53-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> C <span class="op">=</span> ToArray<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">string</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span>        <span class="co">// string[] | number[]  (distributed)</span></span>
<span id="cb53-3"><a href="#cb53-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb53-4"><a href="#cb53-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> ToArrayNoDist<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> [T] <span class="kw">extends</span> [<span class="dt">any</span>] <span class="op">?</span> T[] <span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">never</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb53-5"><a href="#cb53-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> D <span class="op">=</span> ToArrayNoDist<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">string</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span>  <span class="co">// (string | number)[]</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>That distribution is exactly how
<code>Exclude&lt;T, U&gt; = T extends U ? never : T</code> works.</p>
<h3 id="recursive-types-deeppartial-deepreadonly">3.3 Recursive types:
<code>DeepPartial</code>, <code>DeepReadonly</code></h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb54"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb54-1"><a href="#cb54-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> DeepPartial<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> (<span class="op">...</span>args<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">any</span>[]) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="dt">any</span></span>
<span id="cb54-2"><a href="#cb54-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">?</span> T                                           <span class="co">// leave functions alone</span></span>
<span id="cb54-3"><a href="#cb54-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">:</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">object</span></span>
<span id="cb54-4"><a href="#cb54-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="op">?</span> { [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T]<span class="op">?:</span> DeepPartial<span class="op">&lt;</span>T[K]<span class="op">&gt;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb54-5"><a href="#cb54-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="op">:</span> T<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb54-6"><a href="#cb54-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb54-7"><a href="#cb54-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> DeepReadonly<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> (<span class="op">...</span>args<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">any</span>[]) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="dt">any</span></span>
<span id="cb54-8"><a href="#cb54-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">?</span> T</span>
<span id="cb54-9"><a href="#cb54-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">:</span> T <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">object</span></span>
<span id="cb54-10"><a href="#cb54-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="op">?</span> { <span class="kw">readonly</span> [K <span class="kw">in</span> <span class="kw">keyof</span> T]<span class="op">:</span> DeepReadonly<span class="op">&lt;</span>T[K]<span class="op">&gt;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb54-11"><a href="#cb54-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="op">:</span> T<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb54-12"><a href="#cb54-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb54-13"><a href="#cb54-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> override<span class="op">:</span> DeepPartial<span class="op">&lt;</span>AppConfig<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> { db<span class="op">:</span> { pool<span class="op">:</span> { max<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">20</span> } } }<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// config overrides in tests</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Edge cases to mention: arrays and <code>Date</code> are objects too.
Production-grade versions special-case them; libraries like
<code>type-fest</code> already do, and I’d use it rather than maintain
my own.</p>
<h3 id="template-literal-types">3.4 Template literal types</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb55"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb55-1"><a href="#cb55-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> HttpMethod <span class="op">=</span> <span class="st">&#39;GET&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;POST&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;PUT&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;DELETE&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb55-2"><a href="#cb55-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Route <span class="op">=</span> <span class="vs">`/api/</span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="st">&#39;users&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;orders&#39;</span><span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb55-3"><a href="#cb55-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Endpoint <span class="op">=</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>HttpMethod<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> </span><span class="sc">${</span>Route<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span><span class="op">;</span>   <span class="co">// &#39;GET /api/users&#39; | &#39;POST /api/users&#39; | ...</span></span>
<span id="cb55-4"><a href="#cb55-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb55-5"><a href="#cb55-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> EventName<span class="op">&lt;</span>T <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>T<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">:created`</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>T<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">:updated`</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>T<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">:deleted`</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb55-6"><a href="#cb55-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> OrderEvent <span class="op">=</span> EventName<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="st">&#39;order&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span>       <span class="co">// &#39;order:created&#39; | &#39;order:updated&#39; | &#39;order:deleted&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb55-7"><a href="#cb55-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb55-8"><a href="#cb55-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Extract route params: &#39;/users/:id/orders/:orderId&#39; -&gt; &#39;id&#39; | &#39;orderId&#39;</span></span>
<span id="cb55-9"><a href="#cb55-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Params<span class="op">&lt;</span>S <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span></span>
<span id="cb55-10"><a href="#cb55-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  S <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>string<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">:</span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="kw">infer</span> P<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">/</span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="kw">infer</span> Rest<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span> <span class="op">?</span> P <span class="op">|</span> Params<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="vs">`/</span><span class="sc">${</span>Rest<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span><span class="op">&gt;</span></span>
<span id="cb55-11"><a href="#cb55-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="op">:</span> S <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>string<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">:</span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="kw">infer</span> P<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span> <span class="op">?</span> P <span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">never</span><span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>That <code>Params</code> type is roughly what Express and React
Router typings do to give you <code>req.params.id</code> with
autocomplete.</p>
<h3 id="as-const-and-satisfies">3.5 <code>as const</code> and
<code>satisfies</code></h3>
<ul>
<li><code>as const</code> makes literals as narrow as possible and
readonly: <code>['a', 'b'] as const</code> is
<code>readonly ['a', 'b']</code>, not <code>string[]</code>.</li>
<li><code>satisfies</code> (TS 4.9) checks a value against a type
<strong>without widening it</strong> to that type.</li>
</ul>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb56"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb56-1"><a href="#cb56-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Theme <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Record</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="st">&#39;primary&#39;</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="st">&#39;danger&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> string <span class="op">|</span> [number<span class="op">,</span> number<span class="op">,</span> number]<span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb56-2"><a href="#cb56-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb56-3"><a href="#cb56-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> a<span class="op">:</span> Theme <span class="op">=</span> { primary<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;#0af&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> danger<span class="op">:</span> [<span class="dv">255</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span>] }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb56-4"><a href="#cb56-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>a<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">primary</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">toUpperCase</span>()<span class="op">;</span>  <span class="co">// error: could be a tuple, annotation widened it</span></span>
<span id="cb56-5"><a href="#cb56-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb56-6"><a href="#cb56-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> b <span class="op">=</span> { primary<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;#0af&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> danger<span class="op">:</span> [<span class="dv">255</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">0</span>] } satisfies Theme<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb56-7"><a href="#cb56-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>b<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">primary</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">toUpperCase</span>()<span class="op">;</span>  <span class="co">// OK: still known to be a string</span></span>
<span id="cb56-8"><a href="#cb56-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>b<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">extra</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="st">&#39;x&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span>            <span class="co">// error anyway: checked against Theme</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>My default for config objects and route maps:
<code>as const satisfies Type</code>. You get validation and the exact
literal types.</p>
<h3 id="branded-types">3.6 Branded types</h3>
<p>Fix structural typing where a mix-up would be costly.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb57"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb57-1"><a href="#cb57-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Brand<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">,</span> B <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> T <span class="op">&amp;</span> { <span class="kw">readonly</span> __brand<span class="op">:</span> B }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb57-2"><a href="#cb57-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> UserId <span class="op">=</span> Brand<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;UserId&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb57-3"><a href="#cb57-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> OrderId <span class="op">=</span> Brand<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;OrderId&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span></span>
<span id="cb57-4"><a href="#cb57-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Paise <span class="op">=</span> Brand<span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;Paise&#39;</span><span class="op">&gt;;</span>          <span class="co">// money in minor units, never mixed with rupees</span></span>
<span id="cb57-5"><a href="#cb57-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb57-6"><a href="#cb57-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> toUserId <span class="op">=</span> (s<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> s <span class="im">as</span> UserId<span class="op">;</span>  <span class="co">// the only place a cast is allowed</span></span>
<span id="cb57-7"><a href="#cb57-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb57-8"><a href="#cb57-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">getOrder</span>(id<span class="op">:</span> OrderId) { <span class="co">/* ... */</span> }</span>
<span id="cb57-9"><a href="#cb57-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">getOrder</span>(<span class="fu">toUserId</span>(<span class="st">&#39;u1&#39;</span>))<span class="op">;</span>                     <span class="co">// compile error</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Zero runtime cost. I’d use it for IDs across service boundaries,
tenant IDs in multi-tenant systems, and money amounts.</p>
<h3 id="enums-vs-unions">3.7 Enums vs unions</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th><code>enum</code></th>
<th>String union / <code>as const</code> object</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Runtime output</td>
<td>Generates a JS object (numeric enums also reverse-map)</td>
<td>Union: nothing. Object: a plain object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Type safety</td>
<td>Numeric enums accept any number</td>
<td>Exact literals only</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Tree-shaking, <code>isolatedModules</code>, Babel/esbuild</td>
<td><code>const enum</code> breaks with isolated transpilers</td>
<td>Works everywhere</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Readability</td>
<td><code>Status.Active</code></td>
<td><code>'active'</code> or <code>Status.Active</code> (object)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb58"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb58-1"><a href="#cb58-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">const</span> OrderStatus <span class="op">=</span> {</span>
<span id="cb58-2"><a href="#cb58-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  Pending<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;pending&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb58-3"><a href="#cb58-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  Paid<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;paid&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb58-4"><a href="#cb58-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  Shipped<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;shipped&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb58-5"><a href="#cb58-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>} <span class="im">as</span> <span class="kw">const</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb58-6"><a href="#cb58-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export type</span> OrderStatus <span class="op">=</span> (<span class="kw">typeof</span> OrderStatus)[<span class="kw">keyof</span> <span class="kw">typeof</span> OrderStatus]<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// &#39;pending&#39; | &#39;paid&#39; | &#39;shipped&#39;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>My rule:</strong> string unions or <code>as const</code>
objects in new code. String enums are acceptable if a codebase or
framework (NestJS Swagger, some ORMs) already relies on them. Avoid
numeric enums and <code>const enum</code>.</p>
<h3 id="function-overloads">3.8 Function overloads</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb59"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb59-1"><a href="#cb59-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">parseDate</span>(input<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Date</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb59-2"><a href="#cb59-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">parseDate</span>(input<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Date</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb59-3"><a href="#cb59-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">parseDate</span>(input<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>[])<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Date</span>[]<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb59-4"><a href="#cb59-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">parseDate</span>(input<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">number</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">string</span>[])<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Date</span> <span class="op">|</span> <span class="bu">Date</span>[] {</span>
<span id="cb59-5"><a href="#cb59-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="bu">Array</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">isArray</span>(input) <span class="op">?</span> input<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">map</span>((s) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Date</span>(s)) <span class="op">:</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Date</span>(input)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb59-6"><a href="#cb59-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Use overloads when the return type depends on the argument type in
ways a union can’t express. Often a generic or a discriminated options
object is simpler.</p>
<h3 id="decorators">3.9 Decorators</h3>
<p><strong>What they are:</strong> functions applied to classes,
methods, properties or parameters at definition time, to attach metadata
or wrap behaviour.</p>
<p>Two versions exist, and knowing that is the senior detail:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Legacy / experimental decorators</strong>
(<code>experimentalDecorators: true</code>, plus
<code>emitDecoratorMetadata</code>): what <strong>NestJS</strong> and
<strong>Angular</strong> use today. Parameter decorators like
<code>@Inject()</code> and DI via <code>reflect-metadata</code> depend
on them.</li>
<li><strong>Standard ECMAScript decorators</strong> (TS 5.0+, no flag):
a different API, no parameter decorators, no metadata emission. Fine for
your own method wrappers in plain projects.</li>
</ul>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb60"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb60-1"><a href="#cb60-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Legacy style, as used with NestJS</span></span>
<span id="cb60-2"><a href="#cb60-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">LogTime</span>()<span class="op">:</span> MethodDecorator {</span>
<span id="cb60-3"><a href="#cb60-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> (_target<span class="op">,</span> key<span class="op">,</span> descriptor<span class="op">:</span> PropertyDescriptor) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb60-4"><a href="#cb60-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> original <span class="op">=</span> descriptor<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">value</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb60-5"><a href="#cb60-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    descriptor<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">value</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">async</span> <span class="kw">function</span> (<span class="op">...</span>args<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">unknown</span>[]) {</span>
<span id="cb60-6"><a href="#cb60-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="kw">const</span> start <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">performance</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">now</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb60-7"><a href="#cb60-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="cf">try</span> { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="cf">await</span> original<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">apply</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">,</span> args)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb60-8"><a href="#cb60-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="cf">finally</span> { <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">log</span>(<span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span><span class="bu">String</span>(key)<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> took </span><span class="sc">${</span>(<span class="bu">performance</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">now</span>() <span class="op">-</span> start)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">toFixed</span>(<span class="dv">1</span>)<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> ms`</span>)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb60-9"><a href="#cb60-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb60-10"><a href="#cb60-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb60-11"><a href="#cb60-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb60-12"><a href="#cb60-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb60-13"><a href="#cb60-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">class</span> ReportService {</span>
<span id="cb60-14"><a href="#cb60-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  @<span class="fu">LogTime</span>()</span>
<span id="cb60-15"><a href="#cb60-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">async</span> <span class="fu">generate</span>(month<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>) { <span class="co">/* ... */</span> }</span>
<span id="cb60-16"><a href="#cb60-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-3-1">How I’d answer — Hour 3</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Implement <code>DeepPartial&lt;T&gt;</code>.</strong>
Write the version in 3.3, then say: “It recurses into objects, leaves
functions alone, and stops at primitives. A production version also
handles arrays, Dates and Maps, which is why I’d normally take it from
<code>type-fest</code>.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. What does <code>infer</code> do?</strong> “It declares a
type variable inside a conditional type, captured from whatever matches
that position. <code>T extends Promise&lt;infer V&gt; ? V : T</code>
pulls out what a promise resolves to. Built-ins like
<code>ReturnType</code> and <code>Awaited</code> are written this
way.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. <code>satisfies</code> vs a type annotation?</strong> “An
annotation widens the value to the declared type, so you lose specifics.
<code>satisfies</code> checks against the type but keeps the inferred
literal types. I use <code>as const satisfies</code> for config, route
tables and permission maps.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. Enums or unions?</strong> “Unions or
<code>as const</code> objects in new code. Numeric enums accept any
number, <code>const enum</code> breaks with esbuild and isolated
modules, and unions emit nothing. I keep string enums only where a
framework expects them.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. When is advanced typing too much?</strong> “When the
types are harder to understand than the code they protect, error
messages become unreadable, or compile times grow. In application code I
keep types simple and readable; clever types belong in a few well-tested
shared helpers or in libraries.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-5">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write <code>DeepReadonly</code>,
<code>Mutable</code> and a <code>PickByValue&lt;T, V&gt;</code> mapped
type</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write
<code>Params&lt;'/users/:id/orders/:orderId'&gt;</code> and test it with
a type-level assertion</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Replace a numeric enum with an
<code>as const</code> object and a derived union</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write a <code>@Retry(3)</code>
method decorator for an async method</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-4-typescript-in-real-projects">Hour 4 — TypeScript in real
projects</h2>
<p>This hour is about decisions you’d own as a lead: compiler settings,
where validation lives, how types are shared across services and
frontends, and how to migrate a JavaScript codebase without stopping
feature work. Then a short practice round and the capstone task.</p>
<h3 id="tsconfig-settings-that-matter">4.1 tsconfig settings that
matter</h3>
<p><code>"strict": true</code> is the baseline. It turns on, among
others:</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Flag (part of <code>strict</code>)</th>
<th>Catches</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>strictNullChecks</code></td>
<td>Using a value that might be
<code>null</code>/<code>undefined</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>noImplicitAny</code></td>
<td>Parameters and variables silently typed <code>any</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>strictFunctionTypes</code></td>
<td>Unsafe function parameter assignments</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>useUnknownInCatchVariables</code></td>
<td><code>catch (e)</code> typed <code>unknown</code> instead of
<code>any</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>strictPropertyInitialization</code></td>
<td>Class fields never assigned in the constructor</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Worth adding on top, and worth mentioning in interviews:</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Flag</th>
<th>Why</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>noUncheckedIndexedAccess</code></td>
<td><code>arr[i]</code> and <code>record[key]</code> become
<code>T \| undefined</code>; catches a lot of real crashes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>exactOptionalPropertyTypes</code></td>
<td><code>{ a?: string }</code> no longer accepts an explicit
<code>undefined</code>; matters for PATCH semantics</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>noImplicitOverride</code></td>
<td>Requires <code>override</code> on overridden methods</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>noFallthroughCasesInSwitch</code></td>
<td>Missing <code>break</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>verbatimModuleSyntax</code></td>
<td>Makes type-only imports explicit; avoids ESM/CJS surprises</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Module settings for Node:</strong>
<code>"module": "NodeNext"</code> and
<code>"moduleResolution": "NodeNext"</code> for services run directly by
Node; <code>"moduleResolution": "Bundler"</code> for frontends built by
Vite or a bundler. Mixing these up is behind most “cannot find module”
and ESM/CJS errors.</p>
<p><strong>Build speed:</strong> in many teams, <code>tsc</code> only
type-checks (<code>--noEmit</code>) in CI and the editor, while esbuild,
swc or <code>tsx</code> do the actual transpiling, because they are far
faster. The trade-off: those tools strip types without checking them, so
CI must still run <code>tsc --noEmit</code>.</p>
<h3 id="validation-at-the-boundary-with-zod">4.2 Validation at the
boundary with Zod</h3>
<p>One schema gives you runtime validation and the static type, so they
can’t drift.</p>

<p>In NestJS the equivalent is DTO classes with
<code>class-validator</code> decorators and a global
<code>ValidationPipe</code> (<code>whitelist: true</code>,
<code>forbidNonWhitelisted: true</code>), or a Zod pipe. Either way, the
point is the same: the boundary rejects bad input before business code
sees it.</p>
<p>The same applies to config: parse <code>process.env</code> with a
schema at startup and crash immediately if something is missing, instead
of failing at 2 a.m. on the first request that needs it.</p>

<p>The generic order is
<code>Request&lt;Params, ResBody, ReqBody, Query&gt;</code>. Typing the
response body is underused; it stops you leaking internal fields like
<code>passwordHash</code> into responses.</p>
<h3 id="sharing-types-across-services-and-frontends">4.4 Sharing types
across services and frontends</h3>
<p>Options, roughly from simplest to most robust:</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Approach</th>
<th>Good</th>
<th>Watch out</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Shared <code>packages/types</code> in a monorepo</td>
<td>Simple, one source of truth, instant refactors</td>
<td>Couples deploys; frontend may import server-only types by
mistake</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Shared Zod schemas package</td>
<td>Types plus runtime validation on both sides</td>
<td>Zod becomes a dependency of every consumer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Generate from OpenAPI (<code>openapi-typescript</code>, Orval)</td>
<td>Works across languages and repos; API is the contract</td>
<td>Needs a generation step in CI</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>tRPC / GraphQL codegen</td>
<td>End-to-end types with no manual DTOs</td>
<td>Ties you to that stack</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>For the capstone: <code>packages/types</code> for shared domain types
and Zod schemas; for public APIs, generate clients from OpenAPI (Day 5).
Keep DTOs (what crosses the wire) separate from entities (what’s in the
database).</p>
<p>In a monorepo, use TypeScript <strong>project references</strong>
(<code>composite: true</code>, <code>references</code> in tsconfig) so
<code>tsc -b</code> builds packages in order and caches results, and set
the package’s <code>exports</code> field so consumers resolve the built
output.</p>
<h3 id="migrating-javascript-to-typescript">4.5 Migrating JavaScript to
TypeScript</h3>
<p>The approach that works on a live product:</p>
<ol type="1">
<li>Add <code>tsconfig</code> with <code>allowJs: true</code> and
<code>checkJs: false</code>; get the build and tests running
unchanged.</li>
<li>Turn on <code>strict</code> for new files only, or use
<code>// @ts-check</code> on files as you touch them.</li>
<li>Convert leaf modules first (utils, models), then services, then
routes; boundaries last.</li>
<li>Type the boundaries with Zod schemas early; that’s where most bugs
hide.</li>
<li>Allow <code>any</code> temporarily but track the count in CI and
make it go down, never up.</li>
<li>Turn on <code>strict</code> globally once the count is near
zero.</li>
</ol>
<p>The mistake to avoid: a big-bang rewrite branch that never
merges.</p>
<h3 id="practice-round-25-min">4.6 Practice round (25 min)</h3>
<p><strong>Typed EventEmitter.</strong> Interviewers like this because
it combines generics, <code>keyof</code> and indexed access.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb64"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb64-1"><a href="#cb64-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Listener<span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> (payload<span class="op">:</span> T) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="dt">void</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb64-2"><a href="#cb64-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>

<p>Points to say out loud: the event map is the single source of truth;
<code>on</code> returns an unsubscribe function, which is the
leak-prevention habit from Day 1; payload types follow the event name
automatically.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-4-1">How I’d answer — Hour 4</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Which compiler options do you enable on a new
project?</strong> “<code>strict</code>, plus
<code>noUncheckedIndexedAccess</code>, <code>noImplicitOverride</code>
and <code>verbatimModuleSyntax</code>, with <code>NodeNext</code> module
settings for services. Then <code>tsc --noEmit</code> in CI as a
required check, because our runtime builds use esbuild, which doesn’t
type-check.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. How do you share types between a Node API and a React
app?</strong> “In a monorepo, a shared package of Zod schemas and
inferred types, so both sides validate with the same rules. Across repos
or teams, the OpenAPI spec is the contract and clients are generated
from it in CI. Either way, I keep wire DTOs separate from database
entities.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How would you migrate a 200k-line JavaScript service to
TypeScript?</strong> “Incrementally. <code>allowJs</code> first so
nothing breaks, then convert leaf modules and type the boundaries with
schemas early. I’d track the number of <code>any</code>s and type errors
in CI and only allow it to decrease, then turn on full strict mode once
it’s close to zero. No big-bang branch.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. Our TypeScript build takes 6 minutes. What would you look
at?</strong> “Split type-checking from transpiling: esbuild or swc for
builds, <code>tsc --noEmit</code> in parallel. Use project references
with incremental builds so unchanged packages are skipped. Then look for
type-level hotspots with <code>tsc --extendedDiagnostics</code> and
<code>--generateTrace</code>; deeply recursive or huge union types are
common culprits.”</p>

<h1 id="day-3-wed-node.js-internals-interview-revision">Day 3 (Wed) —
Node.js internals, interview revision</h1>
<h2 id="hour-1-node-architecture-v8-libuv-the-thread-pool">Hour 1 — Node
architecture: V8, libuv, the thread pool</h2>
<p>Day 1 covered the event loop from the JavaScript side. Today goes one
layer down. With 8 years of Node behind you, the interview question
won’t be “what is the event loop”; it will be “why did our file uploads
slow down when bcrypt traffic went up?” Answering that needs this
hour.</p>
<h3 id="the-layers">1.1 The layers</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Layer</th>
<th>What it does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Your JS + Node’s JS core (<code>lib/</code>)</td>
<td><code>fs</code>, <code>http</code>, <code>crypto</code> APIs you
call</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Bindings (C++)</td>
<td>Bridge from JS calls to native code</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>V8</strong></td>
<td>Parses, compiles (Ignition interpreter, TurboFan optimising
compiler) and runs JS; owns the heap and garbage collector</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>libuv</strong></td>
<td>Cross-platform event loop, async I/O, timers, and a worker thread
pool</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>OS</td>
<td>epoll (Linux), kqueue (macOS), IOCP (Windows) for non-blocking
sockets</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>“Node is single-threaded” is only half true.</strong> Your
JavaScript runs on one thread. The Node process has several: the main
thread, V8’s background threads (GC, compilation), and libuv’s thread
pool.</p>
<h3 id="two-kinds-of-async-os-level-vs-thread-pool">1.2 Two kinds of
async: OS-level vs thread pool</h3>
<p>This distinction is the heart of the hour and what most candidates
miss.</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Work</th>
<th>How libuv does it</th>
<th>Limited by</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>TCP/HTTP sockets, DB connections, HTTP clients</td>
<td>OS non-blocking I/O (epoll/kqueue/IOCP); no thread per request</td>
<td>OS limits, file descriptors</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>File system (<code>fs.*</code> async)</td>
<td><strong>Thread pool</strong></td>
<td>Pool size</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>dns.lookup</code> (used by <code>http.get('host')</code> by
default)</td>
<td><strong>Thread pool</strong> (calls <code>getaddrinfo</code>)</td>
<td>Pool size</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Async <code>crypto</code>: <code>pbkdf2</code>, <code>scrypt</code>,
<code>randomBytes</code>, <code>generateKeyPair</code></td>
<td><strong>Thread pool</strong></td>
<td>Pool size</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>zlib</code> async compression</td>
<td><strong>Thread pool</strong></td>
<td>Pool size</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>dns.resolve*</code></td>
<td>c-ares, network-based, not the pool</td>
<td>Network</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>The thread pool defaults to 4 threads</strong>
(<code>UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE</code>, max 1024). It is shared by everything
in the table above.</p>
<p><strong>The incident this explains:</strong> a login endpoint hashes
passwords with async <code>bcrypt</code>/<code>scrypt</code>. Under a
login spike, all 4 pool threads are busy hashing. Now every
<code>fs.readFile</code>, every gzip and every <code>dns.lookup</code>
queues behind them. Static file serving, uploads and outbound HTTP calls
(which do a DNS lookup) all slow down, even though CPU on the main
thread looks fine.</p>
<p>Fixes, in order: tune hashing cost sensibly; raise
<code>UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE</code> (set it as an env var before the process
starts; roughly the number of cores, more if the work is I/O-bound like
fs); cache DNS or use an HTTP agent with keep-alive so lookups are rare;
move heavy hashing to a dedicated service or worker pool.</p>
<h3 id="what-v8-does-that-you-should-know">1.3 What V8 does that you
should know</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>JIT tiers:</strong> code starts interpreted (Ignition). Hot
functions get optimised by TurboFan using assumptions about types. If
those assumptions break (a function that always got numbers suddenly
gets a string), V8 <strong>deoptimises</strong> it. Keeping object
shapes consistent (same properties, same order, set in the constructor)
keeps hot paths fast.</li>
<li><strong>Hidden classes / shapes:</strong> objects with the same
property layout share a shape. Adding properties dynamically or
<code>delete obj.prop</code> creates new shapes and slows property
access. In hot loops, prefer setting a property to
<code>undefined</code> over <code>delete</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Heap and GC:</strong> covered in Hour 4.</li>
</ul>
<p>None of this matters for 95% of API code. It matters in hot paths:
serialisers, parsers, tight loops over large arrays.</p>
<h3 id="what-blocks-the-main-thread">1.4 What blocks the main
thread</h3>
<p>Everything below runs on the JS thread and stalls every request in
the process:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>*Sync</code> APIs: <code>fs.readFileSync</code>,
<code>crypto.pbkdf2Sync</code>, <code>zlib.gzipSync</code>,
<code>child_process.execSync</code></li>
<li><code>JSON.parse</code> / <code>JSON.stringify</code> on large
payloads (multi-MB)</li>
<li>Regexes with catastrophic backtracking on user input (ReDoS)</li>
<li>Large in-memory sorts, aggregations and report building</li>
<li>Template rendering of large pages, PDF/image generation
in-process</li>
</ul>
<p><code>*Sync</code> is fine at startup (loading config, certs) and in
CLI scripts. It is never fine in a request path.</p>
<p><strong>Measure it:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb65"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb65-1"><a href="#cb65-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> { monitorEventLoopDelay } <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:perf_hooks&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb65-2"><a href="#cb65-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> h <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">monitorEventLoopDelay</span>({ <span class="dt">resolution</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">20</span> })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb65-3"><a href="#cb65-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>h<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">enable</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb65-4"><a href="#cb65-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="pp">setInterval</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb65-5"><a href="#cb65-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  metrics<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">gauge</span>(<span class="st">&#39;event_loop_delay_p99_ms&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> h<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">percentile</span>(<span class="dv">99</span>) <span class="op">/</span> <span class="fl">1e6</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// ns -&gt; ms</span></span>
<span id="cb65-6"><a href="#cb65-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  h<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">reset</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb65-7"><a href="#cb65-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">10_000</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>A healthy API stays in low single-digit ms at p99. Sustained 100 ms+
means something is blocking; alert on it.</p>
<h3 id="startup-and-the-module-system">1.5 Startup and the module
system</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>CommonJS</strong> (<code>require</code>): synchronous, loads
and caches modules on first require (<code>require.cache</code>); the
same module object is returned on every later require, which is why
module-level state is a singleton.</li>
<li><strong>ES modules</strong> (<code>import</code>): asynchronous
loading, static analysis, top-level <code>await</code>, live bindings.
Node decides by <code>"type": "module"</code> in package.json or the
<code>.mjs</code>/<code>.cjs</code> extension.</li>
<li>Interop: ESM can import CJS; CJS can’t <code>require</code> ESM
synchronously in older versions (since Node 22.12,
<code>require(esm)</code> works by default for ES modules without
top-level await; those with it throw
<code>ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE</code>). Many “ERR_REQUIRE_ESM” errors
come from a dependency going ESM-only.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-1-2">How I’d answer — Hour 1</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Is Node single-threaded?</strong> “JavaScript execution
is single-threaded: one call stack, one event loop. The process isn’t.
libuv has a thread pool, four threads by default, for file system work,
DNS lookups, async crypto and compression. Network sockets don’t use the
pool; they use the OS’s non-blocking I/O. V8 also runs GC and
compilation on background threads.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. What runs in the libuv thread pool, and why should I
care?</strong> “fs operations, <code>dns.lookup</code>, async crypto
like pbkdf2 and scrypt, and zlib. It’s only four threads and they’re
shared, so heavy password hashing can starve file reads and DNS lookups
for outbound HTTP calls. I’d watch for that pattern and tune
<code>UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE</code>, use keep-alive agents, or move hashing
out.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. Uploads got slow during a login spike, but CPU on the
main thread looked normal. Why?</strong> “My first guess is thread pool
saturation. Login hashing fills the four pool threads, and file writes
for uploads queue behind it. I’d confirm by looking at pool-bound
operation latency versus event-loop delay; the loop delay would look
fine while fs latency jumps.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. What blocks the event loop in practice?</strong> “Sync
APIs in request paths, large JSON serialisation, bad regexes on user
input, and heavy in-process computation. I track event-loop delay at p99
as a standard metric and alert on it.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. How does <code>require</code> caching work?</strong> “The
first <code>require</code> executes the module and caches its
<code>module.exports</code> by resolved filename. Later requires return
the cached object. That’s why module-level variables act like
singletons, and why mutating an exported object is visible
everywhere.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-6">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Run 8 parallel
<code>crypto.pbkdf2</code> calls with <code>UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE</code> of
4, then 8; time both and explain the difference</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Add the event-loop delay metric
above to the capstone API skeleton</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write a ReDoS-vulnerable regex
(e.g. <code>/^(a+)+$/</code>), time it on a long input, then fix
it</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-2-streams-backpressure-buffers">Hour 2 — Streams,
backpressure, buffers</h2>
<p>Streams are how Node handles data bigger than memory: CSV imports,
report exports, file uploads to S3, proxying responses. Teams that skip
them end up with services that work fine in testing and run out of
memory on the first big customer file. Expect “how would you import a 5
GB CSV?” in some form.</p>
<h3 id="what-a-stream-is">2.1 What a stream is</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> an object that moves data in chunks over
time, instead of loading it all at once. Memory use stays roughly
constant regardless of total size.</p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Direction</th>
<th>Examples</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Readable</td>
<td>Source</td>
<td><code>fs.createReadStream</code>, HTTP request on the server, DB
cursor streams</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Writable</td>
<td>Sink</td>
<td><code>fs.createWriteStream</code>, HTTP response, S3 upload</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Duplex</td>
<td>Both, independent</td>
<td>TCP socket</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Transform</td>
<td>Both, output derived from input</td>
<td>gzip, CSV parser, encryption, line splitter</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>All streams are <code>EventEmitter</code>s. Key events:
<code>data</code>, <code>end</code>, <code>error</code>,
<code>finish</code>, <code>close</code>, <code>drain</code>.</p>
<h3 id="backpressure">2.2 Backpressure</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> the mechanism that stops a fast producer
from overwhelming a slow consumer. Without it, chunks pile up in memory
until the process dies.</p>
<p>How it works:</p>
<ul>
<li>Every stream has an internal buffer limited by
<code>highWaterMark</code> (64 KB for byte streams in recent Node
versions, 16 objects in object mode).</li>
<li><code>writable.write(chunk)</code> returns <code>false</code> when
the buffer is full. The producer should stop writing.</li>
<li>The writable emits <code>'drain'</code> when it’s ready again.</li>
</ul>
<p>The manual version, to show you understand it:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb66"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb66-1"><a href="#cb66-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">copy</span>(readable<span class="op">,</span> writable) {</span>
<span id="cb66-2"><a href="#cb66-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  readable<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">on</span>(<span class="st">&#39;data&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> (chunk) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb66-3"><a href="#cb66-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span>writable<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">write</span>(chunk)) {</span>
<span id="cb66-4"><a href="#cb66-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      readable<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">pause</span>()<span class="op">;</span>                          <span class="co">// stop the producer</span></span>
<span id="cb66-5"><a href="#cb66-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      writable<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">once</span>(<span class="st">&#39;drain&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> readable<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resume</span>())<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb66-6"><a href="#cb66-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    }</span>
<span id="cb66-7"><a href="#cb66-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb66-8"><a href="#cb66-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  readable<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">on</span>(<span class="st">&#39;end&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> writable<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">end</span>())<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb66-9"><a href="#cb66-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>The version you’d actually ship:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb67"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb67-1"><a href="#cb67-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> { pipeline } <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:stream/promises&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb67-2"><a href="#cb67-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> zlib <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:zlib&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb67-3"><a href="#cb67-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> fs <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:fs&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb67-4"><a href="#cb67-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb67-5"><a href="#cb67-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">await</span> <span class="fu">pipeline</span>(</span>
<span id="cb67-6"><a href="#cb67-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  fs<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">createReadStream</span>(<span class="st">&#39;orders.csv&#39;</span>)<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb67-7"><a href="#cb67-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  zlib<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">createGzip</span>()<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb67-8"><a href="#cb67-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  fs<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">createWriteStream</span>(<span class="st">&#39;orders.csv.gz&#39;</span>)<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb67-9"><a href="#cb67-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong><code>pipe</code> vs <code>pipeline</code>:</strong> both
handle backpressure. <code>pipe</code> does <strong>not</strong> forward
errors or destroy the other streams when one fails, which leaks file
descriptors and leaves half-written files. <code>pipeline</code>
destroys every stream on error and gives you one place to handle it. My
rule: always <code>pipeline</code>.</p>
<h3 id="async-iteration">2.3 Async iteration</h3>
<p>Readable streams are async iterables, which is often the clearest way
to process records with natural backpressure:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb68"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb68-1"><a href="#cb68-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> readline <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:readline&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb68-2"><a href="#cb68-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb68-3"><a href="#cb68-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> rl <span class="op">=</span> readline<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">createInterface</span>({ <span class="dt">input</span><span class="op">:</span> fs<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">createReadStream</span>(<span class="st">&#39;users.csv&#39;</span>) })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb68-4"><a href="#cb68-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">for</span> <span class="cf">await</span> (<span class="kw">const</span> line <span class="kw">of</span> rl) {</span>
<span id="cb68-5"><a href="#cb68-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="fu">processLine</span>(line)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// the next line isn&#39;t read until this resolves</span></span>
<span id="cb68-6"><a href="#cb68-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>

<span id="cb69-40"><a href="#cb69-40" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">parse</span>({ <span class="dt">columns</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="kw">true</span> })<span class="op">,</span></span>

<p>Why each choice: upsert by a natural key makes re-runs safe
(idempotent); <code>ordered: false</code> lets one bad document not stop
the batch; batch size balances round trips against memory. In a real
system this runs as a background job (queue + worker), not inside an
HTTP request, and the API returns a job ID the client polls.</p>
<h3 id="streaming-http-responses">2.5 Streaming HTTP responses</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb70"><pre

<span id="cb70-12"><a href="#cb70-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
