<p>The last line is a detail interviewers like: once streaming has
started, the status code is already sent, so you can only abort the
connection.</p>
<h3 id="buffers">2.6 Buffers</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a fixed-size chunk of raw bytes,
allocated outside the V8 heap. Byte streams emit Buffers.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Buffer.from('héllo', 'utf8')</code>,
<code>buf.toString('base64')</code>,
<code>Buffer.concat([a, b])</code>.</li>
<li><code>Buffer.alloc(n)</code> is zero-filled;
<code>Buffer.allocUnsafe(n)</code> is faster but may contain old memory.
Never send an <code>allocUnsafe</code> buffer before filling it
completely.</li>
<li>Watch out for splitting multi-byte UTF-8 characters across chunk
boundaries; use <code>setEncoding('utf8')</code> or
<code>string_decoder</code> rather than calling <code>toString()</code>
on each chunk.</li>
<li>Buffers count toward process memory (RSS), not the JS heap, so a
leak of Buffers shows as RSS growing while heap looks flat.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-2-2">How I’d answer — Hour 2</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. How would you import a 5 GB CSV into a database?</strong>
“Never load it into memory. Run it as a background job, stream the file
through a CSV parser and a validation transform into a writable that
batches upserts of about a thousand rows. Backpressure keeps memory
flat. Upserts on a natural key make retries safe, invalid rows go to an
error report, and the job publishes progress so the UI can poll it.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. What is backpressure?</strong> “A slow consumer
signalling a fast producer to wait. In Node, <code>write()</code>
returns false when the writable’s buffer passes
<code>highWaterMark</code>; the producer pauses until
<code>drain</code>. <code>pipeline</code> and async iteration handle it
for you. Ignoring it is how services run out of memory on large
uploads.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. <code>pipe</code> vs <code>pipeline</code>?</strong>
“Both manage backpressure, but <code>pipe</code> doesn’t propagate
errors or clean up the other streams, so a failure can leak file handles
and leave partial output. <code>pipeline</code> destroys everything on
error and gives a single promise or callback to handle it. I use
<code>pipeline</code> everywhere.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. An error happens halfway through streaming a CSV
response. What does the client see?</strong> “Headers and a 200 are
already sent, so I can’t change the status. The right move is to destroy
the response so the client sees an aborted download rather than a
silently truncated file, log the error, and for important exports
generate the file asynchronously and give a download link instead.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-7">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Stream a 2 GB file through gzip with
<code>pipeline</code>; watch memory stay flat
(<code>process.memoryUsage().rss</code>)</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Do the same with
<code>readFile</code> and <code>gzipSync</code> and compare memory and
event-loop delay</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Build the CSV-to-Mongo importer
above for the capstone’s product catalog</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-3-cluster-worker_threads-child_process">Hour 3 — cluster,
worker_threads, child_process</h2>
<p>The question behind this hour is always “how do you use more than one
core, and how do you handle CPU-heavy work in Node?” The senior answer
depends on where the service runs: on a VM, inside Kubernetes, or as a
background worker. Interviewers like it when you bring that context up
yourself.</p>
<h3 id="the-three-options">3.1 The three options</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th><code>cluster</code></th>
<th><code>worker_threads</code></th>
<th><code>child_process</code></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>What it creates</td>
<td>Separate Node processes sharing a server port</td>
<td>Threads inside one process, each with its own V8 isolate and event
loop</td>
<td>Any separate OS process (Node or not)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Memory</td>
<td>Separate heaps, full process each</td>
<td>Separate JS heaps, can share memory via
<code>SharedArrayBuffer</code></td>
<td>Fully separate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Communication</td>
<td>IPC messages</td>
<td><code>postMessage</code> (structured clone), transferable objects,
shared memory</td>
<td>stdin/stdout/stderr streams, or IPC with <code>fork</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Crash isolation</td>
<td>One worker dies, others keep serving</td>
<td>An uncaught error kills only that worker thread (if handled)</td>
<td>Full isolation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Best for</td>
<td>Using all cores for an HTTP server on a single machine</td>
<td>CPU-heavy JS work: hashing, image processing, parsing,
compression</td>
<td>Running external tools (ffmpeg, ImageMagick, Python scripts,
git)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h3 id="cluster">3.2 cluster</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a primary process forks N worker
processes; incoming connections on the shared port are distributed
between them (round-robin by the primary on Linux by default).</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb71"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb71-1"><a href="#cb71-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> cluster <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:cluster&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb71-2"><a href="#cb71-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> os <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:os&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb71-3"><a href="#cb71-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb71-4"><a href="#cb71-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> (cluster<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">isPrimary</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb71-5"><a href="#cb71-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">for</span> (<span class="kw">let</span> i <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span> i <span class="op">&lt;</span> os<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">availableParallelism</span>()<span class="op">;</span> i<span class="op">++</span>) cluster<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">fork</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb71-6"><a href="#cb71-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  cluster<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">on</span>(<span class="st">&#39;exit&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> (worker<span class="op">,</span> code) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb71-7"><a href="#cb71-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">console</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">error</span>(<span class="vs">`worker </span><span class="sc">${</span>worker<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">process</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">pid</span><span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> died (</span><span class="sc">${</span>code<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">), restarting`</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb71-8"><a href="#cb71-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    cluster<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">fork</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb71-9"><a href="#cb71-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb71-10"><a href="#cb71-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>} <span class="cf">else</span> {</span>
<span id="cb71-11"><a href="#cb71-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;./server&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// each worker runs the full app</span></span>
<span id="cb71-12"><a href="#cb71-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Consequences people forget:</strong> each worker has its own
memory, so in-memory caches, sessions, rate-limit counters and WebSocket
connection maps are <strong>not shared</strong>. Anything that must be
shared goes to Redis. Sticky sessions are needed for WebSocket/socket.io
long-polling fallbacks.</p>
<p><strong>PM2</strong> wraps the same idea
(<code>pm2 start app.js -i max</code>) with restarts, zero-downtime
reloads and log handling. Common on VMs.</p>
<p><strong>In Kubernetes, my rule:</strong> don’t use cluster or PM2
cluster mode. Run one Node process per container, give the pod about one
CPU, and let the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler add pods. The orchestrator
already does restarts, load balancing and health checks; adding a
process manager inside the container hides crashes from it and makes
memory limits harder to reason about.</p>
<h3 id="worker_threads">3.3 worker_threads</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> real threads running separate JS
instances in the same process. Use them so CPU-bound work doesn’t block
the main event loop.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb72"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb72-1"><a href="#cb72-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// hash-worker.js</span></span>
<span id="cb72-2"><a href="#cb72-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> { parentPort } <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:worker_threads&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb72-3"><a href="#cb72-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> crypto <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:crypto&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb72-4"><a href="#cb72-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>parentPort<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">on</span>(<span class="st">&#39;message&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> ({ id<span class="op">,</span> data }) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb72-5"><a href="#cb72-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> digest <span class="op">=</span> crypto<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">createHash</span>(<span class="st">&#39;sha256&#39;</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">update</span>(data)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">digest</span>(<span class="st">&#39;hex&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// pretend this is heavy</span></span>
<span id="cb72-6"><a href="#cb72-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  parentPort<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">postMessage</span>({ id<span class="op">,</span> digest })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb72-7"><a href="#cb72-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Creating a worker per request is expensive (tens of milliseconds and
several MB each). In production, use a <strong>pool</strong>. Piscina is
the standard library for this:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb73"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb73-1"><a href="#cb73-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> Piscina <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;piscina&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb73-2"><a href="#cb73-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> pool <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">Piscina</span>({</span>
<span id="cb73-3"><a href="#cb73-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">filename</span><span class="op">:</span> require<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resolve</span>(<span class="st">&#39;./resize-worker.js&#39;</span>)<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb73-4"><a href="#cb73-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">maxThreads</span><span class="op">:</span> os<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">availableParallelism</span>() <span class="op">-</span> <span class="dv">1</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="co">// leave a core for the event loop</span></span>
<span id="cb73-5"><a href="#cb73-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">maxQueue</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">1000</span><span class="op">,</span>                             <span class="co">// reject instead of queuing forever</span></span>
<span id="cb73-6"><a href="#cb73-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb73-7"><a href="#cb73-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb73-8"><a href="#cb73-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">post</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/images/resize&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">async</span> (req<span class="op">,</span> res) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb73-9"><a href="#cb73-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> out <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> pool<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">run</span>({ <span class="dt">buffer</span><span class="op">:</span> req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">body</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dt">width</span><span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">800</span> })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb73-10"><a href="#cb73-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">type</span>(<span class="st">&#39;image/webp&#39;</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">send</span>(out)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb73-11"><a href="#cb73-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Passing data:</strong> <code>postMessage</code> copies data
with the structured clone algorithm, which costs time for large objects.
Transfer an <code>ArrayBuffer</code> instead
(<code>postMessage(buf, [buf])</code>) to move ownership without
copying. <code>SharedArrayBuffer</code> with <code>Atomics</code> allows
true shared memory, but you rarely need it in application code.</p>
<p><strong>When not to use worker threads:</strong> for I/O. Database
calls and HTTP requests are already non-blocking; moving them to a
thread adds overhead and gains nothing.</p>
<h3 id="child_process">3.4 child_process</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Function</th>
<th>Use</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>spawn(cmd, args)</code></td>
<td>Stream output of a long-running command (ffmpeg, large exports)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>execFile(file, args)</code></td>
<td>Run a binary and get buffered output; no shell</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>exec(cmdString)</code></td>
<td>Runs through a shell, buffers output</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>fork(modulePath)</code></td>
<td>Spawn a Node process with an IPC channel</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Security point to raise yourself:</strong> never build an
<code>exec</code> command string from user input; it runs through a
shell, so <code>file.jpg; rm -rf /</code> becomes command injection. Use
<code>spawn</code> or <code>execFile</code> with an argument array.
Also, <code>exec</code> buffers all output in memory
(<code>maxBuffer</code>), so large outputs either fail or eat memory;
use <code>spawn</code> and stream instead.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb74"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb74-1"><a href="#cb74-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> { spawn } <span class="op">=</span> <span class="pp">require</span>(<span class="st">&#39;node:child_process&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb74-2"><a href="#cb74-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> ff <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">spawn</span>(<span class="st">&#39;ffmpeg&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> [<span class="st">&#39;-i&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> inputPath<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;-vf&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;scale=640:-1&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> outputPath])<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// args array, no shell</span></span>
<span id="cb74-3"><a href="#cb74-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>ff<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">stderr</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">on</span>(<span class="st">&#39;data&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> (d) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> logger<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">debug</span>(d<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">toString</span>()))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb74-4"><a href="#cb74-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>ff<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">on</span>(<span class="st">&#39;close&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> (code) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> code <span class="op">===</span> <span class="dv">0</span> <span class="op">?</span> <span class="fu">resolve</span>() <span class="op">:</span> <span class="fu">reject</span>(<span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Error</span>(<span class="vs">`ffmpeg exited </span><span class="sc">${</span>code<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs">`</span>)))<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="choosing-as-an-architect">3.5 Choosing, as an architect</h3>
<p>For CPU-heavy work, the most scalable answer is often <strong>none of
the above inside the API</strong>: put the job on a queue (RabbitMQ,
SQS, BullMQ on Redis) and let separate worker services process it. The
API stays fast and responsive, workers scale independently, and failed
jobs can retry. Use worker threads when the result is needed
synchronously in the request and the work is short (tens to a few
hundred milliseconds).</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-3-2">How I’d answer — Hour 3</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. cluster vs worker_threads vs child_process?</strong>
“cluster runs multiple copies of the server as separate processes so one
machine’s cores all serve HTTP. worker_threads run CPU-heavy JavaScript
off the main thread inside one process. child_process runs external
programs. In Kubernetes I skip cluster and scale pods instead, and use a
worker pool like Piscina for CPU work in the request path.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. We need to generate thumbnails on upload. How?</strong>
“Upload the original straight to object storage, return immediately, and
publish an ‘image uploaded’ event. A separate worker service consumes it
and generates thumbnails, using a worker-thread pool or sharp, which
already uses native threads. That keeps the API fast and lets thumbnail
capacity scale on its own.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. What breaks when you move an app from one process to
cluster mode?</strong> “Anything stored in process memory: caches,
sessions, rate-limit counters, scheduled jobs that now run N times,
WebSocket connection maps. I’d move shared state to Redis, use a
distributed lock or a single scheduler for cron jobs, and enable sticky
sessions for WebSockets.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. Why is <code>exec</code> with user input
dangerous?</strong> “It runs the string through a shell, so special
characters let a user run arbitrary commands. Use <code>execFile</code>
or <code>spawn</code> with an argument array, validate inputs against an
allow-list, and never pass raw user strings to a shell.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-8">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Compute a slow Fibonacci in a route
handler; measure latency of a second endpoint while it runs</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Move the work to a Piscina pool;
measure again</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write a <code>spawn</code>-based
wrapper that streams a command’s output to a log and rejects on a
non-zero exit code</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-4-memory-gc-leaks-profiling">Hour 4 — Memory, GC, leaks,
profiling</h2>
<p>This is the hour that turns “I know Node” into “I’ve run Node in
production”. A good answer here walks through an investigation: the
symptom, the metric that confirms it, the tool that finds it, and the
fix plus prevention. Practise telling it as a story.</p>
<h3 id="how-v8-manages-memory">4.1 How V8 manages memory</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Area</th>
<th>Holds</th>
<th>Collected by</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>New space</strong> (young generation)</td>
<td>Newly created objects; small (a few MB to tens of MB)</td>
<td><strong>Scavenge</strong>: fast, frequent, copies survivors</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Old space</strong> (old generation)</td>
<td>Objects that survived a couple of scavenges</td>
<td><strong>Mark-sweep-compact</strong>: slower, mostly
concurrent/incremental, occasional pauses</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Large object space</td>
<td>Objects too big for normal pages</td>
<td>With old space</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Code space</td>
<td>Compiled code</td>
<td>—</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Outside the heap</td>
<td>Buffers, native addon memory</td>
<td>Freed when their JS handles are collected</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Generational hypothesis:</strong> most objects die young
(request-scoped objects, temporary arrays). That’s why the cheap
young-generation GC handles most garbage, and why long-lived caches cost
more: they get promoted to old space and make major GCs slower.</p>
<p><strong>What you see in
<code>process.memoryUsage()</code>:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>heapUsed</code> / <code>heapTotal</code>: the JS heap</li>
<li><code>rss</code>: total process memory (heap + Buffers + native +
code); what the container limit is measured against</li>
<li><code>external</code> / <code>arrayBuffers</code>: memory for
Buffers and ArrayBuffers</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="heap-limits-in-containers">4.2 Heap limits in containers</h3>
<p>The old-space limit is set by V8 at startup
(<code>--max-old-space-size</code>, in MB). Recent Node versions derive
a default from available memory, but in containers I set it explicitly,
around 70–75% of the container memory limit, leaving room for Buffers,
native memory and the rest of RSS.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb75"><pre
class="sourceCode dockerfile"><code class="sourceCode dockerfile"><span id="cb75-1"><a href="#cb75-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co"># for a 2 GiB container limit (Dockerfile comments must be on their own line)</span></span>
<span id="cb75-2"><a href="#cb75-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">ENV</span> NODE_OPTIONS=<span class="st">&quot;--max-old-space-size=1536&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Two different failures to tell apart:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>“JavaScript heap out of memory”</strong> crash in the logs:
the V8 heap limit was hit. Heap leak, or the limit is too low for the
workload.</li>
<li><strong>Pod killed with OOMKilled, no Node error:</strong> the
container’s RSS passed its limit. Often Buffers or native memory, or the
heap limit set higher than the container allows.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="common-leaks">4.3 Common leaks</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Leak</th>
<th>Typical code</th>
<th>Fix</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Unbounded in-memory cache</td>
<td><code>const cache = {}</code> keyed by user or URL</td>
<td>LRU with max size and TTL (<code>lru-cache</code>), or Redis</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Listeners added per request</td>
<td><code>emitter.on('x', ...)</code> inside a handler</td>
<td>Add once, or remove in cleanup; watch for
<code>MaxListenersExceededWarning</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Timers never cleared</td>
<td><code>setInterval</code> per connection</td>
<td><code>clearInterval</code> on close</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Closures capturing big objects</td>
<td>Callbacks stored long-term referencing request data</td>
<td>Capture only what’s needed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Global arrays used as queues/logs</td>
<td><code>failedJobs.push(job)</code> forever</td>
<td>Bounded buffer, or send to a real store</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Promises that never settle</td>
<td>Awaiting something that never resolves, holding its scope</td>
<td>Timeouts on every external call</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Module-level <code>Map</code> keyed by object</td>
<td>Strong references keep keys alive</td>
<td><code>WeakMap</code> when keys are objects</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><code>MaxListenersExceededWarning</code> (more than 10 listeners on
one event) is often the first visible sign of a listener leak. Don’t
silence it by raising the limit; find out who is adding listeners.</p>
<h3 id="investigating-a-leak-in-production">4.4 Investigating a leak in
production</h3>
<ol type="1">
<li><strong>Confirm:</strong> heap used (after GC) climbs steadily under
steady traffic and never returns to a baseline; restarts fix it
temporarily. Spiky memory that returns down is just load, not a
leak.</li>
<li><strong>Reproduce</strong> in staging with a load test (autocannon,
k6) against the suspected endpoint.</li>
<li><strong>Capture heap snapshots:</strong> <code>node --inspect</code>
+ Chrome DevTools → Memory, or <code>v8.writeHeapSnapshot()</code>
triggered by a signal or admin endpoint, or
<code>--heapsnapshot-signal=SIGUSR2</code>. Take one, run load, take a
second and a third.</li>
<li><strong>Compare snapshots:</strong> in DevTools use the Comparison
view; sort by size delta; look at what keeps growing (often
<code>(string)</code>, <code>Object</code>, closures or your own class
names).</li>
<li><strong>Follow retainers:</strong> the Retainers panel shows the
chain from the leaked object to a GC root, which points at the global
cache, listener or timer holding it.</li>
<li><strong>Fix and prove:</strong> apply the fix, rerun the load test,
confirm heap now plateaus.</li>
<li><strong>Prevent:</strong> add a heap-used and RSS dashboard with
alerts, and a load test to the pipeline for critical services.</li>
</ol>
<p>Caution: writing a heap snapshot pauses the process and needs roughly
as much memory again as the heap. Take snapshots on a single instance
pulled out of the load balancer, not on every pod at once.</p>
<h3 id="cpu-profiling-and-diagnostics-tools">4.5 CPU profiling and
diagnostics tools</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Tool</th>
<th>Use it for</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>

</tr>

<tr>

<tr>
<td>APM (Datadog, New Relic, Elastic, OpenTelemetry)</td>
<td>Per-endpoint latency, traces, event-loop and GC metrics continuously

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>diagnostics_channel</code>, <code>async_hooks</code> /
<code>AsyncLocalStorage</code></td>
<td>Request context (request IDs) through async calls</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Reading a flame graph:</strong> width is time spent. Look for
wide plateaus near the top that belong to your code (or a library you
call): that’s the hot path.</p>
<h3 id="graceful-shutdown-production-habit-that-belongs-here">4.6
Graceful shutdown (production habit that belongs here)</h3>
<p>On a deploy, Kubernetes sends SIGTERM, waits
<code>terminationGracePeriodSeconds</code> (30 s by default), then
SIGKILL. Without handling it, in-flight requests get cut off.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb76"><pre
class="sourceCode js"><code class="sourceCode javascript"><span id="cb76-1"><a href="#cb76-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">let</span> shuttingDown <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">false</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb76-2"><a href="#cb76-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/health/ready&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> (req<span class="op">,</span> res) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">status</span>(shuttingDown <span class="op">?</span> <span class="dv">503</span> <span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">200</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">end</span>())<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb76-3"><a href="#cb76-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb76-4"><a href="#cb76-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="bu">process</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">on</span>(<span class="st">&#39;SIGTERM&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">async</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb76-5"><a href="#cb76-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  shuttingDown <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">true</span><span class="op">;</span>                 <span class="co">// readiness fails, so no new traffic is routed here</span></span>
<span id="cb76-6"><a href="#cb76-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  server<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">close</span>(<span class="kw">async</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {           <span class="co">// stop accepting, finish in-flight requests</span></span>
<span id="cb76-7"><a href="#cb76-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">allSettled</span>([db<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">close</span>()<span class="op">,</span> redis<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">quit</span>()<span class="op">,</span> consumer<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">disconnect</span>()])<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb76-8"><a href="#cb76-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="bu">process</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">exit</span>(<span class="dv">0</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb76-9"><a href="#cb76-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb76-10"><a href="#cb76-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">process</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">exit</span>(<span class="dv">1</span>)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">25_000</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">unref</span>()<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// hard stop before SIGKILL</span></span>
<span id="cb76-11"><a href="#cb76-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Also close idle keep-alive connections
(<code>server.closeIdleConnections()</code> in Node 18.2+) or shutdown
can hang until timeouts expire.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-4-2">How I’d answer — Hour 4</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Tell me how you’d find a memory leak in a Node
service.</strong> “First confirm it’s a leak: heap after GC rising under
steady load, not just traffic spikes. Then reproduce in staging with a
load test, take heap snapshots a few minutes apart, and compare them to
see which objects keep growing. The retainer chain usually points
straight at the culprit: an unbounded cache, listeners added per
request, or uncleared timers. After the fix, I rerun the load test to
confirm the heap plateaus, and add heap metrics and alerts so we catch
it early next time.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. OOMKilled vs ‘heap out of memory’, what’s the
difference?</strong> “The first is the container exceeding its memory
limit, measured on RSS, so it includes Buffers and native memory. The
second is V8 hitting its own heap limit. I set
<code>--max-old-space-size</code> to about 75% of the container limit so
V8 collects before the container kills it, and I look at heap versus RSS
to see which side is growing.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How does garbage collection work in V8?</strong>
“Generational. New objects go to a small young space that’s collected
often with a fast copying scavenger; most objects die there. Survivors
are promoted to old space, collected by mark-sweep-compact, mostly
concurrently, with short pauses. Practically: avoid keeping lots of
medium-lived objects around, because promotion makes major GCs more
expensive.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. How do you handle shutdown in Kubernetes?</strong> “On
SIGTERM, fail the readiness probe, stop accepting new connections, let
in-flight requests finish, close DB, Redis and message consumers, then
exit. A hard timeout below the grace period guarantees we exit cleanly
before SIGKILL.”</p>

<h1 id="day-4-thu-node-architecture-security-machine-coding">Day 4 (Thu)
— Node architecture, security, machine coding</h1>
<h2 id="hour-1-api-architecture">Hour 1 — API architecture</h2>
<p>At principal level the question shifts from “can you build an
endpoint” to “how do you structure a service so 10 engineers can work in
it for three years without it rotting?” Have a clear default structure,
know why each layer exists, and be honest about when the structure is
overkill.</p>
<h3 id="layered-structure">1.1 Layered structure</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Layer</th>
<th>Responsibility</th>
<th>Knows about</th>
<th>Must not know about</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Routes / controllers</td>
<td>HTTP: parse, validate, call service, map to response and status
code</td>
<td>Request/response, DTOs</td>
<td>Database, SQL, Mongo queries</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Services (use cases)</td>
<td>Business rules, orchestration, transactions</td>
<td>Domain types, repository interfaces</td>
<td>HTTP, <code>req</code>/<code>res</code>, Express</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Repositories</td>
<td>Data access, queries, mapping rows to domain objects</td>
<td>ORM / driver</td>
<td>HTTP, business rules</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Domain</td>
<td>Entities, value objects, invariants</td>
<td>Nothing external</td>
<td>Frameworks</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Infrastructure</td>
<td>DB clients, message brokers, external APIs, config</td>
<td>Libraries</td>
<td>Business rules</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<pre class="text"><code>src/
  modules/
    orders/
      order.controller.ts
      order.service.ts
      order.repository.ts
      order.schemas.ts      # Zod DTOs
      order.types.ts
      order.service.test.ts
    users/ ...
  shared/ (errors, logger, middleware, config)
  app.ts   # builds the app, wires dependencies
  server.ts # starts listening, handles signals</code></pre>
<p><strong>Group by feature (module), not by technical type.</strong>
<code>controllers/</code>, <code>services/</code>, <code>models/</code>
folders at the top level force every change to touch five directories
and hide module boundaries. Feature folders make it obvious what belongs
together and make a later split into microservices much easier.</p>
<p><strong>Hexagonal / clean architecture</strong> takes this further:
the service depends only on interfaces (“ports”); infrastructure
provides “adapters”. The payoff is testability (swap the DB for an
in-memory fake) and freedom to change infrastructure. The cost is more
files and indirection. <strong>My rule:</strong> layered with feature
modules by default; full hexagonal only for complex domains with real
business rules (payments, loyalty, pricing). A CRUD admin service
doesn’t need it.</p>
<h3 id="dependency-injection">1.2 Dependency injection</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a class receives its collaborators
instead of creating or importing them, so they can be swapped in tests
or per environment.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb78"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb78-1"><a href="#cb78-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">class</span> OrderService {</span>

<span id="cb78-4"><a href="#cb78-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">private</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> payments<span class="op">:</span> PaymentGateway<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb78-5"><a href="#cb78-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">private</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> events<span class="op">:</span> EventPublisher<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb78-6"><a href="#cb78-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  ) {}</span>
<span id="cb78-7"><a href="#cb78-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb78-8"><a href="#cb78-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">async</span> <span class="fu">place</span>(input<span class="op">:</span> CreateOrderInput)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>Order<span class="op">&gt;</span> {</span>

<span id="cb78-12"><a href="#cb78-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">return</span> order<span class="op">;</span></span>

<span id="cb78-15"><a href="#cb78-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb78-16"><a href="#cb78-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// composition root (app.ts) — the only place that knows concrete classes</span></span>
<span id="cb78-17"><a href="#cb78-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> service <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">OrderService</span>(<span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">MongoOrderRepository</span>(db)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">RazorpayGateway</span>(cfg)<span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">KafkaPublisher</span>(producer))<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>In Express, a simple composition root like this is enough. NestJS and
Angular have a DI container that does it via decorators. Either way, the
benefit to name in interviews: unit tests pass fakes and run in
milliseconds without a database.</p>
<h3 id="express-vs-nestjs-vs-fastify">1.3 Express vs NestJS vs
Fastify</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>Express</th>
<th>NestJS</th>
<th>Fastify</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Style</td>
<td>Minimal, unopinionated</td>
<td>Opinionated framework: modules, DI, decorators (Angular-like)</td>
<td>Minimal but faster, schema-first</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Performance</td>
<td>Baseline</td>
<td>Runs on Express (default) or Fastify adapter</td>
<td>Noticeably higher throughput, lower overhead</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Validation</td>
<td>Bring your own (Zod, Joi)</td>
<td>Pipes + class-validator</td>
<td>JSON Schema built in (also serialisation)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Structure</td>
<td>Whatever the team decides</td>
<td>Enforced</td>
<td>Plugins and encapsulation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Async errors</td>
<td>Express 4: you must catch; Express 5: handled</td>
<td>Handled</td>
<td>Handled</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Good for</td>
<td>Small services, teams with strong conventions</td>
<td>Large teams, many services, enterprise consistency</td>
<td>Performance-sensitive APIs, gateways</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>How I’d frame the choice:</strong> the framework matters less
than consistent structure. For a large team building many services I’d
pick NestJS, because it enforces the same layout everywhere and new
joiners are productive quickly. For a lean, high-throughput service or a
gateway, Fastify. Express is fine when the team already has strong
conventions, and Express 5 finally handles async errors.</p>
<h3 id="middleware-order">1.4 Middleware order</h3>
<p>Order matters; each middleware sees the request only after the ones
above it.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb79"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb79-1"><a href="#cb79-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(<span class="fu">requestId</span>())<span class="op">;</span>              <span class="co">// 1. correlation ID first, so every log line has it</span></span>
<span id="cb79-2"><a href="#cb79-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(<span class="fu">httpLogger</span>())<span class="op">;</span>             <span class="co">// 2. log request/response with that ID</span></span>
<span id="cb79-3"><a href="#cb79-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(<span class="fu">helmet</span>())<span class="op">;</span>                 <span class="co">// 3. security headers</span></span>
<span id="cb79-4"><a href="#cb79-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(<span class="fu">cors</span>(corsOptions))<span class="op">;</span>        <span class="co">// 4. CORS before routes (and before auth for preflight)</span></span>
<span id="cb79-5"><a href="#cb79-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(express<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">json</span>({ limit<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;1mb&#39;</span> }))<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// 5. body parsing with a size limit</span></span>
<span id="cb79-6"><a href="#cb79-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(<span class="fu">rateLimiter</span>())<span class="op">;</span>            <span class="co">// 6. reject abusive traffic early, before expensive work</span></span>
<span id="cb79-7"><a href="#cb79-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/api/v1&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> authenticate<span class="op">,</span> routes)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// 7. auth, then routes</span></span>
<span id="cb79-8"><a href="#cb79-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(notFoundHandler)<span class="op">;</span>          <span class="co">// 8. unmatched routes</span></span>
<span id="cb79-9"><a href="#cb79-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>(errorHandler)<span class="op">;</span>             <span class="co">// 9. error handler LAST, with 4 arguments</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="error-handling">1.5 Error handling</h3>
<p><strong>Two kinds of errors</strong> (a distinction from Node’s own
best practices that interviewers like):</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Operational errors:</strong> expected failures in a correct
program: invalid input, not found, payment declined, DB timeout. Handle
them: return the right status, retry, or degrade.</li>
<li><strong>Programmer errors:</strong> bugs:
<code>undefined is not a function</code>, wrong assumptions. Don’t try
to keep running in an unknown state: log, return 500, and for truly
unexpected crashes let the process restart.</li>
</ul>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb80"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb80-1"><a href="#cb80-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">class</span> AppError <span class="kw">extends</span> <span class="bu">Error</span> {</span>
<span id="cb80-2"><a href="#cb80-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">constructor</span>(</span>
<span id="cb80-3"><a href="#cb80-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">public</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> code<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb80-4"><a href="#cb80-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    message<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb80-5"><a href="#cb80-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">public</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> status <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">500</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb80-6"><a href="#cb80-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">public</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> details<span class="op">?:</span> <span class="dt">unknown</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb80-7"><a href="#cb80-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  ) { <span class="kw">super</span>(message)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb80-8"><a href="#cb80-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb80-9"><a href="#cb80-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">class</span> NotFoundError <span class="kw">extends</span> AppError {</span>
<span id="cb80-10"><a href="#cb80-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">constructor</span>(resource<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> id<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>) { <span class="kw">super</span>(<span class="st">&#39;NOT_FOUND&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="vs">`</span><span class="sc">${</span>resource<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> </span><span class="sc">${</span>id<span class="sc">}</span><span class="vs"> not found`</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="dv">404</span>)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb80-11"><a href="#cb80-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb80-12"><a href="#cb80-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb80-13"><a href="#cb80-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">errorHandler</span>(err<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">unknown</span><span class="op">,</span> req<span class="op">:</span> Request<span class="op">,</span> res<span class="op">:</span> Response<span class="op">,</span> _next<span class="op">:</span> NextFunction) {</span>
<span id="cb80-14"><a href="#cb80-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (err <span class="kw">instanceof</span> AppError) {</span>
<span id="cb80-15"><a href="#cb80-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">log</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">warn</span>({ err<span class="op">,</span> code<span class="op">:</span> err<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">code</span> }<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;handled error&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb80-16"><a href="#cb80-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">return</span> res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">status</span>(err<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">status</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">json</span>({ error<span class="op">:</span> { code<span class="op">:</span> err<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">code</span><span class="op">,</span> message<span class="op">:</span> err<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">message</span><span class="op">,</span> details<span class="op">:</span> err<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">details</span> } })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb80-17"><a href="#cb80-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb80-18"><a href="#cb80-18" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">log</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">error</span>({ err }<span class="op">,</span> <span class="st">&#39;unhandled error&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span>      <span class="co">// full stack in logs only</span></span>
<span id="cb80-19"><a href="#cb80-19" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">status</span>(<span class="dv">500</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">json</span>({ error<span class="op">:</span> { code<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;INTERNAL&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> message<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;Something went wrong&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> requestId<span class="op">:</span> req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span> } })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb80-20"><a href="#cb80-20" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Rules I hold to: one consistent error shape across all services (or
RFC 9457 Problem Details); never leak stack traces or SQL errors to
clients; always include the request ID so support can find the log line;
map infrastructure errors (duplicate key, timeout) to domain errors in
the repository layer.</p>
<h3 id="logging-and-request-context">1.6 Logging and request
context</h3>
<p>Use structured JSON logs (pino is the fast default), one line per
event, with a request ID on every line. <code>AsyncLocalStorage</code>
carries the ID through async calls without passing it everywhere:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb81"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb81-1"><a href="#cb81-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">import</span> { AsyncLocalStorage } <span class="im">from</span> <span class="st">&#39;node:async_hooks&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb81-2"><a href="#cb81-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">const</span> context <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">AsyncLocalStorage</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>{ requestId<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">;</span> userId<span class="op">?:</span> <span class="dt">string</span> }<span class="op">&gt;</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb81-3"><a href="#cb81-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb81-4"><a href="#cb81-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>app<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">use</span>((req<span class="op">,</span> res<span class="op">,</span> next) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb81-5"><a href="#cb81-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> requestId <span class="op">=</span> req<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">header</span>(<span class="st">&#39;x-request-id&#39;</span>) <span class="op">??</span> crypto<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">randomUUID</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb81-6"><a href="#cb81-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">setHeader</span>(<span class="st">&#39;x-request-id&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> requestId)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb81-7"><a href="#cb81-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  context<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">run</span>({ requestId }<span class="op">,</span> next)<span class="op">;</span>       <span class="co">// everything downstream can read it</span></span>
<span id="cb81-8"><a href="#cb81-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb81-9"><a href="#cb81-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb81-10"><a href="#cb81-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">const</span> log <span class="op">=</span> (msg<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> extra <span class="op">=</span> {}) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span></span>
<span id="cb81-11"><a href="#cb81-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  logger<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">info</span>({ <span class="op">...</span>context<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">getStore</span>()<span class="op">,</span> <span class="op">...</span>extra }<span class="op">,</span> msg)<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Forward the same ID in headers to downstream services and in message
metadata, so one ID traces a request across the system (OpenTelemetry
does this formally in Week 3). Never log passwords, tokens, card numbers
or full PII; configure pino’s <code>redact</code> paths.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-1-3">How I’d answer — Hour 1</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. How do you structure a Node.js API?</strong> “Feature
modules, each with a thin controller, a service holding business logic,
and a repository for data access. Controllers only deal with HTTP;
services never see <code>req</code> or <code>res</code>; repositories
hide the database. Dependencies are injected from one composition root,
so services are unit-tested with fakes. For complex domains I go further
toward hexagonal architecture; for CRUD services I keep it simple.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. Express or NestJS?</strong> “For a large team or many
services, NestJS: it enforces structure, DI and validation conventions,
so every service looks the same. For a small or performance-critical
service, Fastify. Express is fine with strong team conventions. The
consistency matters more than the framework.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How do you design error handling for a large Express
app?</strong> “A typed <code>AppError</code> hierarchy for operational
errors with a code and status; repositories translate driver errors into
those. One error middleware at the end maps them to a single response
format with a request ID, logs unknown errors with full stack, and
returns a generic 500. Unhandled rejections crash the process so the
orchestrator restarts it cleanly.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. How do you trace one request across five
services?</strong> “Generate or accept a request ID at the edge, keep it
in <code>AsyncLocalStorage</code>, put it on every log line, and forward
it in headers and message metadata. In practice I’d use OpenTelemetry
for proper traces with spans, and keep the request ID for log
correlation.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-9">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Scaffold
<code>services/auth-service</code> with the feature-module layout,
composition root, <code>AppError</code> hierarchy and error
middleware</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Add pino with redaction and the
<code>AsyncLocalStorage</code> request ID</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write one service unit test using a
fake repository (no database)</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-2-authentication-and-api-security">Hour 2 — Authentication
and API security</h2>
<p>Auth is one of the few areas where a single design mistake becomes a
breach. Interviewers test whether you know the trade-offs rather than
one tutorial’s JWT setup: where tokens live, how you revoke them, how
one user is stopped from reading another user’s order. Fintech
experience is a real asset here; tie answers back to it.</p>
<h3 id="authentication-vs-authorization">2.1 Authentication vs
authorization</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Authentication:</strong> who are you? (login, tokens,
sessions)</li>
<li><strong>Authorization:</strong> what are you allowed to do with this
specific resource? (roles, ownership, policies)</li>
</ul>
<p>Most real breaches in APIs are authorization failures, not broken
logins.</p>
<h3 id="sessions-vs-jwt">2.2 Sessions vs JWT</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>Server-side sessions</th>
<th>JWT (stateless access tokens)</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Where state lives</td>
<td>Session store (Redis); client holds an opaque ID in a cookie</td>
<td>In the signed token itself</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Revocation</td>
<td>Delete the session: instant</td>
<td>Hard: token is valid until it expires</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Scaling</td>
<td>Needs a shared store across instances</td>
<td>Any service can verify with the public key</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Size</td>
<td>Tiny cookie</td>
<td>Grows with claims, sent on every request</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Best for</td>
<td>Server-rendered apps, single backend, admin panels</td>
<td>Many services/APIs, mobile clients, service-to-service</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>My default for an SPA + microservices:</strong> short-lived
JWT access token (5–15 min) plus a long-lived, rotating refresh token
stored server-side. That gives stateless verification for normal
requests and real revocation through the refresh token.</p>
<h3 id="jwt-done-properly">2.3 JWT done properly</h3>
<p><strong>Structure:</strong> <code>header.payload.signature</code>,
base64url-encoded. The payload is <strong>encoded, not
encrypted</strong>: anyone can read it. Never put secrets or sensitive
PII in it.</p>
<p>Checklist:</p>
<ul>
<li>Sign with <strong>RS256 or ES256</strong> (asymmetric) when several
services verify tokens: only the auth service holds the private key;
others fetch public keys from a <strong>JWKS</strong> endpoint, which
also allows key rotation (<code>kid</code> header).</li>
<li>HS256 (shared secret) is acceptable only for a single service; with
many services, every one of them holding the secret can mint
tokens.</li>
<li>On verify, pin the algorithm (<code>algorithms: ['RS256']</code>)
and check <code>exp</code>, <code>iss</code>, <code>aud</code>. Never
accept <code>alg: none</code>.</li>
<li>Keep claims minimal: <code>sub</code> (user ID), <code>roles</code>
or <code>scope</code>, <code>tenantId</code>, <code>exp</code>,
<code>iat</code>, <code>jti</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="refresh-token-rotation-with-reuse-detection">2.4 Refresh token
rotation with reuse detection</h3>
<pre class="text"><code>Login       -&gt; access token (10 min) + refresh token R1 (family F, stored hashed in DB)
Refresh R1  -&gt; mark R1 used, issue access + R2 (same family F)
Refresh R2  -&gt; mark R2 used, issue access + R3
Refresh R1 again (stolen copy) -&gt; R1 already used = reuse detected -&gt; revoke whole family F, force re-login</code></pre>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb83"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb83-1"><a href="#cb83-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">async</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">refresh</span>(presented<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">string</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb83-2"><a href="#cb83-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> record <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> tokens<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">findByHash</span>(<span class="fu">sha256</span>(presented))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-3"><a href="#cb83-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span>record <span class="op">||</span> record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">expiresAt</span> <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Date</span>()) <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">UnauthorizedError</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-4"><a href="#cb83-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">usedAt</span> <span class="op">||</span> record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">revokedAt</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb83-5"><a href="#cb83-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">await</span> tokens<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">revokeFamily</span>(record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">familyId</span>)<span class="op">;</span>           <span class="co">// theft signal</span></span>
<span id="cb83-6"><a href="#cb83-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    audit<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">warn</span>(<span class="st">&#39;refresh_token_reuse&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> { userId<span class="op">:</span> record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">userId</span> })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-7"><a href="#cb83-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">UnauthorizedError</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-8"><a href="#cb83-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb83-9"><a href="#cb83-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">await</span> tokens<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">markUsed</span>(record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-10"><a href="#cb83-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> next <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">randomToken</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-11"><a href="#cb83-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">await</span> tokens<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">create</span>({ userId<span class="op">:</span> record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">userId</span><span class="op">,</span> familyId<span class="op">:</span> record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">familyId</span><span class="op">,</span> hash<span class="op">:</span> <span class="fu">sha256</span>(next)<span class="op">,</span> expiresAt<span class="op">:</span> <span class="fu">in30Days</span>() })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-12"><a href="#cb83-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> { accessToken<span class="op">:</span> <span class="fu">signAccess</span>(record<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">userId</span>)<span class="op">,</span> refreshToken<span class="op">:</span> next }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb83-13"><a href="#cb83-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Store refresh tokens <strong>hashed</strong> (like passwords, but a
fast hash is fine because they’re long random values). Logout and “log
out of all devices” revoke the family or all families for the user.</p>
<h3 id="where-the-browser-keeps-tokens">2.5 Where the browser keeps
tokens</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Storage</th>
<th>XSS risk</th>
<th>CSRF risk</th>
<th>Notes</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>localStorage</code> / <code>sessionStorage</code></td>
<td>High: any injected script can read it</td>
<td>None</td>
<td>Common in tutorials; weakest option</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>JS memory only</td>
<td>Lower (not persisted)</td>
<td>None</td>
<td>Lost on reload, so pair with a refresh cookie</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>httpOnly; Secure; SameSite</code> cookie</td>
<td>Script can’t read it</td>
<td>Possible; mitigated by <code>SameSite=Lax/Strict</code> and CSRF
tokens</td>
<td>Best for refresh tokens</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>My setup:</strong> access token in memory, refresh token in
an <code>httpOnly</code>, <code>Secure</code>,
<code>SameSite=Strict</code> cookie scoped to the refresh path
(<code>Path=/auth/refresh</code>). On page load, the SPA calls refresh
to get a new access token.</p>
<h3 id="oauth-2.0-and-openid-connect">2.6 OAuth 2.0 and OpenID
Connect</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>OAuth 2.0</strong> is for delegated
<strong>authorization</strong> (“this app may read my calendar”).
<strong>OIDC</strong> adds an identity layer on top (ID token: who
logged in).</li>
<li><strong>Authorization Code + PKCE:</strong> the flow for SPAs and
mobile apps. Implicit flow is deprecated.</li>
<li><strong>Client Credentials:</strong> service-to-service, no user
involved.</li>
<li>In enterprises, use an identity provider (Keycloak, Auth0, Okta,
Cognito, Azure AD) rather than building login yourself; your services
just validate tokens.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="passwords">2.7 Passwords</h3>
<ul>
<li>Hash with <strong>argon2id</strong> (preferred) or
<strong>bcrypt</strong> with cost 10–12; never SHA-256 or MD5 for
passwords, they are built to be fast.</li>
<li>Use the async APIs; remember they run on the libuv thread pool (Day
3), so huge login spikes compete with fs and DNS.</li>
<li>Rate-limit and lock out by account and by IP; return the same error
for “user not found” and “wrong password” so attackers can’t enumerate
emails.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="authorization-rbac-abac-and-ownership">2.8 Authorization: RBAC,
ABAC and ownership</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>RBAC:</strong> permissions attached to roles
(<code>admin</code>, <code>support</code>, <code>customer</code>).
Simple; enough for most products.</li>
<li><strong>ABAC / policy-based:</strong> decisions based on attributes
(user’s tenant, resource owner, time, region). Needed for multi-tenant
and B2B products. Tools: CASL, Casbin, OPA, Cerbos.</li>
<li><strong>Ownership checks belong in the query</strong>, not after
it:</li>
</ul>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb84"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb84-1"><a href="#cb84-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Vulnerable (BOLA): any logged-in user can read any order by guessing IDs</span></span>
<span id="cb84-2"><a href="#cb84-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> order <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> Orders<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">findById</span>(req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">params</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb84-3"><a href="#cb84-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb84-4"><a href="#cb84-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// Safe: scope by the authenticated user (or tenant) in the query itself</span></span>
<span id="cb84-5"><a href="#cb84-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> order <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> Orders<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">findOne</span>({ _id<span class="op">:</span> req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">params</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="op">,</span> customerId<span class="op">:</span> req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">user</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span> })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb84-6"><a href="#cb84-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span>order) <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">NotFoundError</span>(<span class="st">&#39;Order&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">params</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// 404, don&#39;t reveal it exists</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="owasp-api-security-top-10-2023">2.9 OWASP API Security Top 10
(2023)</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>#</th>
<th>Risk</th>
<th>What it looks like</th>
<th>Defence</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)</td>
<td><code>/orders/123</code> returns someone else’s order</td>
<td>Ownership/tenant filter in every query</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>Broken Authentication</td>
<td>Weak tokens, no rate limit on login, long-lived tokens</td>
<td>Standard flows, short TTLs, lockouts, MFA</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td>Broken Object Property Level Authorization</td>
<td>Response leaks <code>passwordHash</code>; client sets
<code>role: 'admin'</code> in a PATCH</td>
<td>Explicit response DTOs; allow-listed input fields</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>Unrestricted Resource Consumption</td>
<td>No pagination limit, huge uploads, expensive queries</td>
<td>Rate limits, max page size, body limits, timeouts</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td>Broken Function Level Authorization</td>
<td>Customer calls <code>/admin/refunds</code></td>
<td>Role checks on every route, deny by default</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6</td>
<td>Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows</td>
<td>Bots buying all stock, coupon abuse</td>
<td>Business-level limits, bot detection, CAPTCHA</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7</td>
<td>Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)</td>
<td>“Import from URL” fetches internal metadata endpoints</td>
<td>Allow-list hosts, block private IP ranges</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8</td>
<td>Security Misconfiguration</td>
<td>Verbose errors, open CORS, default credentials</td>
<td>Helmet, strict CORS, hardened config</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>9</td>
<td>Improper Inventory Management</td>
<td>Old <code>/v1</code> still live and unpatched</td>
<td>API inventory, retire old versions</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>10</td>
<td>Unsafe Consumption of APIs</td>
<td>Trusting third-party responses blindly</td>
<td>Validate external responses too, timeouts</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Other basics to mention: <code>helmet</code> for headers, CORS with
an explicit origin allow-list (never <code>*</code> with credentials),
body size limits, <code>npm audit</code> / Dependabot / Snyk in CI,
secrets in a vault or KMS rather than <code>.env</code> files committed
anywhere.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-2-3">How I’d answer — Hour 2</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. JWT or sessions?</strong> “Depends on the architecture.
For a single server-rendered app, sessions in Redis are simpler and
revocation is instant. For an SPA talking to several services,
short-lived JWT access tokens verified with a public key via JWKS, plus
rotating refresh tokens stored server-side so we can still revoke. The
access token’s short lifetime limits the damage window.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. How do you revoke a JWT?</strong> “You mostly don’t; you
keep it short-lived and revoke the refresh token so it can’t be renewed.
For high-risk cases, like a compromised account, a small deny-list of
<code>jti</code>s in Redis, checked until those tokens expire, closes
the gap.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. Where should a SPA store tokens?</strong> “Not in
localStorage, because any XSS can read it. Access token in memory,
refresh token in an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie limited to the
refresh endpoint, plus CSRF protection where cookies are used for
state-changing requests.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. What’s the most common API vulnerability you’d look for
in a review?</strong> “BOLA: fetching a resource by ID without checking
it belongs to the caller. I want ownership or tenant scoping inside the
query itself, and integration tests that log in as user A and try to
read user B’s resources.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. How do you detect a stolen refresh token?</strong>
“Rotation with reuse detection. Each refresh issues a new token and
marks the old one used. If a used token is presented again, either the
user or an attacker has a copy, so I revoke the whole token family and
force re-login.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-10">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Build login, refresh (rotation +
reuse detection), logout and logout-all in the capstone auth
service</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Store refresh tokens hashed with a
<code>familyId</code>; refresh cookie is httpOnly, Secure,
SameSite=Strict</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />RS256 signing with a JWKS endpoint;
a second service verifies tokens using only the public key</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Write an integration test proving
user A gets 404 on user B’s order</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-3-performance-and-scaling-a-node-api">Hour 3 — Performance
and scaling a Node API</h2>
<p>“How would you scale this API to 50,000 requests per second?” is a
standard senior question. A weak answer lists technologies. A strong one
starts by asking what the traffic looks like, finds the bottleneck with
numbers, and fixes the cheapest thing first. Structure your answer that
way.</p>
<h3 id="start-with-numbers">3.1 Start with numbers</h3>
<p>Questions to ask before proposing anything: read/write ratio? peak vs
average? p95/p99 latency target? payload size? Is it one hot endpoint or
spread out?</p>
<p>Rough capacity reasoning: a well-written Node instance on one core
typically handles somewhere in the low thousands of simple I/O-bound
requests per second; heavy JSON, auth and DB work lowers that. So 50k
RPS is tens of instances behind a load balancer, <strong>and</strong> a
data layer that can take the load, which is almost always the real
bottleneck. Always say “I’d load-test to get the real per-instance
number” rather than quoting one as fact.</p>
<p><strong>Load testing tools:</strong> autocannon (quick, Node), k6
(scripted scenarios, thresholds in CI), Gatling or JMeter in some
enterprises. Test against production-like data volumes; most performance
problems only appear with real data size.</p>
<h3 id="make-instances-stateless-then-scale-horizontally">3.2 Make
instances stateless, then scale horizontally</h3>
<ul>
<li>No in-memory sessions, caches that must be consistent, or rate-limit
counters on the instance; move them to Redis.</li>
<li>File uploads go to object storage (S3), not local disk.</li>
<li>Scheduled jobs run once (a dedicated worker or a distributed lock),
not on every instance.</li>
<li>Then: load balancer + autoscaling (Kubernetes HPA on CPU, or on
requests per pod / queue depth).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="the-usual-bottlenecks-in-the-order-i-check-them">3.3 The usual
bottlenecks, in the order I check them</h3>
