<span id="cb85-7"><a href="#cb85-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> product<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb85-8"><a href="#cb85-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb85-9"><a href="#cb85-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// On update: write to DB, then DEL the key (invalidate, don&#39;t update)</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Caching pitfalls to name: <strong>stampede</strong> when a hot key
expires and thousands of requests hit the DB at once (fix: TTL jitter, a
lock or “single flight” so one request rebuilds), <strong>stale
data</strong> after writes (invalidate on write, short TTLs), and
caching per-user data under shared keys (data leak).</p>
<h3 id="protecting-the-service-from-its-dependencies">3.5 Protecting the
service from its dependencies</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Timeouts on every outbound call.</strong> Default HTTP
clients often wait far too long. A dependency with no timeout turns a
slow partner into your outage.</li>
<li><strong>Retries</strong> only for idempotent operations, with
exponential backoff and jitter, and a cap.</li>
<li><strong>Circuit breaker</strong> (opossum): after repeated failures,
fail fast for a while instead of waiting on a dead dependency; serve a
fallback if possible.</li>
<li><strong>Bulkheads:</strong> separate connection pools or concurrency
limits per dependency, so one slow partner can’t use up everything.</li>
<li><strong>Load shedding:</strong> when overloaded, reject some
requests quickly with 503 rather than serving all of them slowly
(e.g. reject when event-loop delay exceeds a threshold).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="cheap-wins-at-the-http-layer">3.6 Cheap wins at the HTTP
layer</h3>
<ul>
<li>Compression (gzip/brotli), ideally at the load balancer or proxy,
not in Node</li>
<li>Pagination everywhere, with a maximum page size; cursor pagination
for large or fast-changing lists</li>
<li>Response field selection or sparse fieldsets for heavy
resources</li>
<li>HTTP/2 between clients and the edge</li>
<li>Move slow work out of the request: return 202 Accepted with a job ID
and process via a queue</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-3-3">How I’d answer — Hour 3</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. How would you scale a Node API to 50k RPS?</strong>
“First I’d clarify the traffic: read/write ratio, peak versus average,
latency targets, which endpoints are hot. Then load-test one instance to
get a real per-instance number and find the bottleneck. Usually the plan
is: make instances stateless and scale them horizontally behind a load
balancer with autoscaling; fix the data layer with indexes, read
replicas and connection pool sizing; add caching at the CDN and Redis
level for hot reads; move slow work to queues. Throughout, timeouts and
circuit breakers so one slow dependency can’t take us down. I’d verify
every step with load tests rather than guessing.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. What is a cache stampede and how do you prevent
it?</strong> “When a popular key expires, many requests miss at once and
all hit the database together. Prevent it with TTL jitter so keys don’t
expire together, a lock or single-flight so only one request rebuilds
the value while others wait or get stale data, and pre-warming for known
hot keys.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How do you size a database connection pool?</strong> “Per
instance, enough to keep the DB busy but not more; more connections than
the DB has cores mostly adds contention. Total connections are pool size
times instance count, so autoscaling to 40 pods with a pool of 20 means
800 connections. That’s why I’d use PgBouncer for Postgres or keep pools
small and measure wait time for a connection.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. A downstream partner API got slow and our whole service
went down. What would you change?</strong> “Aggressive timeouts on that
client, a circuit breaker so we fail fast once it’s clearly unhealthy, a
separate concurrency limit so it can’t consume all our capacity, and a
fallback or queued retry for the feature that depends on it. Plus
alerting on that dependency’s latency so we see it before customers
do.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-11">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Load-test the auth service login and
a cached product GET with autocannon; record p50/p99 and
RPS</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Add Redis cache-aside with TTL
jitter and invalidation on update</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Wrap one outbound HTTP call with a
timeout and an opossum circuit breaker; simulate the dependency being
down</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-4-machine-coding-round">Hour 4 — Machine-coding round</h2>
<p>These three problems show up constantly in senior Node machine-coding
rounds because each one connects to a production concern: caching, rate
limiting and controlling concurrency. Treat this as a mock: 15–20
minutes per problem, no AI, no autocomplete, talking out loud.</p>
<p>The routine that scores well in these rounds:</p>
<ol type="1">
<li>Restate the requirements and ask about edge cases (2 minutes).</li>
<li>State the approach and its complexity before typing.</li>
<li>Write clean, working code first; optimise after.</li>
<li>Walk through a test case by hand.</li>
<li>Volunteer how you’d make it production-ready (distributed,
observable, tested).</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="lru-cache">4.1 LRU cache</h3>
<p><strong>Problem:</strong> a cache with a fixed capacity;
<code>get</code> and <code>set</code> in O(1); when full, evict the
least recently used entry.</p>
<p><strong>Questions to ask:</strong> does <code>get</code> count as
use? (yes) What should <code>get</code> return on a miss? Is capacity ≥
1? Do we need TTL?</p>
<p><strong>Approach:</strong> a JavaScript <code>Map</code> remembers
insertion order. Re-inserting a key on every access moves it to the end,
so the first key is always the least recently used.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb86"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb86-1"><a href="#cb86-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">class</span> LRUCache<span class="op">&lt;</span>K<span class="op">,</span> V<span class="op">&gt;</span> {</span>

<span id="cb86-4"><a href="#cb86-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span><span class="bu">Number</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">isInteger</span>(capacity) <span class="op">||</span> capacity <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="dv">1</span>) <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">RangeError</span>(<span class="st">&#39;capacity must be &gt;= 1&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb86-5"><a href="#cb86-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>

<span id="cb86-19"><a href="#cb86-19" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">map</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">delete</span>(oldest)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb86-20"><a href="#cb86-20" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    }</span>
<span id="cb86-21"><a href="#cb86-21" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">map</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(key<span class="op">,</span> value)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb86-22"><a href="#cb86-22" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb86-23"><a href="#cb86-23" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb86-24"><a href="#cb86-24" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">get</span> <span class="fu">size</span>() { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">map</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">size</span><span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb86-25"><a href="#cb86-25" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Complexity: O(1) average for both operations; O(capacity) memory.</p>
<p><strong>Follow-ups to expect:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><em>“Do it without relying on Map ordering.”</em> Hash map from key
to node, plus a doubly linked list with head (most recent) and tail
(least recent). <code>get</code> unlinks the node and moves it to the
head; eviction removes the tail. Both O(1). This is the classic answer
in languages without ordered maps.</li>
<li><em>“Add TTL.”</em> Store <code>{ value, expiresAt }</code>; on
<code>get</code>, treat expired entries as a miss and delete them (lazy
expiry). Optionally sweep periodically with an <code>unref()</code>’d
timer.</li>
<li><em>“How would you use this in production?”</em>
<code>lru-cache</code> package for in-process; Redis with
<code>maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru</code> for a shared cache across
instances.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="token-bucket-rate-limiter">4.2 Token-bucket rate limiter</h3>
<p><strong>Problem:</strong> limit each client to N requests per period,
allowing short bursts.</p>
<p><strong>How the algorithm works:</strong> each client has a bucket
holding up to <code>capacity</code> tokens. Tokens refill continuously
at <code>refillPerSecond</code>. Each request takes one token; if the
bucket is empty, reject with 429.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb87"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb87-1"><a href="#cb87-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">class</span> TokenBucket {</span>
<span id="cb87-2"><a href="#cb87-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">private</span> tokens<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-3"><a href="#cb87-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">private</span> lastRefill <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Date</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">now</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-4"><a href="#cb87-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">constructor</span>(<span class="kw">private</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> capacity<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">private</span> <span class="kw">readonly</span> refillPerSecond<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb87-5"><a href="#cb87-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">tokens</span> <span class="op">=</span> capacity<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-6"><a href="#cb87-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb87-7"><a href="#cb87-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">private</span> <span class="fu">refill</span>() {</span>
<span id="cb87-8"><a href="#cb87-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> now <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Date</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">now</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-9"><a href="#cb87-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> elapsedSec <span class="op">=</span> (now <span class="op">-</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">lastRefill</span>) <span class="op">/</span> <span class="dv">1000</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-10"><a href="#cb87-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">tokens</span> <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Math</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">min</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">capacity</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">tokens</span> <span class="op">+</span> elapsedSec <span class="op">*</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">refillPerSecond</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-11"><a href="#cb87-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">lastRefill</span> <span class="op">=</span> now<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-12"><a href="#cb87-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb87-13"><a href="#cb87-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">tryTake</span>(cost <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">1</span>)<span class="op">:</span> { allowed<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">boolean</span><span class="op">;</span> remaining<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span><span class="op">;</span> retryAfterSec<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span> } {</span>
<span id="cb87-14"><a href="#cb87-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">refill</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-15"><a href="#cb87-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">tokens</span> <span class="op">&gt;=</span> cost) {</span>
<span id="cb87-16"><a href="#cb87-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">tokens</span> <span class="op">-=</span> cost<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-17"><a href="#cb87-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="cf">return</span> { allowed<span class="op">:</span> <span class="kw">true</span><span class="op">,</span> remaining<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Math</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">floor</span>(<span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">tokens</span>)<span class="op">,</span> retryAfterSec<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">0</span> }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-18"><a href="#cb87-18" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    }</span>
<span id="cb87-19"><a href="#cb87-19" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> retryAfterSec <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Math</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">ceil</span>((cost <span class="op">-</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">tokens</span>) <span class="op">/</span> <span class="kw">this</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">refillPerSecond</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-20"><a href="#cb87-20" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">return</span> { allowed<span class="op">:</span> <span class="kw">false</span><span class="op">,</span> remaining<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">,</span> retryAfterSec }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-21"><a href="#cb87-21" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb87-22"><a href="#cb87-22" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb87-23"><a href="#cb87-23" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb87-24"><a href="#cb87-24" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">rateLimit</span>({ capacity <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">20</span><span class="op">,</span> refillPerSecond <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">5</span><span class="op">,</span> keyOf <span class="op">=</span> (req<span class="op">:</span> Request) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> req<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">ip</span> <span class="op">??</span> <span class="st">&#39;anon&#39;</span> } <span class="op">=</span> {}) {</span>
<span id="cb87-25"><a href="#cb87-25" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> buckets <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Map</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> TokenBucket<span class="op">&gt;</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-26"><a href="#cb87-26" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> (req<span class="op">:</span> Request<span class="op">,</span> res<span class="op">:</span> Response<span class="op">,</span> next<span class="op">:</span> NextFunction) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb87-27"><a href="#cb87-27" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> key <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">keyOf</span>(req)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-28"><a href="#cb87-28" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">let</span> bucket <span class="op">=</span> buckets<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(key)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-29"><a href="#cb87-29" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span>bucket) { bucket <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">TokenBucket</span>(capacity<span class="op">,</span> refillPerSecond)<span class="op">;</span> buckets<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">set</span>(key<span class="op">,</span> bucket)<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb87-30"><a href="#cb87-30" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> { allowed<span class="op">,</span> remaining<span class="op">,</span> retryAfterSec } <span class="op">=</span> bucket<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">tryTake</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-31"><a href="#cb87-31" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">setHeader</span>(<span class="st">&#39;RateLimit-Remaining&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="bu">String</span>(remaining))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-32"><a href="#cb87-32" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (<span class="op">!</span>allowed) {</span>
<span id="cb87-33"><a href="#cb87-33" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">setHeader</span>(<span class="st">&#39;Retry-After&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="bu">String</span>(retryAfterSec))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-34"><a href="#cb87-34" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="cf">return</span> res<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">status</span>(<span class="dv">429</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">json</span>({ error<span class="op">:</span> { code<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;RATE_LIMITED&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> message<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;Too many requests&#39;</span> } })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-35"><a href="#cb87-35" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    }</span>
<span id="cb87-36"><a href="#cb87-36" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="fu">next</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-37"><a href="#cb87-37" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb87-38"><a href="#cb87-38" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Refill is computed lazily on each request, so there are no timers per
client. Things to point out yourself: the <code>buckets</code> map grows
with every new IP, so evict idle buckets (or use the LRU from 4.1); key
by user ID or API key when authenticated, by IP otherwise; behind a
proxy, set Express’s <code>trust proxy</code> correctly or
<code>req.ip</code> is the load balancer’s address.</p>
<p><strong>Algorithms compared:</strong></p>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Algorithm</th>
<th>Behaviour</th>
<th>Trade-off</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Fixed window</td>
<td>Count per minute, reset on the minute</td>
<td>Simple; allows 2× burst at window edges</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Sliding log</td>
<td>Store each request timestamp</td>
<td>Exact; memory per request</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Sliding window counter</td>
<td>Weighted mix of current and previous window</td>
<td>Good accuracy, cheap; common in Redis</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Token bucket</td>
<td>Refill at a rate, bursts up to capacity</td>
<td>Allows controlled bursts; most popular for APIs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Leaky bucket</td>
<td>Queue drained at a fixed rate</td>
<td>Smooth output; adds latency</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Production version:</strong> an in-memory limiter only works
per instance, so with 10 pods each client effectively gets 10× the
limit. Use Redis with an atomic Lua script (or
<code>rate-limiter-flexible</code>), or enforce limits at the API
gateway.</p>
<h3 id="async-task-queue-with-a-concurrency-limit">4.3 Async task queue
with a concurrency limit</h3>
<p><strong>Problem:</strong> run many async tasks (e.g. 10,000 API
calls) with at most N running at once; each caller gets its own result
or error.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb88"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb88-1"><a href="#cb88-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">createLimiter</span>(concurrency<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">number</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb88-2"><a href="#cb88-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">if</span> (concurrency <span class="op">&lt;</span> <span class="dv">1</span>) <span class="cf">throw</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">RangeError</span>(<span class="st">&#39;concurrency must be &gt;= 1&#39;</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-3"><a href="#cb88-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">let</span> active <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-4"><a href="#cb88-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> queue<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Array</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="dt">void</span><span class="op">&gt;</span> <span class="op">=</span> []<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-5"><a href="#cb88-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb88-6"><a href="#cb88-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">const</span> next <span class="op">=</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb88-7"><a href="#cb88-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (active <span class="op">&gt;=</span> concurrency) <span class="cf">return</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-8"><a href="#cb88-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> start <span class="op">=</span> queue<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">shift</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-9"><a href="#cb88-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">if</span> (start) <span class="fu">start</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-10"><a href="#cb88-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-11"><a href="#cb88-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb88-12"><a href="#cb88-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">limit</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>(task<span class="op">:</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>)<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb88-13"><a href="#cb88-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>((resolve<span class="op">,</span> reject) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb88-14"><a href="#cb88-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      queue<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">push</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb88-15"><a href="#cb88-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        active<span class="op">++;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-16"><a href="#cb88-16" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>        <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">resolve</span>()</span>
<span id="cb88-17"><a href="#cb88-17" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>          <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(task)                 <span class="co">// also catches tasks that throw synchronously</span></span>
<span id="cb88-18"><a href="#cb88-18" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>          <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">then</span>(resolve<span class="op">,</span> reject)</span>
<span id="cb88-19"><a href="#cb88-19" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>          <span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">finally</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> { active<span class="op">--;</span> <span class="fu">next</span>()<span class="op">;</span> })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-20"><a href="#cb88-20" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-21"><a href="#cb88-21" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="fu">next</span>()<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-22"><a href="#cb88-22" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-23"><a href="#cb88-23" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-24"><a href="#cb88-24" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb88-25"><a href="#cb88-25" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb88-26"><a href="#cb88-26" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// usage</span></span>
<span id="cb88-27"><a href="#cb88-27" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> limit <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">createLimiter</span>(<span class="dv">5</span>)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb88-28"><a href="#cb88-28" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> results <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">allSettled</span>(userIds<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">map</span>((id) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="fu">limit</span>(() <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> crm<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">sync</span>(id))))<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Design points to say out loud: one failing task doesn’t stop the
others (each promise settles independently);
<code>Promise.resolve().then(task)</code> turns a synchronous throw into
a rejection; <code>queue.shift()</code> is O(n), fine for thousands of
tasks, but a real queue would use a ring buffer or linked list.
Extensions interviewers ask for: per-task timeout, cancellation with
<code>AbortSignal</code>, priorities, and a <code>onIdle()</code>
promise.</p>
<p><strong>Add retry with exponential backoff and jitter:</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb89"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb89-1"><a href="#cb89-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">async</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">retry</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span>(fn<span class="op">:</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;,</span> { attempts <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">4</span><span class="op">,</span> baseMs <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">200</span><span class="op">,</span> maxMs <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">5000</span><span class="op">,</span> isRetryable <span class="op">=</span> (_e<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">unknown</span>) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="kw">true</span> } <span class="op">=</span> {})<span class="op">:</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>T<span class="op">&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb89-2"><a href="#cb89-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="kw">let</span> lastError<span class="op">:</span> <span class="dt">unknown</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb89-3"><a href="#cb89-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">for</span> (<span class="kw">let</span> i <span class="op">=</span> <span class="dv">0</span><span class="op">;</span> i <span class="op">&lt;</span> attempts<span class="op">;</span> i<span class="op">++</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb89-4"><a href="#cb89-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">try</span> { <span class="cf">return</span> <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="fu">fn</span>()<span class="op">;</span> }</span>
<span id="cb89-5"><a href="#cb89-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">catch</span> (err) {</span>
<span id="cb89-6"><a href="#cb89-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      lastError <span class="op">=</span> err<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb89-7"><a href="#cb89-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="cf">if</span> (i <span class="op">===</span> attempts <span class="op">-</span> <span class="dv">1</span> <span class="op">||</span> <span class="op">!</span><span class="fu">isRetryable</span>(err)) <span class="cf">break</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb89-8"><a href="#cb89-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="kw">const</span> delay <span class="op">=</span> <span class="bu">Math</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">min</span>(maxMs<span class="op">,</span> baseMs <span class="op">*</span> <span class="dv">2</span> <span class="op">**</span> i) <span class="op">*</span> (<span class="fl">0.5</span> <span class="op">+</span> <span class="bu">Math</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">random</span>() <span class="op">/</span> <span class="dv">2</span>)<span class="op">;</span> <span class="co">// jitter</span></span>
<span id="cb89-9"><a href="#cb89-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Promise</span>((r) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> <span class="pp">setTimeout</span>(r<span class="op">,</span> delay))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb89-10"><a href="#cb89-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    }</span>
<span id="cb89-11"><a href="#cb89-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb89-12"><a href="#cb89-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">throw</span> lastError<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb89-13"><a href="#cb89-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Why jitter: without it, every client that failed at the same moment
retries at the same moment, and the recovering service gets hit by
synchronised waves. Only retry idempotent operations or ones protected
by an idempotency key, and never retry 4xx validation errors.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-4-3">How I’d answer — Hour 4</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Implement an LRU cache in O(1).</strong> Write 4.1 with a
<code>Map</code>, then add: “Without ordered maps I’d use a hash map
plus a doubly linked list: map lookups find the node, the list keeps
recency order, so moving a node to the head and evicting the tail are
both constant time.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. How would you rate-limit an API that runs on 20
pods?</strong> “Not in memory, since each pod would allow the full
limit. A shared counter in Redis with an atomic Lua script implementing
a token bucket or sliding window, keyed by API key or user, with
standard <code>RateLimit</code> and <code>Retry-After</code> headers.
For coarse protection, limits at the gateway or WAF as well.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How do you call an external API for 50,000 records
without getting blocked?</strong> “A concurrency limiter so only N calls
are in flight, a rate limiter matching the partner’s quota, retries with
exponential backoff and jitter for 429s and 5xx, and respecting their
<code>Retry-After</code>. For very large jobs, run it as a background
job with progress tracking and resume from a checkpoint.”</p>

said out loud, each under 90 seconds</label></li>
</ul>
<h1 id="day-5-fri-rest-graphql-swagger-testing">Day 5 (Fri) — REST,
GraphQL, Swagger, testing</h1>
<h2 id="hour-1-rest-api-design">Hour 1 — REST API design</h2>
<p>Everyone has built REST APIs; few can defend their design choices.
Expect “design the API for X” exercises where the interviewer pushes on
pagination, retries, concurrent updates and versioning. Those four are
where senior answers differ from mid-level ones.</p>
<h3 id="resources-and-urls">1.1 Resources and URLs</h3>
<p><strong>What REST is, practically:</strong> model the domain as
resources (nouns) identified by URLs, and use HTTP methods for actions
on them. State lives on the server; each request carries everything
needed (stateless).</p>
<pre class="text"><code>GET    /v1/orders                     list (filter, sort, paginate)
POST   /v1/orders                     create
GET    /v1/orders/{orderId}           read one
PATCH  /v1/orders/{orderId}           partial update
DELETE /v1/orders/{orderId}           delete / cancel
GET    /v1/customers/{id}/orders      sub-collection (ownership is clear)
POST   /v1/orders/{orderId}/refunds   an action modelled as creating a resource
POST   /v1/orders/{orderId}:cancel    an action as a custom method (Google API style)</code></pre>
<p>Conventions I’d keep consistent across services: plural nouns,
kebab-case paths, camelCase JSON, IDs as opaque strings (UUID/ULID;
never expose auto-increment IDs, they leak volume and invite
enumeration), ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, money as integer minor units plus
currency (<code>{ "amount": 49900, "currency": "INR" }</code>), never
floats.</p>
<p>Avoid nesting deeper than one level.
<code>/customers/1/orders/2/items/3</code> couples the URL to a
hierarchy that changes; <code>/order-items/3</code> or
<code>/orders/2/items</code> is enough.</p>
<h3 id="methods-safety-and-idempotency">1.2 Methods, safety and
idempotency</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Method</th>
<th>Safe (no side effects)</th>
<th>Idempotent (same effect if repeated)</th>
<th>Typical response</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>GET</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>200</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>HEAD / OPTIONS</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>200 / 204</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>PUT (full replace)</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>200 or 204 (201 if it created)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>DELETE</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>204 (and 204 or 404 on repeat, by convention)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>PATCH (partial)</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>Not guaranteed</td>
<td>200</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>POST (create / action)</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>No</td>
<td>201 + <code>Location</code> header, or 202</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Why idempotency matters:</strong> networks fail after the
server processed a request but before the client got the response.
Clients and gateways retry. Retrying an idempotent call is safe;
retrying a non-idempotent POST can charge a customer twice.</p>
<p><strong>PUT vs PATCH:</strong> PUT replaces the whole resource
(missing fields are cleared); PATCH changes only what’s sent. With
PATCH, decide and document the semantics: JSON Merge Patch (send changed
fields; <code>null</code> means remove) is simpler and what most APIs
use; JSON Patch (a list of operations) is more precise.</p>
<h3 id="idempotency-keys-for-post">1.3 Idempotency keys for POST</h3>
<p>The standard fix for payments, orders and anything that must not
happen twice (Stripe popularised it):</p>
<pre class="text"><code>POST /v1/payments
Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2a9e-...   (client generates one per logical operation)</code></pre>
<p>Server logic:</p>
<ol type="1">
<li>Look up the key (scoped to the client/user) in a store (Redis or a
DB table with a unique index).</li>
<li>Not found: insert it as “in progress” atomically, process the
request, store the response status and body against the key, return
it.</li>
<li>Found and completed: return the stored response without
re-processing.</li>
<li>Found and in progress: return 409 so the client retries later.</li>
<li>Same key with a different request body: 422, it’s a client bug.</li>
<li>Expire keys after 24–48 hours.</li>
</ol>
<p>The same idea protects message consumers (Week 3): store processed
message IDs and skip duplicates.</p>
<h3 id="status-codes-worth-being-precise-about">1.4 Status codes worth
being precise about</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Code</th>
<th>Use</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>200 / 201 / 202 / 204</td>
<td>OK / created (+ Location) / accepted for async processing / success
with no body</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>400</td>
<td>Malformed request, validation failed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>401</td>
<td>Not authenticated (missing or invalid token)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>403</td>
<td>Authenticated but not allowed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>404</td>
<td>Not found, also used instead of 403 to avoid revealing a resource
exists</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>409</td>
<td>Conflict: duplicate, invalid state transition, idempotency key in
progress</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>412</td>
<td>Precondition failed (<code>If-Match</code> version mismatch)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>415 / 422</td>
<td>Unsupported media type / well-formed but semantically invalid (teams
use 400 or 422; pick one)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>429</td>
<td>Rate limited (+ <code>Retry-After</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>500 / 502 / 503 / 504</td>
<td>Bug / bad upstream response / overloaded or in maintenance /
upstream timeout</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>One error body format everywhere, for example RFC 9457 Problem
Details: <code>{ type, title, status, detail, instance }</code> plus
your own <code>code</code> and <code>errors[]</code> for field-level
validation.</p>
<h3 id="pagination">1.5 Pagination</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>Offset (<code>?page=3&amp;limit=20</code>)</th>
<th>Cursor (<code>?limit=20&amp;after=eyJpZCI6...</code>)</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>How</td>
<td><code>SKIP n LIMIT m</code></td>
<td><code>WHERE (createdAt, id) &lt; (lastCreatedAt, lastId) ORDER BY ... LIMIT m</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Jump to page 50</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>No, next/previous only</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Performance on deep pages</td>
<td>Gets slower: the DB still reads and discards skipped rows</td>
<td>Constant: uses the index directly</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Consistency when data changes</td>
<td>Items shift: duplicates or gaps between pages</td>
<td>Stable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Good for</td>
<td>Admin tables with page numbers, small datasets</td>
<td>Feeds, infinite scroll, large or fast-changing data, public
APIs</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb92"><pre
class="sourceCode json"><code class="sourceCode json"><span id="cb92-1"><a href="#cb92-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">{</span></span>
<span id="cb92-2"><a href="#cb92-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">&quot;data&quot;</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="ot">[</span> <span class="er">...</span> <span class="ot">]</span><span class="fu">,</span></span>
<span id="cb92-3"><a href="#cb92-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="dt">&quot;page&quot;</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="fu">{</span> <span class="dt">&quot;limit&quot;</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="dv">20</span><span class="fu">,</span> <span class="dt">&quot;nextCursor&quot;</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="st">&quot;eyJjcmVhdGVkQXQiOiIyMDI2LTExLTIwVDEwOjAwOjAwWiIsImlkIjoiYWJjIn0&quot;</span><span class="fu">,</span> <span class="dt">&quot;hasMore&quot;</span><span class="fu">:</span> <span class="kw">true</span> <span class="fu">}</span></span>
<span id="cb92-4"><a href="#cb92-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>The cursor is an opaque, base64-encoded tuple of the sort key plus a
unique tiebreaker (<code>id</code>), because sorting by
<code>createdAt</code> alone breaks when two rows share a timestamp.
Always enforce a maximum <code>limit</code>.</p>
<p>Filtering and sorting:
<code>GET /orders?status=paid&amp;createdFrom=2026-11-01&amp;sort=-createdAt</code>.
Allow-list filterable and sortable fields so clients can’t sort on
unindexed columns and bring the DB down.</p>
<h3 id="concurrency-optimistic-locking-with-etags">1.6 Concurrency:
optimistic locking with ETags</h3>
<p>Two admins edit the same product; the second save silently overwrites
the first (lost update). Fix:</p>
<pre class="text"><code>GET /v1/products/42            -&gt; 200, ETag: &quot;v7&quot;
PATCH /v1/products/42
If-Match: &quot;v7&quot;                 -&gt; 200, ETag: &quot;v8&quot;   (version matched)
PATCH /v1/products/42
If-Match: &quot;v7&quot;                 -&gt; 412 Precondition Failed (someone else saved v8)</code></pre>
<p>In the database:
<code>UPDATE products SET ..., version = version + 1 WHERE id = $1 AND version = $2</code>;
zero rows updated means conflict. ETags also enable conditional GETs
(<code>If-None-Match</code> → 304 Not Modified) to save bandwidth.</p>
<h3 id="versioning-and-long-running-operations">1.7 Versioning and
long-running operations</h3>
<p><strong>Versioning options:</strong> URL (<code>/v1/</code>) is the
most common and the easiest to route, cache and debug; header or
media-type versioning is cleaner in theory but harder to use. <strong>My
rule:</strong> URL major versions, and avoid needing v2 by making only
additive, non-breaking changes (Hour 3). Announce deprecations with the
<code>Deprecation</code> and <code>Sunset</code> headers and a
timeline.</p>
<p><strong>Long-running work</strong> (reports, bulk imports, video
processing): return <code>202 Accepted</code> with
<code>Location: /v1/jobs/{jobId}</code>; the client polls the job
resource (<code>status: queued | running | succeeded | failed</code>,
progress, result link), or gets a webhook when it finishes.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-1-4">How I’d answer — Hour 1</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Design the API for placing and paying for an
order.</strong> “<code>POST /v1/orders</code> with cart items creates an
order in <code>pending_payment</code> and returns 201 with its location.
<code>POST /v1/orders/{id}/payments</code> with an Idempotency-Key
starts payment, returning 202 if the gateway is asynchronous; the
gateway’s webhook updates the payment, and the order moves to
<code>paid</code>. <code>GET /v1/orders</code> uses cursor pagination
with status and date filters, scoped to the caller. State changes are
explicit transitions, invalid ones return 409, and admin edits use
<code>If-Match</code> to avoid lost updates.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. Offset or cursor pagination?</strong> “Cursor for
anything large, user-facing or fast-changing, because it uses the index
directly and doesn’t produce duplicates when new rows arrive. Offset
only where people genuinely need page numbers on a modest dataset, like
an admin table.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How do you prevent double charges when the client
retries?</strong> “An idempotency key per logical operation, sent in a
header. The server stores the key with the response; a retry with the
same key returns the stored result instead of charging again. Concurrent
duplicates get 409. Downstream, the payment provider call uses its own
idempotency key too.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. PUT vs PATCH?</strong> “PUT replaces the whole resource
and is idempotent. PATCH changes part of it. For most APIs I use PATCH
with merge-patch semantics and an allow-list of editable fields, and
protect concurrent edits with ETags.”</p>
<p><strong>Q5. How do you handle two users updating the same
record?</strong> “Optimistic concurrency: a version field returned as an
ETag. Updates send <code>If-Match</code>; the DB update includes the
version in its WHERE clause, and a mismatch returns 412 so the client
can reload and merge. For high-contention counters like stock, I’d use
atomic DB operations instead.”</p>

</ul>
<h2 id="hour-2-graphql">Hour 2 — GraphQL</h2>
<p>GraphQL questions at senior level are rarely about syntax. They’re
about the problems it introduces: N+1 queries, malicious deep queries,
caching, authorization on every field. And about judgement: when it’s
worth adopting, and when REST is simpler.</p>
<h3 id="what-it-is">2.1 What it is</h3>
<p><strong>What it is:</strong> a query language and runtime for APIs.
The server publishes a typed schema; clients send a query describing
exactly the fields they want, usually to a single endpoint
(<code>POST /graphql</code>), and get back JSON in the same shape.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Query:</strong> read. <strong>Mutation:</strong> write.
<strong>Subscription:</strong> server pushes updates (usually over
WebSockets).</li>
<li>Solves <strong>over-fetching</strong> (getting fields you don’t
need) and <strong>under-fetching</strong> (several round trips to build
one screen).</li>
</ul>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb94"><pre
class="sourceCode graphql"><code class="sourceCode graphql"><span id="cb94-1"><a href="#cb94-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Product {</span>
<span id="cb94-2"><a href="#cb94-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  id: <span class="dt">ID</span>!</span>
<span id="cb94-3"><a href="#cb94-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  name: <span class="dt">String</span>!</span>
<span id="cb94-4"><a href="#cb94-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  price: Money!</span>
<span id="cb94-5"><a href="#cb94-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  reviews(first: <span class="dt">Int</span> = <span class="dv">10</span>, after: <span class="dt">String</span>): ReviewConnection!</span>
<span id="cb94-6"><a href="#cb94-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb94-7"><a href="#cb94-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb94-8"><a href="#cb94-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Query {</span>
<span id="cb94-9"><a href="#cb94-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  product(id: <span class="dt">ID</span>!): Product</span>
<span id="cb94-10"><a href="#cb94-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  products(first: <span class="dt">Int</span> = <span class="dv">20</span>, after: <span class="dt">String</span>, filter: ProductFilter): ProductConnection!</span>
<span id="cb94-11"><a href="#cb94-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb94-12"><a href="#cb94-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb94-13"><a href="#cb94-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">type</span> Mutation {</span>
<span id="cb94-14"><a href="#cb94-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  addToCart(<span class="kw">input</span>: AddToCartInput!): AddToCartPayload!</span>
<span id="cb94-15"><a href="#cb94-15" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb95"><pre
class="sourceCode graphql"><code class="sourceCode graphql"><span id="cb95-1"><a href="#cb95-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">query</span> ProductPage(<span class="va">$id</span>: <span class="dt">ID</span>!) {</span>
<span id="cb95-2"><a href="#cb95-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  product(id: <span class="va">$id</span>) {</span>
<span id="cb95-3"><a href="#cb95-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    name</span>
<span id="cb95-4"><a href="#cb95-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    price { amount currency }</span>
<span id="cb95-5"><a href="#cb95-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    reviews(first: <span class="dv">5</span>) { edges { node { rating text author { name } } } }</span>
<span id="cb95-6"><a href="#cb95-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }</span>
<span id="cb95-7"><a href="#cb95-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Schema-first vs code-first:</strong> schema-first writes SDL
and implements resolvers to match; code-first generates the schema from
TypeScript classes or builders (NestJS GraphQL, Pothos, TypeGraphQL).
Code-first keeps types and schema in one place; schema-first makes the
contract easier to review. Either way, generate TypeScript types for
resolvers and clients (GraphQL Code Generator).</p>
<h3 id="resolvers-and-the-n1-problem">2.2 Resolvers and the N+1
problem</h3>
<p><strong>Resolvers</strong> are functions that return the value for
each field. The runtime calls them along the shape of the query.</p>
<p><strong>N+1:</strong> a query for 20 products, each with its reviews’
authors:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb96"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb96-1"><a href="#cb96-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> resolvers <span class="op">=</span> {</span>
<span id="cb96-2"><a href="#cb96-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  Query<span class="op">:</span> { products<span class="op">:</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> productRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">list</span>(<span class="dv">20</span>) }<span class="op">,</span>              <span class="co">// 1 query</span></span>
<span id="cb96-3"><a href="#cb96-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  Product<span class="op">:</span> { reviews<span class="op">:</span> (p) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> reviewRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">byProduct</span>(p<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span>) }<span class="op">,</span>       <span class="co">// +20 queries</span></span>
<span id="cb96-4"><a href="#cb96-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  Review<span class="op">:</span> { author<span class="op">:</span> (r) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> userRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">findById</span>(r<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">authorId</span>) }<span class="op">,</span>      <span class="co">// +100 queries</span></span>
<span id="cb96-5"><a href="#cb96-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>DataLoader</strong> fixes it by batching all keys requested
in the same tick into one call and caching per request:</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb97"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb97-1"><a href="#cb97-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">import</span> DataLoader <span class="im">from</span> <span class="st">&#39;dataloader&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb97-2"><a href="#cb97-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb97-3"><a href="#cb97-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">export</span> <span class="kw">function</span> <span class="fu">createLoaders</span>() {           <span class="co">// NEW instance per request: the cache must not leak between users</span></span>
<span id="cb97-4"><a href="#cb97-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="cf">return</span> {</span>
<span id="cb97-5"><a href="#cb97-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    userById<span class="op">:</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">DataLoader</span><span class="op">&lt;</span><span class="dt">string</span><span class="op">,</span> User <span class="op">|</span> <span class="dt">null</span><span class="op">&gt;</span>(<span class="kw">async</span> (ids) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb97-6"><a href="#cb97-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="kw">const</span> users <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> userRepo<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">findByIds</span>([<span class="op">...</span>ids])<span class="op">;</span>          <span class="co">// 1 query: WHERE id IN (...)</span></span>
<span id="cb97-7"><a href="#cb97-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="kw">const</span> map <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="bu">Map</span>(users<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">map</span>((u) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> [u<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">id</span><span class="op">,</span> u]))<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb97-8"><a href="#cb97-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>      <span class="cf">return</span> ids<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">map</span>((id) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> map<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">get</span>(id) <span class="op">??</span> <span class="kw">null</span>)<span class="op">;</span>                <span class="co">// same order and length as ids</span></span>
<span id="cb97-9"><a href="#cb97-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    })<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb97-10"><a href="#cb97-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb97-11"><a href="#cb97-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>}</span>
<span id="cb97-12"><a href="#cb97-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb97-13"><a href="#cb97-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// context: ({ req }) =&gt; ({ user: req.user, loaders: createLoaders() })</span></span>
<span id="cb97-14"><a href="#cb97-14" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> resolvers <span class="op">=</span> { Review<span class="op">:</span> { author<span class="op">:</span> (r<span class="op">,</span> _args<span class="op">,</span> ctx) <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> ctx<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">loaders</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="at">userById</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">load</span>(r<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">authorId</span>) } }<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>The two rules interviewers check: the batch function must return
results in the <strong>same order and length</strong> as the keys, and
loaders are created <strong>per request</strong> so one user’s data is
never served from another’s cache.</p>
<h3 id="pagination-and-errors">2.3 Pagination and errors</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Pagination:</strong> the Relay connection pattern
(<code>edges { node, cursor }</code>,
<code>pageInfo { hasNextPage, endCursor }</code>) is the common
standard; it’s cursor pagination from Hour 1 with a fixed shape.</li>
<li><strong>Errors:</strong> GraphQL usually returns HTTP 200 with an
<code>errors</code> array, and can return partial data. That breaks
monitoring that only looks at status codes. Good practice: put error
codes in <code>extensions.code</code>, and model expected business
failures as typed results in the schema:</li>
</ul>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb98"><pre
class="sourceCode graphql"><code class="sourceCode graphql"><span id="cb98-1"><a href="#cb98-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">union</span> AddToCartPayload = CartUpdated | OutOfStock | ProductNotFound</span></code></pre></div>
<h3 id="security-and-performance-limits">2.4 Security and performance
limits</h3>
<p>A public GraphQL endpoint lets clients write arbitrarily expensive
queries. Without limits, one nested query can take down the
database.</p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb99"><pre
class="sourceCode graphql"><code class="sourceCode graphql"><span id="cb99-1"><a href="#cb99-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">query</span> Evil { products(first: <span class="dv">100</span>) { reviews(first: <span class="dv">100</span>) { author { orders(first: <span class="dv">100</span>) { items { product { reviews(first: <span class="dv">100</span>) { ... } } } } } } } }</span></code></pre></div>
<p>Defences to list:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Depth limit</strong> (e.g. max 7–10 levels)</li>
<li><strong>Query cost / complexity analysis</strong>: assign costs to
fields and list sizes, reject queries over a budget</li>
<li><strong>Maximum page size</strong> on every list field</li>
<li><strong>Persisted queries / allow-listing:</strong> clients send a
hash of a pre-registered query, so arbitrary queries aren’t accepted in
production (best for first-party apps)</li>
<li><strong>Disable introspection</strong> in production for private
APIs</li>
<li><strong>Timeouts</strong> and rate limiting by cost, not just by
request count</li>
<li><strong>Authorization in the business layer</strong>, not only at
the top-level resolver: every path to a <code>User.email</code> field
must check permissions, because a client can reach the same type through
many routes in the graph</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="caching">2.5 Caching</h3>
<p>REST GETs cache naturally at the HTTP level (CDN, browser) because
each resource has a URL. GraphQL POSTs to one endpoint don’t. Options:
client-side normalised caches (Apollo Client, urql), persisted queries
over GET so CDNs can cache them, response caching per field with
<code>@cacheControl</code> hints, and DataLoader plus Redis on the
server side. Mention this trade-off unprompted; it’s often the deciding
factor.</p>
<h3 id="federation">2.6 Federation</h3>
<p>For many teams, <strong>Apollo Federation</strong> (or GraphQL Mesh /
schema stitching) lets each service own part of one graph: the Orders
service defines <code>Order</code>, the Users service extends it with
<code>Order.customer</code>. A gateway (router) plans and splits queries
across services. Powerful for large organisations; adds operational
complexity and another critical component. Don’t start there.</p>
<h3 id="rest-vs-graphql-vs-grpc">2.7 REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>REST</th>
<th>GraphQL</th>
<th>gRPC</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Contract</td>
<td>OpenAPI (optional)</td>
<td>Schema (mandatory)</td>
<td>Protobuf (mandatory)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Transport / format</td>
<td>HTTP + JSON</td>
<td>HTTP + JSON, usually one endpoint</td>
<td>HTTP/2 + binary Protobuf</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Fetching flexibility</td>
<td>Fixed per endpoint</td>
<td>Client chooses fields</td>
<td>Fixed per method</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>HTTP caching</td>
<td>Excellent</td>
<td>Hard</td>
<td>None at HTTP level</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Performance</td>
<td>Good</td>
<td>Good; risk of expensive queries</td>
<td>Best: compact, streaming, multiplexed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Browser support</td>
<td>Native</td>
<td>Native</td>
<td>Needs gRPC-Web proxy</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Best for</td>
<td>Public APIs, simple CRUD, cacheable resources</td>
<td>Rich UIs aggregating many sources, mobile apps on slow networks,
BFF</td>
<td>Internal service-to-service calls, low latency, streaming</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>My usual architecture:</strong> REST (or GraphQL as a BFF) at
the edge for frontends and partners, gRPC or async messaging between
internal services where performance matters, REST internally where
simplicity matters more.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-2-4">How I’d answer — Hour 2</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. REST vs GraphQL, when would you pick each?</strong>
“GraphQL when many different clients need different shapes of data from
several sources, like a web and mobile app on a product page; it removes
over- and under-fetching and gives a strongly typed contract. REST when
resources are simple, caching at the CDN matters, or the API is public
and needs to be easy to consume. GraphQL brings costs: N+1 handling,
query cost limits, field-level auth and weaker HTTP caching, so I don’t
adopt it by default.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. What is the N+1 problem in GraphQL and how do you solve
it?</strong> “Resolvers run per field per item, so a list of 20 items
each loading a related record makes 21 queries. DataLoader batches all
keys requested in one tick into a single <code>IN</code> query and
caches per request. The loader must be created per request and return
results in key order.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. How do you secure a GraphQL API?</strong> “Authentication
at the gateway, authorization in the business layer so every path to a
field is checked, depth and cost limits, maximum page sizes, persisted
queries for our own clients, introspection off in production, and rate
limiting by query cost.”</p>
<p><strong>Q4. GraphQL returns 200 even when it fails. How do you
monitor it?</strong> “Instrument at the GraphQL layer: log and measure
per operation name, count <code>errors</code> by
<code>extensions.code</code>, and trace resolver timings with
OpenTelemetry. Expected business failures are modelled as typed union
results, so the errors array contains only real failures.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-13">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Add Apollo Server to the product
service with <code>products</code> (connection pagination) and
<code>Product.reviews</code> / <code>Review.author</code></label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Log DB query count for one request
before and after adding DataLoader</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Add a depth limit and a max
<code>first</code> of 50; prove a deep query is rejected</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-3-openapi-swagger-and-api-contracts">Hour 3 — OpenAPI /
Swagger and API contracts</h2>
<p>Most teams treat Swagger as auto-generated docs nobody reads. At lead
level the contract is a working tool: it’s reviewed before code is
written, generates clients and mocks, and CI blocks breaking changes.
That’s the story to tell.</p>
<h3 id="terms">3.1 Terms</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>OpenAPI Specification (OAS):</strong> the standard format
(YAML/JSON) describing a REST API: paths, parameters, request/response
schemas, auth, errors. Current major version 3.x (3.1 aligns schemas
with JSON Schema).</li>
<li><strong>Swagger:</strong> the original name, now the tooling brand:
Swagger UI (interactive docs), Swagger Editor, Swagger Codegen.</li>
<li>Other tools: Redoc (nicer docs), Stoplight / Spectral (linting),
Prism (mock server), openapi-typescript and Orval (TypeScript types and
clients).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="a-small-spec-the-parts-that-matter">3.2 A small spec, the parts
that matter</h3>

<span id="cb100-34"><a href="#cb100-34" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="at">        </span><span class="fu">total</span><span class="kw">:</span><span class="at"> </span><span class="kw">{</span><span class="at"> </span><span class="fu">$ref</span><span class="kw">:</span><span class="at"> </span><span class="st">&#39;#/components/schemas/Money&#39;</span><span class="at"> </span><span class="kw">}</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>Things reviewers look for: every operation has an
<code>operationId</code>, reusable <code>components</code> instead of
copy-paste, error responses documented (not just 200), examples, auth
declared, and descriptions written for the consumer.</p>
<h3 id="design-first-vs-code-first">3.3 Design-first vs code-first</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>Design-first (spec before code)</th>
<th>Code-first (spec generated from code)</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>How</td>
<td>Write and review YAML, then implement</td>
<td>Decorators or schemas in code produce the spec</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Good</td>
<td>Frontend, mobile and partners start in parallel against a mock; API
reviewed as a product</td>
<td>Spec can’t drift from the implementation; less duplication</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Risk</td>
<td>Implementation can drift from spec unless validated</td>
<td>API shape becomes an accident of the code; harder to review
early</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Tools</td>
<td>Spectral, Prism, openapi-backend, express-openapi-validator</td>
<td>NestJS <code>@nestjs/swagger</code>, <code>zod-to-openapi</code>,
tsoa, Fastify schemas</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>My approach:</strong> design-first for public and cross-team
APIs: write the spec, review it like code, mock it with Prism so the
frontend starts immediately, and validate requests and responses against
it in the service (so drift fails tests). Code-first is fine for
internal APIs owned by one team, as long as the generated spec is
committed and diffed in CI.</p>
<p><strong>Code-first with Zod (no duplication):</strong></p>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb101"><pre

<span id="cb101-8"><a href="#cb101-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb101-9"><a href="#cb101-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>registry<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">registerPath</span>({</span>
<span id="cb101-10"><a href="#cb101-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  method<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;get&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> path<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;/orders/{orderId}&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> operationId<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;getOrder&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb101-11"><a href="#cb101-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  request<span class="op">:</span> { params<span class="op">:</span> z<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">object</span>({ orderId<span class="op">:</span> z<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">string</span>()<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">uuid</span>() }) }<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb101-12"><a href="#cb101-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  responses<span class="op">:</span> { <span class="dv">200</span><span class="op">:</span> { description<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;The order&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> content<span class="op">:</span> { <span class="st">&#39;application/json&#39;</span><span class="op">:</span> { schema<span class="op">:</span> OrderSchema } } } }<span class="op">,</span></span>
<span id="cb101-13"><a href="#cb101-13" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>In NestJS, <code>@ApiProperty()</code> on DTOs plus
<code>SwaggerModule.setup('docs', app, document)</code> does the
same.</p>
<h3 id="generating-clients">3.4 Generating clients</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb102"><pre
class="sourceCode bash"><code class="sourceCode bash"><span id="cb102-1"><a href="#cb102-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="ex">npx</span> openapi-typescript ./openapi.yaml <span class="at">-o</span> packages/api-client/schema.d.ts</span></code></pre></div>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb103"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb103-1"><a href="#cb103-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">import</span> createClient <span class="im">from</span> <span class="st">&#39;openapi-fetch&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb103-2"><a href="#cb103-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">import</span> <span class="im">type</span> { paths } <span class="im">from</span> <span class="st">&#39;./schema&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb103-3"><a href="#cb103-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> api <span class="op">=</span> <span class="fu">createClient</span><span class="op">&lt;</span>paths<span class="op">&gt;</span>({ baseUrl<span class="op">:</span> <span class="st">&#39;/api/v1&#39;</span> })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb103-4"><a href="#cb103-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">const</span> { data<span class="op">,</span> error } <span class="op">=</span> <span class="cf">await</span> api<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">GET</span>(<span class="st">&#39;/orders/{orderId}&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> { params<span class="op">:</span> { path<span class="op">:</span> { orderId } } })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb103-5"><a href="#cb103-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="co">// data is typed as Order; a wrong path or param is a compile error</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>The React and Angular apps in Week 2 use generated clients, so a
backend change that breaks the contract breaks the frontend build, not
production.</p>
<h3 id="breaking-vs-non-breaking-changes">3.5 Breaking vs non-breaking
changes</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Non-breaking (safe in v1)</th>
<th>Breaking (needs a new version or a migration plan)</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Add an endpoint</td>
<td>Remove or rename an endpoint or field</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Add an optional request field</td>
<td>Make an optional request field required</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Add a response field</td>
<td>Change a field’s type or format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Add a new enum value in a request</td>
<td>Add an enum value to a <strong>response</strong> (clients with
exhaustive switches may break)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Relax validation</td>
<td>Tighten validation; change status codes or error format</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Prevent accidents in CI: diff the spec against <code>main</code> with
<strong>oasdiff</strong> (or openapi-diff) and fail the build on
breaking changes unless the PR is explicitly labelled. Clients should
also follow the <strong>tolerant reader</strong> principle: ignore
unknown fields.</p>
<h3 id="contract-testing">3.6 Contract testing</h3>
<p><strong>Problem:</strong> service A’s tests mock service B. Both test
suites pass, and production breaks because the mock doesn’t match B’s
real behaviour.</p>
<p><strong>Consumer-driven contract testing (Pact):</strong></p>
<ol type="1">
<li>The consumer’s tests record what it expects from the provider
(request + minimal response) into a contract file.</li>
<li>Contracts are published to a Pact Broker.</li>
<li>The provider’s CI replays each contract against the real provider
and fails if it can’t satisfy it.</li>
<li><code>can-i-deploy</code> checks before release that the versions
about to be deployed are compatible.</li>
</ol>
<p>Cheaper alternative when you’re design-first: validate the provider’s
real responses against the OpenAPI spec in its integration tests, and
generate consumer mocks from the same spec. Both sides are then tested
against one contract.</p>
<h3 id="how-id-answer-hour-3-4">How I’d answer — Hour 3</h3>
<p><strong>Q1. Design-first or code-first?</strong> “Design-first for
APIs other teams or partners consume: the spec is reviewed before code,
the frontend works against a Prism mock in parallel, and the service
validates against the spec so it can’t drift. Code-first for internal
single-team APIs, generating the spec from Zod or Nest decorators,
committing it and diffing it in CI.”</p>
<p><strong>Q2. How do you stop teams from shipping breaking API
changes?</strong> “The spec lives in the repo, and CI runs oasdiff
against main and fails on breaking changes. Consumers use generated
clients, so incompatibilities break their builds. For
service-to-service, consumer-driven contract tests with Pact and a
<code>can-i-deploy</code> gate. Real breaking changes go to a new
version with deprecation headers and a sunset date.”</p>
<p><strong>Q3. Is adding a field breaking?</strong> “Adding a response
field isn’t, if clients are tolerant readers. Adding a required request
field is. A subtle one: adding an enum value to a response can break
clients with exhaustive switches, so I document enums as extensible and
tell clients to handle unknown values.”</p>
<h3 id="practice-14">Practice</h3>
<ul class="task-list">
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Generate an OpenAPI spec for the
auth and product services (Nest Swagger or zod-to-openapi); serve
Swagger UI at <code>/docs</code></label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Generate a typed client into
<code>packages/api-client</code> with openapi-typescript</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" />Add an oasdiff step to CI that fails
on breaking changes; prove it by renaming a field</label></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hour-4-testing-strategy-git-ci">Hour 4 — Testing strategy, Git,
CI</h2>
<p>For a lead role, testing questions are about strategy and trade-offs:
what you test at which level, how you keep the suite fast and
trustworthy, and how you stop flaky tests from eroding the team’s
confidence. Git and CI questions are about how a team ships safely every
day.</p>
<h3 id="the-test-pyramid-and-its-honest-variants">4.1 The test pyramid
(and its honest variants)</h3>
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Level</th>
<th>Tests</th>
<th>Speed</th>
<th>Use for</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Unit</td>
<td>One function or class, dependencies faked</td>
<td>Milliseconds</td>
<td>Business rules, calculations, state transitions, edge cases</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Integration</td>
<td>Your service with real DB, Redis, broker (in containers), HTTP
in-process</td>
<td>Seconds</td>
<td>Repositories, queries, transactions, API endpoints, auth</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Contract</td>
<td>Agreement between services (Hour 3)</td>
<td>Seconds</td>
<td>Service-to-service compatibility</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>End-to-end</td>
<td>Full system through the UI or public API</td>
<td>Minutes</td>
<td>A handful of critical user journeys (signup, checkout)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>The classic pyramid says “mostly unit tests”. For typical Node APIs,
where most bugs live in queries, validation and wiring rather than
complex algorithms, many teams get more value from the <strong>testing
trophy</strong>: a solid layer of integration tests against real
dependencies, unit tests for real business logic, and few E2E tests.
<strong>My position:</strong> test business rules with unit tests, every
endpoint with integration tests against real databases in containers,
and only critical journeys end to end.</p>
<h3 id="unit-tests-with-fakes">4.2 Unit tests with fakes</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb104"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb104-1"><a href="#cb104-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">import</span> { describe<span class="op">,</span> it<span class="op">,</span> expect<span class="op">,</span> vi } <span class="im">from</span> <span class="st">&#39;vitest&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb104-2"><a href="#cb104-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb104-3"><a href="#cb104-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">describe</span>(<span class="st">&#39;OrderService.place&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb104-4"><a href="#cb104-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  <span class="fu">it</span>(<span class="st">&#39;rejects orders above the credit limit&#39;</span><span class="op">,</span> <span class="kw">async</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
<span id="cb104-5"><a href="#cb104-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> orders <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">InMemoryOrderRepository</span>()<span class="op">;</span>          <span class="co">// a fake, not a mock library</span></span>
<span id="cb104-6"><a href="#cb104-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> events <span class="op">=</span> { publish<span class="op">:</span> vi<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">fn</span>() }<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb104-7"><a href="#cb104-7" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="kw">const</span> svc <span class="op">=</span> <span class="kw">new</span> <span class="fu">OrderService</span>(orders<span class="op">,</span> <span class="fu">fakePayments</span>()<span class="op">,</span> events)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb104-8"><a href="#cb104-8" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb104-9"><a href="#cb104-9" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="cf">await</span> <span class="fu">expect</span>(svc<span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">place</span>(<span class="fu">orderWithTotal</span>(<span class="dv">1_000_001</span>)))<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">rejects</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">toThrow</span>(CreditLimitExceededError)<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb104-10"><a href="#cb104-10" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>    <span class="fu">expect</span>(events<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">publish</span>)<span class="op">.</span><span class="at">not</span><span class="op">.</span><span class="fu">toHaveBeenCalled</span>()<span class="op">;</span>         <span class="co">// no side effects on failure</span></span>
<span id="cb104-11"><a href="#cb104-11" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>  })<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb104-12"><a href="#cb104-12" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a>})<span class="op">;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p><strong>Fakes vs mocks:</strong> a fake is a working lightweight
implementation (in-memory repository); a mock asserts specific calls.
Prefer fakes and assertions on outcomes; heavy mocking ties tests to
implementation details, so every refactor breaks tests that were never
protecting behaviour.</p>
<h3 id="integration-tests-with-real-dependencies">4.3 Integration tests
with real dependencies</h3>
<div class="sourceCode" id="cb105"><pre
class="sourceCode ts"><code class="sourceCode typescript"><span id="cb105-1"><a href="#cb105-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">import</span> request <span class="im">from</span> <span class="st">&#39;supertest&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb105-2"><a href="#cb105-2" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="im">import</span> { PostgreSqlContainer } <span class="im">from</span> <span class="st">&#39;@testcontainers/postgresql&#39;</span><span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb105-3"><a href="#cb105-3" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb105-4"><a href="#cb105-4" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="kw">let</span> app<span class="op">:</span> Express<span class="op">;</span> <span class="kw">let</span> container<span class="op">:</span> StartedPostgreSqlContainer<span class="op">;</span></span>
<span id="cb105-5"><a href="#cb105-5" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a></span>
<span id="cb105-6"><a href="#cb105-6" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"></a><span class="fu">beforeAll</span>(<span class="kw">async</span> () <span class="kw">=&gt;</span> {</span>
